title: Coast Guard and FBI boarded tankers due to cyberattacks. How big is the risk?
summary: U.S. Coast Guard personnel and FBI agents boarded two Texas-bound energy tankers last month after cyberattacks struck the vessels while they were traveling toward the United States, according to U.S. officials.
story: U.S. Coast Guard personnel and FBI agents boarded two Texas-bound energy tankers last month after cyberattacks struck the vessels while they were traveling toward the United States, according to U.S. officials.

One of the vessels was the VL Prosperity, a 1,093-foot Liberian-flagged crude oil tanker headed to Galveston, Texas. Iranian state media identified the ship shortly after the incident and claimed hackers had gained access to its propulsion, navigation and cargo systems, knocking out communications for 30 hours.

The Coast Guard has not publicly pinned the attacks on Iran. But Rear Adm. Amy Grable, commander of U.S. Coast Guard Cyber Command, told CBS News in a network exclusive interview that investigators did find evidence of a malicious cyber actor.
"They started out by doing an assessment of the information technology and the other systems on board the vessel, and they did find malicious cyber activity," Grable said.
The U.S. is investigating whether the two cyberattacks are connected and whether Iran or another foreign adversary was behind the attacks.
What happened?
The VL Prosperity is what's known as a supertanker — more than three football fields long and capable of carrying roughly 2.3 million barrels of oil.

Public vessel data shows the ship departed Egypt's Sidi Kerir oil terminal on Aug. 1 headed for Galveston. U.S. officials say it slowed near the Strait of Gibraltar around the time of the cyberattack before continuing across the Atlantic and toward the U.S.

Iran's Mehr News Agency reported on Aug. 20 that the VL Prosperity had been attacked on Aug. 7 while transiting through the Strait of Gibraltar. Citing an unnamed crew member, Mehr alleged hackers breached the engine room, reducing engine cooling flow, increasing engine speed and interfering with fuel systems.

Rob Lee, CEO of Dragos, an industrial cybersecurity firm specializing in operational technology, said the Iranian report's details were technically plausible, but warned that authorities have not yet revealed who was behind the incident.
"The details that they published, from what we understand of these types of vehicles and ships and similar, is spot on," Lee said. "Everything they're saying is very realistic."
The next day, Aug. 21, Coast Guard cyber personnel, law enforcement officers, a vessel inspector and FBI Cyber Action Team operators boarded the ship for four days.

Grable said Coast Guard teams had been alerted by interagency partners and went offshore with the FBI to climb aboard — one of roughly 40 to 50 missions the Coast Guard's Cyber Protection Team has undergone in the past year.
She said investigators were hunting for malware and combing through information technology systems to root out malicious activity.

"The real thing we're concerned about is those IT systems being connected to other systems on the ship that control propulsion, navigation and other systems that are critical to the safety of that vessel," Grable added.

Typically, investigators collect data that is later analyzed, and Grable told CBS News that the Coast Guard plans to provide the vessel owner with recommendations for patching vulnerabilities. She stressed that response teams did not find any evidence indicating the ship had become unsafe to navigate when they boarded it.
How difficult is it to attack a ship?
The concern surrounding large cargo vessels and maritime critical infrastructure transcends stolen files or disrupted communications.

More and more, modern commercial vessels run on internet-connected systems, relying on them for navigation, propulsion, steering, ballast and additional critical machinery. A cyberattack that penetrates those operational systems could potentially be weaponized or manipulated.

"When these vessels are highly connected, they're susceptible to cyber threats," Grable said, warning that an attack could lead to "a vessel blocking a waterway or a pollution incident or any other number of safety and security hazards to our ports and waterways."
The danger that a large vessel could be compromised near an American port is something that authorities fear.

"Of course we're worried about a collision, an explosion, anything that blocks the channel for other vessels to safely enter and exit the port, pollution incidents — we're kind of worried about the whole gamut," Grable said.
The potential economic impact is also colossal. Grable said $5.4 trillion in commerce flows through U.S. ports annually — which could mean high economic stakes for even a relatively small disruption.

"Any small delay, because of a cyber breach, like, for example, if a port has to shift to manual operations, it causes a big delay with tankers and cargo vessels coming in and out of the port," she said.
Perhaps most concerning, Grable said the technical barrier may not be as high as the public assumes.
How sophisticated would an attacker have to be to move beyond breaking into a computer network to manipulating machinery aboard a modern tanker?
"Not necessarily that sophisticated," Grable told CBS News. "There is malicious source code that people can get their hands on."
Grable said that code is available right now, and added that "artificial intelligence is accelerating the rate at which we need to take action."
She urged operators to zero in on network segmentation, phishing attacks and basic cyber hygiene. "Just taking basic precautions would prevent most of these occurrences."
Just one firewall away
On many ships, the barrier between a satellite internet connection and critical onboard systems can be as fragile as a single firewall.
Behind that firewall, Lee said, can be a shared network containing "navigation, propulsion, ballast, steering, ship command — everything on one shared network."

Lee explained that artificial intelligence could make that problem worse because it can assist attackers in picking out weakly protected systems, speeding up attempts to breach internet-facing systems on energy carriers.
"The very thing that we think is our one protection — not that you should have one protection — is the very thing that AI is actually really good at," Lee said.

Still, experts concede that while older vessels may not have the same digitally connected control systems, even on modern ships, reaching critical machinery still requires some knowledge of the onboard environment.
Is "remote hijacking" a real threat?
Asked whether cyber access to a ship could amount to a form of remote hijacking, Grable called it a fair description of the broader risk.
"That's a good way to characterize it, and yes, it is a concern," she said.
Lee agreed that the scenario is realistic if an attacker gains a foothold.
"I do think there's a realistic concern," Lee said, describing the possibility of remotely messing with a maritime asset, even running it aground.
But former Coast Guard cyber official Quinton DuBose seemed skeptical of the notion that hackers could simply take over an entire supertanker like a remote-controlled vehicle.
"I'd be kind of cautious about saying that somebody can just take control of the ship," DuBose said. "Ships are incredibly complicated systems."
The more realistic threat, he said, may be an attacker disrupting one or more critical subsystems enough to make the vessel unsafe.

"Rather than looking at it as, 'okay, I'm going to take full control of this thing,' it's, 'what systems can I disrupt to the point where it affects the safe handling and makes the ship less safe to operate,'" DuBose said.
Iranian state media claims under scrutiny

The U.S. has not publicly stated who is behind either cyberattack. But Iranian state media began pushing out content around the VL Prosperity incident before U.S. authorities even publicly acknowledged the boarding.
Four days after Mehr's initial report, Iran's Tasnim News Agency published an article with the headline, "No American Vessel Is Safe Anymore: Will Cannons Give Way to Codes?"
DuBose stressed that the Iranian narrative remains unverified, cautioning that Iranian-linked actors are often quick to oversell their cyber influence.
Attribution in cyberspace can take weeks or months, DuBose added.
According to Grable, investigators typically compare the attacker's tactics, techniques and procedures — effectively their digital fingerprints — against known threat actors.

"We look at things called TTPs, which are tactics, techniques and protocols that certain adversaries use — kind of like their trademark fingerprints on how they gain access to systems and what they do and what their payloads are," she said.
A warning to the maritime industry

For Coast Guard Cyber Command, the growing concern is that increasingly connected vessels create more porous entry points for attackers, as ships adopt satellite communications and connect IT networks with their onboard control systems.
"Because they're facing the internet, that is a vector for attackers to gain access and deploy malicious activity on the vessels," she said.
DuBose said the industry should take the threat seriously, while resisting the notion that all vessels are suddenly vulnerable to remote takeover.
He added that maritime infrastructure is so critical that the federal government "has increasingly imposed baseline cyber requirements across the sector."
Grable's warning to vessel owners and operators was blunt: "We need everybody to pay attention to this."

title: ‘Charlie’s Angels’ star Jaclyn Smith lived apart from her husband for 17 years during their 35-year love story
summary: Jaclyn Smith's memoir details her four marriages, a chance encounter with Warren Beatty, and the long-distance love that lasted 35 years.
story: Jaclyn Smith tells Fox News Digital the one powerful force behind her ageless appearance at the Paley Honors Spring Gala in New York.
For Jaclyn Smith, love wasn't waiting in Hollywood — it walked into her father's hospital room.

The actress, who starred as Kelly Garrett on the TV series "Charlie's Angels" from 1976 to 1981, recently penned a memoir, "I Once Knew a Guy Named Charlie." In it, the 80-year-old revealed that she and her fourth husband, Dr. Brad Allen, lived apart for 17 of their 35 years together.

Smith first met Allen, 72, when he helped perform her father's heart surgery in 1991. About two years later, Allen took a job at the University of Illinois in Chicago. He spent the next 17 years there while Smith continued living in Los Angeles.
‘CHARLIE’S ANGELS’ STAR JACLYN SMITH SAYS BEAUTY SECRET ISN’T MAKEUP OR DIET AFTER FANS PRAISE YOUTHFUL GLOW
Dr. Brad Allen and Jaclyn Smith attend the Farrah Fawcett Foundation Tex-Mex Fiesta Benefit on Oct. 20, 2022, in Dallas, Texas. (Getty Images for Farrah Fawcett Foundation)

"It's true, the greatest love comes when you're least looking for it," Smith told Fox News Digital. "He operated on my dad. I remember he walked into the room, and he looked like the guys I grew up with, clean cut and just collegiate. He looked like just the guy down the street. And he was so good to my parents."
After three divorces, Smith said motherhood changed everything. While a romance quickly blossomed, she wasn't willing to gamble on love again. This time, she wouldn't rush walking down the aisle.
"Brad and I finally said 'I do!' in Los Angeles on Oct. 11, 1997," Jaclyn Smith wrote in her memoir. (Courtesy of Jaclyn Smith)

"You see, when I met Brad, I had two children," she explained. "It was no longer me going, 'OK, my heart's beating out of my chest, and I'm going to get married right away.' It had to be a three-way decision."
WATCH: CHARLIES ANGELS STAR JACLYN SMITH, 80, REVEALS SECRET TO HER AGELESS LOOK

"Ultimately, we commuted for 17 years," she continued. "We married after seven years. And when we got married, we really knew one another. We knew each other's families. We knew our priorities. We knew what we expected in life. And that is important in any relationship."
Jaclyn Smith is seen here with her family today. (Courtesy of Jaclyn Smith)

Smith and Allen married in 1997. Smith's daughter, then 11 years old, was the maid of honor, People magazine reported. According to the outlet, her son, then 15, gave her away. The outlet reported that Allen closed the distance for good in 2009.
For Smith, the true test of marriage isn't only falling in love — it's building a life together.

Jaclyn Smith says love and family are behind her youthful glow at 80, as she reunited with Kate Jackson for the 50th anniversary of "Charlie's Angels" earlier this year. (Tina Thorpe / Disney; Harry Langdon / Getty Images)

"We see life the same rather than your heart just beating out," she said. "Yes, it beats out of your chest at first, but then you have to get down to the nitty-gritty of what makes the world go round, that day-to-day living."
Allen supported Smith through her 2002 breast cancer diagnosis. The star is now cancer-free after undergoing a lumpectomy and radiation.
Jaclyn Smith attends the Farrah Fawcett Foundation 2025 Tex-Mex Fiesta at The Rustic on Oct. 30, 2025 in Dallas, Texas. (Omar Vega/Getty Images for Farrah Fawcett Foundation)
Smith first married Roger Davis, then a star of "Dark Shadows," in 1968. He proposed to Smith after two dates.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Jaclyn Smith attends "Jaclyn Smith in Conversation: Beyond Charlie's Angels" at 92NY in New York City on Sept. 9, 2026. (Getty Images)

Two years into their relationship, Smith wrote that she was walking with a friend in New York City to look at an apartment she and Davis were considering renting when she ran into Warren Beatty. The actor asked her to interview for a role in a film he was working on. But moments later, Davis appeared and told Beatty that Smith only did commercials.

Smith wrote she later learned that while she was talking to Beatty, Davis was upstairs having sex with their real estate agent in the apartment. Smith split from Davis after finding him with another woman on their fourth wedding anniversary.
"I Once Knew a Guy Named Charlie: A Memoir" by Jaclyn Smith is available now. (Gallery Books)

"I knew my marriage wasn't everything I dreamed," Smith said. "I knew there were problems from day one. I think I have a line in the book about love masquerading as foundation, attraction as permanence. And I came from a background of you didn't live with people. It was the '50s. I didn't want to disappoint my parents. And I really believed in that picket fence. Why wouldn't this be great?"
Jaclyn Smith was a successful model before "Charlie's Angels" came calling. (2008 American Broadcasting Companies, Inc.)

"To fall in love, get married and go the distance — I think that's a wonderful thing," she continued. "There is a bond when that truly happens. I've seen my brother, who fell in love at age 19 or 20, get married. They went on to have three children and were together until my brother passed away. So I do think that's pretty wonderful when that happens. It just didn't for me. And a lot of it was my innocence. I was a romantic. I didn't look beneath the paper. It just looked good on paper. It looked perfect."
Smith said that while they were both actors, her values and Davis' values were vastly different.
Jaclyn Smith is seen here with her two children, circa 1988. (Courtesy of Jaclyn Smith)

"You tend to overlook that big statement, 'love is blind,'" Smith said. "But attraction is blind. Love comes from all your lessons. And listen, today is different. Nothing is left to the imagination on these dating sites. I'm glad I didn't start out at that point. I think values are so important, to share the same values. People tend to overlook that initially and think it's a sure shot."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Jaclyn Smith attends the 2026 Paley Honors Spring Gala at The Plaza Hotel in New York City on May 14, 2026. (Theo Wargo/Getty Images)
When asked if she regretted not taking a chance to work with Beatty, Smith replied, "Things happen for a reason."

"I never had a definite plan for my career," she explained. "I was never overly driving or ambitious. I just wanted to take what came my way at the time. That was shocking to me when Warren Beatty remembered my name and I didn't know too much about Warren Beatty except I loved his movie 'Bonnie and Clyde.'"
Faye Dunaway and Warren Beatty are seen here as Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow in the 1967 film "Bonnie and Clyde," directed by Arthur Penn. (Getty Images)

"I think whether I did the James Bond movie or the Warren Beatty movie, I think what happened in my life. Everything's unpredictable," Smith said. "And I like the path I took. I really do. Sometimes, it's all about chance. 'Charlie's Angels' was a chance.' Without that, I might have been living in Houston teaching ballet. When it came to my career, I took it day by day. I didn't have huge plans."
Jaclyn Smith, Farrah Fawcett and Kate Jackson are seen here on the set of "Charlie's Angels." (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
Smith married actor Dennis Cole in 1978 after about a year and a half of dating. They divorced in 1981.

"One day, I found a note in his pocket," Smith wrote. "The writer turned out to be a girl I knew. She was his son's girlfriend. I would not repeat the mistake I'd made with Roger. This time, I wasn't going to overlook what I learned, and I was not going to stick around and try to work it out. I didn't rationalize Dennis' actions, and I didn't blame myself. My one and only thought was to get out."
Actress Jaclyn Smith and her husband, actor Dennis Cole, are seen here on Feb. 22, 1980, at the Beverly Hills Hotel in Beverly Hills, California. (Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)

In 1980, Smith met British cinematographer Anthony B. "Tony" Richmond while filming "Nightkill." They married in 1981. They welcomed a son, Gaston Anthony, in 1982, and a daughter, Spencer Margaret, in 1985. Smith wrote the marriage was strained by Richmond's struggles with alcohol and drugs.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Anthony B. Richmond and Jaclyn Smith attend an event at the White House in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 4, 1983. (Penske Media via Getty Images)

"I'd had enough," Smith wrote. ". . . I was done. I couldn't stay with a man who chose drugs and alcohol over his family. . . . We had a wonderful life when he was sober. . . . [But] I needed to do the best I could for my children, to protect them from the ravages I knew could come from substance abuse."
Fox News Digital reached out to Davis and Richmond for comment. Cole died in 2009 at age 69.
Jaclyn Smith's granddaughters: Bea, Olivia and Wren. "The joys of my life." (Courtesy of Jaclyn Smith)

"You know, in writing this book, I learned that I'm really strong," Smith said. "I had a great beginning. I had the best parents in the world, but I had marriages that didn't make it. Your heart gets broken here and there. You have successes along the way. And I worked hard to be there for my children more than anything. It's ferocious."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Jaclyn Smith arrives for the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards at the Peacock Theatre at LA Live in Los Angeles on Sept. 14, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

"You have to give up control when you don't want to because you don't want anything to hurt them. I think of my journey, it's been unpredictable. I come away thinking, 'What would my parents think?' But I'm a girl who stuck to things, worked very hard and just gave it all to my family."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Sylvester Stallone reveals what he said to Trump after surprise Hollywood ambassador appointment
summary: Sylvester Stallone says he learned about Trump's Hollywood ambassador appointment while watching TV and later told the president it was impossible.
story: Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo brings ‘The Ingraham Angle’ to the red carpet at the Kennedy Center Honors and interviews stars in music and Hollywood.
Sylvester Stallone revealed that he was blindsided when President Donald Trump announced his appointment as a special ambassador to Hollywood.

Days before his second inauguration in January 2025, Trump shared a post on his platform Truth Social in which he named Stallone, Mel Gibson and Jon Voight as "Special Envoys," describing the role as a way for the three actors to serve as his "eyes and ears" in Hollywood and advise him on efforts to bring film and television production back to the U.S.
During a recent interview with The Sunday Times, the 80-year-old "Rocky" star recalled that he found out about the appointment while watching television.
SYLVESTER STALLONE'S 'TULSA KING' SEASON 4 TEASER SPARKS FAN FRENZY: 'THE KING IS BACK!'

"I was watching TV one night, and they go, ‘So Stallone and Mel Gibson and Jon Voight will be …’ And I went, ‘What?’ I said, ‘Excuse me? Really?’ Because if they had asked me in the beginning, I would have said, ‘This is not possible,'" Stallone said.

Sylvester Stallone revealed that he was blindsided when President Donald Trump announced him as a "special Hollywood ambassador." (Weiss Eubanks/NBCUniversal via Getty Images; Artur Widak/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Stallone told the outlet that he was hesitant about taking on the role because he didn't believe it was feasible. When asked if he had reservations after Trump's announcement, Stallone said, "Yes. Yes, because Hollywood, I guess it’s like feudal states."
'AMERICAN IDOL' DITCHES HOLLYWOOD FOR GEORGIA AFTER TWO DECADES AS CALIFORNIA LOSES ANOTHER PRODUCTION
"They have their little kingdoms," he continued. "You don’t go in and tell six studios how to do things. And Mel Gibson and Jon Voight, we’re kind of do-our-own-thing people. No, it won’t work."
The "Tulsa King" star recalled that he later explained his reasoning to Trump.
"I said thank you and ciao, because it’s impossible," Stallone said. "Hollywood works, and it will evolve."
"It’s corporate, and corporate people won’t want to hear me tell them about finance," he added.
Stallone said he told Trump that the role was "not possible." (Joe Raedle)
'I PLAY ROCKY' REVIVES THE GAMBLE THAT MADE SYLVESTER STALLONE A SUPERSTAR

In his original post on Jan. 16, 2025, Trump wrote, "It is my honor to announce Jon Voight, Mel Gibson, and Sylvester Stallone, to be Special Ambassadors to a great but very troubled place, Hollywood, California."

"They will serve as Special Envoys to me for the purpose of bringing Hollywood, which has lost much business over the last four years to Foreign Countries, BACK—BIGGER, BETTER, AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!" he continued. "These three very talented people will be my eyes and ears, and I will get done what they suggest. It will again be, like The United States of America itself, The Golden Age of Hollywood!"
DWAYNE 'THE ROCK' JOHNSON REJECTS HOLLYWOOD’S POLITICAL OBSESSION, BLASTS CELEBRITY ATTACK CULTURE
At the time, Gibson, 70, shared that he was caught off-guard by Trump's announcement and did not have previous knowledge about his presidential appointment.
Gibson said he was "surprised" by Trump's announcement.  (Mike Marsland/Mike Marsland/WireImage via Getty Images)

"I got the tweet at the same time as all of you and was just as surprised," he told Variety in January 2025. "Nevertheless, I heed the call. My duty as a citizen is to give any help and insight I can."
"Any chance the position comes with an Ambassador’s residence?" Gibson joked.

Though Stallone may not have been onboard with his role as a special Hollywood ambassador, the action star appears to have a friendly relationship with Trump and heaped praise on the president during a speech following his victory in the November 2024 election.
Days after the election, Stallone introduced Trump at the America First Policy Institute Gala held at the president-elect's Mar-A-Lago Club in Palm Beach, Florida.

"We’re in the presence of a really mythical character," Stallone said of Trump. "I love mythology. And this individual does not exist on this planet. Nobody in the world could have pulled off what he pulled off, so I’m in awe."

"When George Washington defended his country, he had no idea that he was gonna change the world," he added. "Because without him, you could imagine what the world would look like. Guess what? We got the second George Washington."
Stallone was later selected as a 2025 Kennedy Center honoree, with Trump personally naming him among that year’s recipients alongside George Strait, KISS, Gloria Gaynor and Michael Crawford.
Trump named Stallone as a 2025 Kennedy Center honoree. (Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images)

The actor has backed Republicans, including John McCain and Trump, but his political history has not been strictly partisan. Over the years, Stallone has made financial contributions to both political parties, donating to various Democratic candidates and committees, including former President Joe Biden and the Democratic National Committee, as well as Republican campaigns.

Meanwhile, Voight, who is a staunch supporter of Trump, appears to have embraced his role as a special ambassador. He has met with the White House and advocated for policies aimed at bringing film and TV production back to the U.S., especially a federal film tax incentive. Voight has been working with his manager Steven Paul and Paul’s associate Scott Karol as part of his push.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

After meeting with the trio at the end of last month, Trump threw his support behind a federal film and television production incentive, urging Congress to pass bipartisan legislation to "save" the American entertainment business.

In a Truth Social post on Aug. 31, Trump wrote that "Hollywood is a Complete and Total Disaster" and said there was "no incentive" for productions to stay there. He said meetings were being set up with leaders of both parties and urged Republicans and Democrats to "immediately craft Legislation to save the Movie, Television, and Entertainment Business in America."
Trump has a longtime friend in Voight, who he also appointed as a special ambassador to Hollywood.  (Mandel Ngan)
Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (D-CA) later issued statements in which they voiced their support for Trump's proposal.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
While speaking with the Hollywood Reporter earlier this month, Voight was asked whether Stallone and Gibson were involved with his efforts.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
They’ve been very busy, both of those guys actually have been extremely busy," Voight said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
However, Paul, who joined Voight for the interview, said, "Sly’s been doing his TV show, but Sly’s been very involved and he signed our letter."
Ashley Hume is an entertainment journalist for Fox News Digital and Fox Business who covers breaking news, celebrity culture, major industry events and the business of entertainment.

title: Paris Hilton heartbroken over Presley Gerber’s death at 27 as she remembers his ‘gentle heart’

Paris Hilton was among those mourning Gerber’s death, remembering him as a "beautiful soul" who "will be so deeply missed."
PRESLEY GERBER, SON OF CINDY CRAWFORD AND RANDE GERBER, DEAD AT 27

Celebrities paid tribute after 27-year-old model Presley Gerber, the son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber, died Sunday at a rehabilitation facility. (LEONARDO MUNOZ/AFP, Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images North America)

Paris Hilton pays tribute to Presley Gerber on Instagram. (Instagram: Paris Hilton)

title: Princess Diana's brother Charles Spencer says King Charles 'gaslit' him over memoir claims
summary: Charles Spencer says he was "gaslit" by King Charles III after Buckingham Palace questioned his memory of a shocking post-Diana conversation.
story: King Charles confirms Prince Harry and Meghan Markle will not return to royal duties. A letter sent on behalf of the King explains their styles as His and Her Royal Highness remain in abeyance, and they are now akin to private citizens.

Princess Diana's brother, Earl Charles Spencer, fired back at Buckingham Palace after the royal household questioned his recollection of a conversation with King Charles III, saying he was being "gaslit" by the monarch.

Earlier this week, The Daily Mail published an excerpt of Spencer's upcoming memoir, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister," in which the king's former brother-in-law described having a heated conversation with Charles after Diana's death. In the excerpt, Spencer alleged that Charles said, "We’ll forget her soon enough!," regarding his ex-wife during their exchange.

Buckingham Palace later responded to Spencer's claims, disputing the earl's account of the conversation and suggesting that grief may have affected his memory of events surrounding his sister's death.
KING CHARLES DRAWS ‘LINE IN THE SAND’ WITH PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE AFTER COUPLE CAUGHT OFF GUARD: EXPERT
During an interview with The Mail on Sunday, Spencer took issue with the palace's response.

"It is not every day you wake up to find you've been gaslit by the king," he said. "It was astonishingly provocative and below the belt because it was essentially trying to say I'd lied without the King being able to deny what I'd said."
Charles Spencer says King Charles III "gaslit" him in response to his claims about an alleged conversation they had after Princess Diana's death. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images)
"I also thought it was a rather poor imitation of the ‘recollections may vary’ quote, which was a much more elegant way of putting things, but in these circumstances entirely out of place," he added.
The remark referenced the palace's famous "recollections may vary" statement issued after Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's explosive 2021 interview with Oprah Winfrey.
In the excerpt, published Wednesday, Spencer described a phone call he said he had with Charles six days after Diana died in August 1997.

"Prince Charles continued his stream of anger, without me interrupting. Then he stopped. I assumed the pause signaled an effort to bring himself under control, but then he unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death," Spencer alleged. "‘Rest assured,’ he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough!’"
PRINCESS DIANA'S HONEYMOON LETTER REVEALS A YOUNG BRIDE 'PLAYING WITH GROWN-UPS' IN THE ROYAL FAMILY
Diana died in August 1997 following a car crash in Paris. (Getty Images)

According to the excerpt, the king and the 9th Earl of Spencer disagreed over the decision to have Prince William and Harry, then 15 and 12, walk behind their mother's casket during the funeral procession.
KING CHARLES CONSIDERED QUEEN CAMILLA 'NON-NEGOTIABLE' AFTER PRINCESS DIANA, AUTHOR CLAIMS
A Buckingham Palace spokesperson issued a rare statement responding to Spencer's claims.

"While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," the statement said, according to People.
Spencer stood by his account of the alleged conversation during an appearance on BBC One's "Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg."
When Kuenssberg pointed out that Buckingham Palace had denied his version of events, Spencer pushed back, saying, "But they haven't actually, Laura. They've sort of smudged that one, haven't they?"
Kuenssberg then read the palace's statement to Spencer, telling him that "the king is plainly furious."
"Well, is he furious? Is he furious or is he embarrassed?" Spencer asked. "Because I can tell you here and now, those are exactly the words he said."
Spencer alleged that Charles said, "We'll forget her soon enough." (Getty Images)
Spencer said he remembered the conversation clearly because he had spoken so infrequently with Charles, who was then Prince of Wales.
"I've only ever had two calls on the line with Prince Charles at any stage of my life," Spencer said. "I was hyper alert to what he was saying and those are precisely the words that he said."
Spencer said he repeated the alleged comment to close friends and family members immediately afterward "because it was so monstrous."

"Which, Charles, are the public meant to believe?" Kuenssberg asked. "Are they to believe you or are they to believe the king, the head of state of this country who's giving the impression very forcefully that this didn't happen? Who are we to believe?"
"Well, I'm telling the truth," Spencer replied.
"So, the king is giving an impression to the country that's not true. Misleading people, even lying?" Kuenssberg asked.

"I can hardly be responsible for what Buckingham Palace says," Spencer replied. "All I can tell you is what was said and what I heard and what shocked me. What else would have made me hang up on the king that day? It was something as outrageous as that slur against Diana."
When asked whether William and Harry would be upset by his account of the alleged phone call with their father, Spencer suggested his nephews were already familiar with his version of events.

"Well, I don't like to talk about what I've been speaking about to William and Harry, but this will not be a surprise to them," he said. "I will tell you that these words will not be a surprise to them."
A Buckingham Palace spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "We won’t be offering any comment."

Spencer said his dispute with Charles was due to the monarch's decision to have William and Harry walk behind their mother's coffin in the funeral procession. ((Photo by Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images))
Diana died at age 36 after suffering injuries sustained in a car accident in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris, France. Her partner, Dodi Fayed, and the driver, Henri Paul, also died in the crash.

At the time of her death, she and Charles had been divorced for about one year. The two married in July 1981, announced their separation in December 1992 and finalized their divorce in August 1996.

Harry wrote about the decision to have him and his brother walk behind their mother's coffin in his 2023 memoir, "Spare," saying that "several adults were aghast" and that "mummy’s brother, Uncle Charles, raised hell," and that he told the royal family, "You can’t make these boys walk behind their mother’s coffin! It’s barbaric."

title: Prince William refuses to repeat King Charles’ jealousy as Kate Middleton captivates royal crowds: experts

title: Chad Gilbert, New Found Glory founding member and lead guitarist, dead at 45
summary: Chad Gilbert, founding member and lead guitarist for New Found Glory, has died at the age of 45. He had battled adrenal cancer since 2021.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Chad Gilbert, the founding member and lead guitarist for the punk rock band New Found Glory, has died. He was 45.

The band and the late musician's wife Lisa Cimorelli announced the news of Gilbert's death in a joint Instagram post Saturday. The post did not cite a cause of death, but Gilbert had battled adrenal cancer since 2021, and in February, underwent brain surgery after doctors found tumors.

"On the morning of September 20th, Chad Everett Gilbert passed away peacefully in his sleep," they wrote. "He left this world surrounded by friends and family and took his final breaths with his wife and mother by his side, just as he wished."
Chad Gilbert of New Found Glory has died at the age of 54.  (FilmMagic)
DUNCAN SHEIK, ‘BARELY BREATHING’ SINGER, DEAD AT 56

"We are devastated and shocked by how quickly he left us, yet so grateful for how peacefully and smoothly he went," they continued. "The amount of visitors that crowded the hospital lobby at a moment’s notice is a testament to how beloved and cherished Chad was, and always will be. He was a legendary musician, but his favorite accomplishment was being a husband and father. His biggest dreams came true. He is survived by his wife, Lisa, his daughter, Lily, his mother, Jackie, and his brother, Brian."

In their statement, New Found Glory, whose members include lead singer Jordan Pundik, bassist Ian Grushka and drummer Cyrus Bolooki, paid tribute to Gilbert’s lasting influence on the band and the deep personal bond that they shared.

"Chad’s guitar playing, songwriting, humor, and relentless drive helped shape New Found Glory for nearly three decades," they wrote. "Through more than a dozen albums, endless tours around the world, and more accolades than we ever could have imagined, Chad challenged all of us to grow as musicians, performers, and human beings."

"While we are devastated to lose him, we are so grateful for the incredible life he lived, the memories we shared, and the brotherhood we had. His influence will always be part of New Found Glory and his spirit will be felt on every stage we stand on, with every note we play."
The band's guitarist and founding member had battled adrenal cancer since 2021.  (Future Publishing via Getty Images)
'YOU'RE SO VAIN' SINGER CARLY SIMON SAYS PARKINSON'S AND CANCER DIAGNOSES KEPT HER FROM PUBLIC EYE
"Rest in peace, Chad. We love you forever," they concluded.
Fox News Digital has reached out to New Found Glory's management company Le Grand Music and label Pure Noise Records for comment.

Gilbert had been open about his battle with stage 4 adrenal cancer that was first diagnosed in 2021 and later spread to his spine, lungs and brain. He was initially diagnosed with metastatic pheochromocytoma, a rare adrenal gland cancer, in which the tumor grows inside the inner part of the adrenal gland.

In a February interview with People magazine, he shared that he began experiencing weakness on the left side of his body and difficulty walking while New Found Glory was promoting its latest album "Listen Up!"

After collapsing at home, Gilbert underwent a scan and doctors discovered he had three brain tumors, one of which required emergency surgery. Gilbert later underwent radiation and immunotherapy to treat the two remaining tumors.
After the operation, he told People magazine his diagnosis changed to adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC), which starts growing in the outer layer of the adrenal gland.
Gilbert helped form the Florida punk rock band in 1997.  (Redferns)
JOAN JETT CANCELS REMAINING 2026 CONCERTS AFTER UNDERGOING SURGERY FOR 'FRACTURED VERTEBRAE'
In a March Instagram post, Gilbert wrote that his "recovery has been bumpy at times," but that he was "feeling much better now and getting stronger by the day."

Gilbert returned to the stage in June, performing with New Found Glory during their tour stop in Nashville, Tennessee. He joined the band onstage to perform a few songs while using a mobility scooter.

"I got to play a show in front of my daughter, something I truly never thought I’d get to do again," he wrote in an Instagram post following the show. "And my beautiful wife and all the nurses and doctors, my amazing team that have kept me alive through my battle. It was very emotional getting up on stage with my band again to play. So many feelings all at once."

Gilbert shared daughter Lily, 5, with Cimorelli, whom he wed in 2020. The guitarist was previously married to Eisley singer Sherri DuPree. The two tied the knot in 2007 but split later that year. Gilbert was also married to Paramore lead singer Hayley Williams from 2016 to 2017.
New Found Glory made their breakthrough with their 2002 album "Sticks and Stones." (WireImage)

Born March 9, 1981 in Coral Springs, Florida, Gilbert helped form New Found Glory in 1997. The band broke through with its 2002 album, "Sticks and Stones," which featured the hit singles "My Friends Over You" and "Head On Collision" and reached No. 4 on the Billboard 200 chart.
New Found Glory followed up with 2004's "Catalyst," which peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, and produced the singles "All Downhill from Here" and "Failure’s Not Flattering."

New Found Glory became one of the defining bands of the early-2000s pop-punk era. The band has released 12 studio albums and toured extensively around the world. Gilbert appeared on all of New Found Glory’s albums, including "Listen Up!," which came out in February.
In June, Gilbert returned to the stage for an emotional performance with New Found Glory in Nashville.  (Getty Images)

Outside New Found Glory, Gilbert was also known for his work in hardcore, including as a vocalist for Shai Hulud and with New Found Glory’s side project International Superheroes of Hardcore. Gilbert also worked as a producer for artists including A Day to Remember, H2O and State Champs, and collaborated with Fall Out Boy.

In addition to his wife and daughter, Gilbert is survived by his mother, Jackie and his brother, Brian.

title: Jack Osbourne admits raising kids without a nanny isn’t as gnarly as he expected

story: Halloween Horror Nights 2026 at Universal Studios Hollywood is officially underway and Jack Osbourne spoke to Fox News Digital about his father outside the Ozzy Osbourne: Prince of Darkness maze.
Jack Osbourne is opening up about the realities of raising five children, revealing that he and his wife, Aree Osbourne, have chosen to parent without a nanny.

"Yeah. So we don’t do the nanny thing," Osbourne told People magazine during an Emmy nominees event in Los Angeles over the weekend. "I thought it was going to be way gnarlier than it is, but you find a rhythm."

Aree, who is a stay-at-home mom, and Jack share daughters Maple, 4, and Ozzy Matilda, 6 months. Jack is also the father of Pearl, 14, Andy, 11, and Minnie, 8, whom he shares with his ex-wife, Lisa Stelly.

"I’m a little more structured with my kids than my parents were with me," Jack previously told People magazine. "I won’t take them out of school just to go travel. We do a little bit, but I think structure is healthy."

Frankie Muniz revealed he recently hit "rock bottom," describing the past six weeks as an emotional "nightmare."

title: Dakota Johnson hopes to start a family after career kept her 'gone for 20 years'
summary: Dakota Johnson reveals she feels "a soul that wants to come through" as she opens up about hoping for motherhood before her "Verity" premiere.
story: Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.
Dakota Johnson thought her life would look a lot different than it does now.
During a recent interview with Vogue, the 36-year-old actress spoke about her career and whether she sees herself starting a family, telling the outlet it's something she really wants for herself.

"I really do. I do, but for whatever reason, that’s the plan of the universe," she said. "So I would love that. I hope that that happens for me. I’ve always felt, especially the last few years, that there is a soul that wants to come through. And I hope that I’m lucky enough to be able to do that."

She went on to say that it can sometimes be hard to be around her friends and co-stars who have children or are starting their families when "things turned out differently than I thought," but says she is still "hopeful for that."
Johnson shared she hopes to have children in the future. (Taylor Hill/WireImage)

Johnson made a name for herself throughout the 2010s, starring in films such as "The Social Network" and "21 Jump Street," before landing the role of Anastasia Steele in "Fifty Shades of Grey," which became her breakout role.
She continued building her resume, starring in films such as "Peanut Butter Falcon," "Madame Web" and "The Materialists," but it looks like she plans on slowing down soon.

"I’ve worked back-to-back for so long that now I have this deep calling to shift my perspective a bit and maybe have a bit more of a real life," she said. "I’ve been gone for, like, 20 years. The people in my life are so used to me leaving for months at a time."
Her main goal is to live her life authentically, noting, "I want to unfold and unfold and really lovingly embrace this life."

title: Christine Taylor’s ‘Hey Dude’ salary was far lower than castmates remembered
summary: Christine Taylor says her "Hey Dude" salary was just $3,500 per episode, far less than her castmates remembered earning on the Nickelodeon series.
story: The "Ned’s Declassified" alum explains why her tiny residual checks went viral and questions whether Hollywood needs a better system for penny payments. The former child star-turned lawyer is now the host of "Off My Meds."
Christine Taylor is looking back at her early Hollywood career — and revealing that her "Hey Dude" salary was far lower than her castmates remembered.

During an appearance on "The Secret World of Alex Mack" actress Natanya Ross’ "We’re Still Here, Babe" podcast Wednesday, Taylor — who played Melody Hanson on Nickelodeon’s Western comedy series from 1989 to 1991 — said she earned approximately $3,500 per episode by the show’s final season.
"By the time ‘Hey Dude’ ended, we had this discussion among our castmates, and everyone seemed to think [that] by the last season, we were making $5,000 an episode," Taylor said.
Christine Taylor opened up about her "Hey Dude" salary. (WireImage/Getty Images)
"No, we were making $3,500 an episode, I’m pretty sure, because they would bump us up $500 every season," she added.
Taylor said all of the cast members earned the same amount, despite her co-stars’ shared belief that they were making $5,000 per episode.
"Everyone in their brain was like, ‘$5,000.’ I was like, ‘No way, no way. That would have… no, it did not happen,’" she recalled.

The actress said she was careful with the money she earned while working on the popular children’s series. She also credited her family with helping her financially as she moved to Los Angeles and pursued acting.
JENNIE GARTH ADMITS ‘SCARY’ FINANCIAL SPIRAL AFTER ‘90210’ FAME
Taylor starred in "Hey Dude" in the late '80s. (Nickelodeon)
Taylor remembered budgeting closely, using laundromats and monitoring her spending during the early stages of her career.
The actress went on to appear in "Saved by the Bell," "Blossom" and "Robin Hood: Men in Tights" before landing her breakout role as Marcia Brady in "The Brady Bunch Movie."
‘BRADY BUNCH’ STAR SHARES THE SIMPLE WORD THAT SAVED HER FROM HOLLYWOOD TRAPS
Taylor also revealed that she was asked to lose 10 pounds before playing the iconic character in the 1995 film.
"Of course, I was embarrassed when that ask came my way," she said, adding that the request reflected the attitudes of the 1990s and "would never happen today."
FORMER DISNEY STAR DYLAN SPROUSE SAYS ACTING AS A KID WAS ‘CHILD LABOR’

Taylor later starred alongside her husband, Ben Stiller, in films, including "Zoolander" and "DodgeBall." The couple married in 2000, separated in 2017 and later reconciled. They share two children, Ella and Quinlin.

Ben Stiller and Christine Taylor share two children together. (Evan Agostini/AP)

Taylor’s experience is part of a broader pattern in Hollywood, where a recognizable television role does not always guarantee financial security. Several former television stars have revealed that their salaries and residual checks were dramatically different from what audiences assumed.
JODIE SWEETIN SHARES SHOCKING 'FULL HOUSE' RESIDUAL CHECK AMOUNT DESPITE SHOW'S MEGA SUCCESS

"The Sopranos" star Drea de Matteo recently said she was forced to find alternative income after acting work slowed down. The actress revealed that she turned to OnlyFans after facing financial difficulties and a lien on her home.

During an appearance on Jamie Kennedy’s podcast, de Matteo said she earned enough through the platform to pay off a $75,000 lien within 75 minutes of posting a bikini photo. She also said she sometimes earned approximately $100,000 per month.

More recently, "Married... with Children" star Ted McGinley revealed that he receives extremely small residual checks from some of his popular television projects, despite starring in long-running shows.

In an interview with Page Six, McGinley — who also found fame on "Happy Days" and "The Love Boat" throughout the 1970s, ’80s and '90s — said he's holding on to a "whole stack" of checks each worth a total of one penny.
Ted McGinley is seen in New York City on May 2, 2026. (Jason Howard/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images)

title: Aaron Rodgers’ famous exes from Shailene Woodley to the romance that sent him into a 'tailspin'
summary: Aaron Rodgers says he regretted letting now-wife Brittani go years earlier, revealing the secret timeline from their 2017 meeting to their 2025 elopement.
story: Actress Shailene Woodley laughs and keeps walking after being asked whether she has anything to say about ex-fiancé Aaron Rodgers and his recent remarks about their relationship. (BACKGRID)
Aaron Rodgers’ love life has taken him from Hollywood romances and a broken engagement to a secret wedding years in the making.

Rodgers’ road to marriage was anything but a straight line. After high-profile romances with Olivia Munn, Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley, the NFL star ultimately found his way back to the woman he says he regretted letting go years earlier.

The now 42-year-old football star's dating life began drawing celebrity-media attention in the late 2000s and early 2010s. Actress Jessica Szohr was among his earliest well-documented Hollywood connections, but his relationships became substantially more public once he began dating Munn in 2014.
AARON RODGERS MAKES BOMBSHELL CLAIMS ABOUT SHAILENE WOODLEY SPLIT

Aaron Rodgers’ dating history includes high-profile romances with Jessica Szohr, Olivia Munn, Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley, pictured, before he reunited with the woman he calls his "biggest regret" and secretly married in 2025. (Getty Images)
Jessica Szohr

The "Gossip Girl" star and Rodgers had an on-and-off relationship in the early 2010s. Szohr and the quarterback were first linked in 2011, after being spotted publicly together. The former couple initially ended things because of their busy schedules.
The two reportedly rekindled their relationship in 2014 before calling it quits again.
Their romance preceded Rodgers’ more heavily publicized relationships, and the pair appeared to remain on friendly terms afterward.
Jessica Szohr and Aaron Rodgers had an on-again-off-again relationship. (Neilson Barnard/Getty Images)
While there aren't many public details about the couple's rumored relationship, People reported Szohr later attended Rodgers’ birthday party in 2017.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Olivia Munn
Rodgers met Olivia Munn while presenting the Song of the Year award at the ACM Awards in 2014. Their relationship quickly became one of his most high-profile romances.
While both had busy schedules, Munn explained how the two made it work.

"There’s a lot of traveling, a lot of driving, and then you’re just really happy with the decisions that you make. And for me, it comes at a time in my life when I end up having to say no to some work because I gotta be somewhere else. It doesn’t make me sad or anything, because I want my life to be full and have all those experiences, so you kind of figure it out as you go," she told E! News in 2014.
Aaron Rodgers' first high-profile romance was with actress Olivia Munn. (Chris Weeks/Getty Images)
Engagement rumors between the two began to surface in 2016 and Munn even stepped out with a ruby on her ring finger. However, the two called it quits just a few months later.

"When you are living out a relationship in the public eye, it’s definitely… it’s difficult. It has some extra constraints, because you have other opinions about your relationship, how it affects your work and, you know, just some inappropriate connections," Rodgers told ESPN shortly after the breakup.
During their relationship, it became public that Rodgers was estranged from his family, and many of his fans blamed Munn for the rift.
Aaron Rodgers and Olivia Munn arrive at the Vanity Fair Oscar Party in Beverly Hills on Feb. 22, 2015. (Reuters)

"There's this whole big narrative that stayed with me for so many years, but there was just this dynamic in the family that had nothing to do with me. It became this whole big thing, and people were like, 'I can't with her, she's keeping this family apart,'" Munn said during a 2025 appearance on the "Armchair Expert" podcast.

In Ian O'Connor’s 2024 biography "Out of the Darkness: The Mystery of Aaron Rodgers," Rodgers shared that the cause of the schism was "deep-rooted." He also clarified that Munn "had nothing to do all the years" of prior estrangement.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Danica Patrick
Rodgers traded Hollywood glamour for racing royalty when he began dating Danica Patrick.

The former IndyCar and NASCAR star confirmed their romance in January 2018, years after the two had initially crossed paths at the ESPYs. The two had actually kept in touch via email before sparks flew.
Danica Patrick and Aaron Rodgers began dating in 2018. (Chris Graythen/Getty Images)

"We kept in touch a little bit, and there were some years we didn’t talk to each other, and then some every now and again, but it wasn’t until obviously recently that we actually had phone numbers. We referred to each other as Chicago and Green Bay – it was very cute," Patrick told Jenny McCarthy on her SiriusXM show.
The relationship quickly became serious and highly visible, with the pair making public appearances and Rodgers openly discussing their life together.

"We’re just two people who enjoy being around each other and love each other," he told Artful Living in 2018. "We’re really into each other… we’re really attracted to each other… we really enjoy traveling… She’s up for anything travel-wise, which is fun. She’s a good travel partner because she’s so laid-back and low-maintenance. And she’s a hell of a cook, so we love just staying in, too. She eats really healthy. She’s inspired me in that way."
But there would be no trip down the aisle: after more than two years as a couple, Patrick's representative confirmed their split in July 2020.
In a 2025 appearance on "The Sage Steele Show," Patrick spoke about her time with Rodgers, claiming that "the nature of the relationship was emotionally abusive."
Danica Patrick claimed that her relationship with Aaron Rodgers was "emotionally abusive." (Getty Images)

"He leaves a trail of blood," she said, later adding, "It gave me the greatest gift, the greatest gift, which is myself. It gave me the greatest gift of how much I needed to show up for myself and take care of myself."

On a recent episode of "Not Just Football with Cam Heyward," Rodgers shared his side of the story, saying, "I dated Danica. She had just retired. She was depressed and not fun to be around. But I didn’t leave her because I was trying to be there and be a good partner. Then it was going a certain direction, obviously. There was no intimacy; there was nothing."
"She tells a story that she was so blindsided… and that ‘he leaves a trail of blood around him.’ And I’m like, what are you talking about? That is not what happened, by any means."

Shailene Woodley
If Rodgers’ previous romances generated headlines, his whirlwind relationship with Shailene Woodley took things to another level.
Speculation the two were romantically linked first surfaced in 2020, but by February 2021, Rodgers stunned fans by revealing he was engaged while accepting his third NFL MVP award.
Aaron Rodgers and Shailene Woodley first sparked romantic speculation in 2020. (Getty Images)
Woodley soon confirmed she was the mystery fiancée.

But the fairy-tale ending never arrived. Their engagement unraveled, and the pair ultimately separated in 2022 after attempts at reconciliation. The breakup has remained a subject of public discussion: Woodley has spoken about experiencing a deeply difficult period around that time, while Rodgers offered his own sharply different account of their relationship and split in September 2026.

On Heyward's podcast, Rodgers explained that he didn't "ruin" the actress' life during their 2022 split. "I proposed to Shailene and she said yes. Now, she maybe felt like she was forced to make a decision. She could have said no," Rodgers began.
Shailene Woodley and Aaron Rodgers officially called it quits in 2022. (Getty Images)

"A couple days after that, she tells me, 'Before we get married, I gotta go f--- this guy,' and I’m like – because her story is that I ruined her life and gave her crazy depression because I left her. But in actuality, she told me that, and then she took off the ring by March – I proposed in December – and we had a couple of times where we tried to get reunited and nothing ever happened," he said.

"There wasn’t even a relationship in 2022 to break off. She literally told me, 'I don’t want to be with you' after we tried some reconciliation in 2021. There’s just a lot of narrative out there that isn’t true," Rodgers clarified.
Woodley has not responded to Rodgers' claims.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Brittani
After years of very public romances, Rodgers ultimately married someone who has made a point of staying almost completely out of the spotlight.
Rodgers revealed in June 2025 that he was a married man and later identified his wife only as Brittani.

"In 2017, I met my wife, and at the time, she was leaving the States and going back to Europe," he told Heyward on the September podcast. "And my biggest regret is not begging her to stay or proposing right there, because that sent me right there into a tailspin of what can I be accused of as a partner in a relationship."
Aaron Rodgers revealed he married Brittani in 2025. (Michael Owens/Getty Images)

The NFL star explained he met Brittani while she was living in Austin after attending the University of Texas. After the two didn't work out, she moved back to Europe before they reconnected years later.
"She was engaged, then I got engaged, and luckily, for me, we came back together," he said.

The couple quietly eloped in 2025, with Rodgers deliberately keeping his new wife away from the celebrity circus that surrounded his previous relationships. And the notoriously private quarterback is already looking toward their next chapter: Rodgers said in September 2026 that he hopes fatherhood is in his future after football.

title: Alix Earle’s stepmom owns ‘reckless’ past, from Spitzer escort scandal to affair with influencer’s dad
summary: Alix Earle's stepmother Ashley Earle details her role in the Eliot Spitzer scandal and affair with TJ Earle in a revealing new essay for Elle.
story: Alix Earle talks Super Bowl LX and also gives insight on her upcoming reality show with her sister.
Ashley Earle isn’t running from her "reckless" past anymore.

Alix Earle’s stepmother opened up about the choices that once made her tabloid fodder, including her connection to the Eliot Spitzer prostitution scandal and her affair with the influencer’s married father. Alix, 25, shot to fame on TikTok and has built a massive following by sharing her life online – including, at times, the complicated family history that played out in the tabloids when she was a child.
Ashley was thrust into the national spotlight in 2008 when she was identified as an escort connected to then-New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer in the prostitution scandal that preceded his resignation.

"At 19, while working as a cocktail waitress, a man approached me and told me I could make $1,000 an hour going on dates with high-profile men," she wrote in an essay for Elle. "My first answer was no, but I kept his card. Eventually, I made the call. I could spend paragraphs explaining why. I was young. I wanted money and independence. I’d spent years operating in survival mode and had become very good at compartmentalizing. But ultimately, I made the call. It was my decision."
ALIX EARLE SPOTTED DANCING WITH TOM BRADY IN ST. BARTS: WHAT TO KNOW ABOUT THE SOCIAL MEDIA SENSATION
Ashley Earle, Alix Earle’s stepmother, opened up about the "reckless" choices that made her tabloid fodder nearly two decades ago. (Getty Images)
According to Ashley, she managed the work for two years without anyone knowing.

"Then, when I was 22, the FBI knocked on my door and showed me a photograph of a man I had seen," she explained. "I didn’t know who he was. When they told me he was the governor of New York, I couldn’t begin to understand what was about to happen."
What followed was a level of attention Ashley said she never could have anticipated.

"Soon, my stage name and face were on the front page of The New York Post. There was an almost ridiculous irony to it," she recalled. "I had come to New York City wanting to be noticed, and suddenly everyone noticed me – for the one thing I never wanted anyone to know."
‘DUCK DYNASTY’ STAR SADIE ROBERTSON HUFF ADMITS ‘FEARS’ OVER PUTTING HER KIDS ON REALITY TV
Ashley Earle was identified as an escort connected to former New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer in the prostitution scandal that preceded Eliot Spitzer’s resignation. (Monica Schipper/Getty Images)
Ashley said she can now look back at that period without minimizing the role she played.

"Context isn’t absolution. I made choices. Some were reckless," she wrote. "Some were selfish. They had consequences. I can own all of that without believing those choices have to be the most interesting thing about me forever."

Ashley's affair with TJ hit the tabloids in 2008, months after she made headline news with the Spitzer scandal. The two had met by chance at a restaurant in New Jersey and things escalated from there. "We talked for five or six hours, and our connection was immediate," Ashley recalled.

"TJ was married," she admitted. "We crossed a line we shouldn’t have crossed, and I take responsibility for my part in that. Our choices affected and hurt other people, including his wife, Alisa, and daughters, Alix and Ashtin, and I don’t take that lightly."
Alix was just a child when the affair turned her family life into tabloid news.

Ashley Earle also acknowledged her affair with Alix Earle’s married father, TJ Earle, which thrust Alix Earle’s family into the spotlight. (Arnaldo Magnani/Getty Images)

"I remember the day very clearly," Alix said on a 2023 episode of "Call Her Daddy." "Paparazzi had shown up at my house and my mom quickly kind of got me and my sister out of the house over to our cousins. We stayed there for a few days and I had no idea what was going on. I didn't know they were paparazzi. I thought news broadcasters were interviewing the neighbors."
While Alix was too young to understand what was happening at the time, she later discovered who Ashley was.

"It was in like fourth grade," she told host Alex Cooper. "I started to kind of hear commentary from people and I had an iPad at the time. I'm Googling my family and, all of a sudden, I see that the past two years of my life had been a lie."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Alix Earle has previously described the painful impact the scandal had on her childhood and family life. (Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images for Netflix)

"My dad had an affair with someone who was well-known for her job having sexual relations with high-class people and one of them was even the governor of New York," Alix said. "She was very well-known from that and, in turn, my dad's affair became a very public situation."
Ashley and TJ later married in 2013. But the fallout followed Alix beyond her family’s front door and into her childhood. Friends often weren't allowed to come over to her home.
"The parents would kind of tell my mom, and she would tell me kind of the harsh truth of why this can't happen," she said. "She would have to sit me down and be like, 'They don't really respect us.'"
Behind closed doors, Alix was also grappling with her father's new relationship.

"When my stepmom started to hang around with my dad after he had moved out, she came into his life, and we were introduced to her, which was super weird," Alix explained. "And I was told that I had to be respectful to this woman, and we had to be nice to her. I wanted to rip her head off. It was very weird because I felt like I was a 10-year-old having to be more mature than someone 20, 30 years older than me."

Ashley Earle, who later married TJ Earle, said she no longer wants to be defined by her past mistakes. (Alexander Tamargo/Getty Images)
Despite their difficult beginning, Ashley eventually became a permanent part of the Earle family. Their relationship evolved in the years that followed, as Ashley and TJ built a life together.
Nearly two decades later, Ashley said she no longer feels the need to convince the world that she is more than her past.
"Twenty years ago, I wanted everyone to understand me. Today, I don’t," Ashley wrote. "The people sitting around my dinner table know who I am. So do I."

"I’m not ashamed of the young woman I was," Ashley added. "I wouldn’t make all of her choices again, but I’m also done wishing her away. She was ambitious, reckless, complicated and sometimes very wrong. But she kept going."

"We live in a culture that can preserve a person’s worst moment forever," she mused. "Accountability matters, but so does allowing people to grow. If we believe that no one can become more than the bad decision they made at 19 or 22, then we leave very little room for any of us to change."

title: Prince Harry’s push to give Archie, Lilibet royal upbringing exposes ‘contradiction’ after palace exit: expert
summary: Prince Harry's children started school in England as experts question whether he can mend the rift with King Charles and Prince William first.
story: British royals expert Hillary Fordwich says Prince Harry is showing signs he wants his children to embrace their English heritage and family roots.
Prince Harry wants his children to embrace their British roots and royal heritage, but one expert says there's a glaring "contradiction."

"Harry spent years telling us why he needed to escape royal life, said his father and brother were trapped, but now appears determined to make sure his children understand and retain their connection to it," Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube's "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital.

"Perhaps with time and distance, he has realized that walking away from royal duties was much easier than walking away from the history, family and identity that came with them," Schofield said. "Ultimately, Harry may finally be recognizing what has always seemed so obvious to the rest of us — being born a prince is an unbelievable privilege."
PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK MOVE PUTS FRESH SPOTLIGHT ON THEIR EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS AGAINST ROYAL FAMILY

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle attend the ESPY Awards on July 11, 2024, in Hollywood, California. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have relocated to the U.K. and are eager to teach their two young children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, about their British roots. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for W+P)

On Aug. 20, it was announced that Harry and his wife, Meghan Markle, had decided to return to the U.K. for an extended stay beginning this fall, but they would not resume their roles as working royals. Their children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, recently started school in England.

A source told People magazine that Harry "wants them to understand the world he grew up in and where their family comes from." Fox News Digital reached out to Archewell, which handles the offices of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, for comment.

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle pose with their newborn baby son, Archie Harrison Mountbatten-Windsor, in St. George's Hall at Windsor Castle in Windsor, west of London, on May 8, 2019. (Pool/AFP via Getty Images)

"It is totally understandable that Harry wants Archie and Lilibet to grow up appreciating their British heritage, traditions and knowing their extended family," British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital. "But after all he has said and done, it's highly unlikely the family will ever trust Harry or welcome them all back into the family fold."
WATCH: PRINCE HARRY WANTS HIS CHILDREN TO EMBRACE ENGLISH HERITAGE: EXPERT

"It would have been surprising if he felt California was like home or in any way comparable to anything his children could experience in the U.K.," Fordwich argued. "He has expressed wanting his children to understand their paternal history."

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back as working royals and moved to California more than six years ago. They later signed lucrative contracts with Netflix and Spotify as they sought to become financially independent.

Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, Nicole Avant, and Ted Sarandos attend Netflix's BEEF season 2 Montecito Tastemaker at a private residence on April 10, 2026, in Montecito, California. (Stefanie Keenan)

In a series of interviews and Harry's memoir "Spare," the couple said they left Britain to escape the restrictions of royal life and criticized palace officials for being insensitive to Meghan's mental health while alleging that at least one member of the royal family had expressed racist views when she was pregnant with their first child. Meghan, a former actress, is biracial.
Prince Harry's book "Spare" is displayed in a bookstore on Dec. 16, 2023, in Bath, England. (Matt Cardy/Getty Images)

Although relations with some members of the royal family have soured since then, Harry told the BBC in 2025 that he wanted to reconcile with his family. In the same interview, however, Harry said he could not envision bringing Meghan and their children back to the U.K. because of concerns over their security. His father, King Charles III, continues to receive treatment for an undisclosed form of cancer.

"Harry and Meghan want their children to build close relationships with their cousins, in fact, the whole British royal family," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle moved their family from California to England late last month. (Getty Images)

"Allegedly, this was one of the deciding factors in their U.K. return. It is understandable at this point why the family will keep their distance from the Sussexes. Harry and Meghan, for their children's sake, should work toward peace with the family. Not just a sweeping statement about reconciliation and doing the exact opposite. But Harry will absolutely want his children to understand their heritage and that they are part of the British royal family."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex leave St Paul's Cathedral after attending the Service of Thanksgiving during Queen Elizabeth II's Platinum Jubilee celebrations in London, on June 3, 2022. (Wiktor Szymanowicz/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images)
A source told People magazine that the family's decision to leave California for an extended period wasn't easy for Meghan.
"They've been planning this for some time, and they feel it's the right thing for their family, but that doesn't mean leaving was easy," the insider explained to the outlet.
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, was born in California. (Karwai Tang/WireImage)

"Meghan really loves their life in Montecito and their home there. They know it's going to take a little bit of time for everyone to settle in and adjust. There's excitement about what's ahead too, especially for the kids. They're really happy for them, and for everything they'll get to experience."
One of the gates to the Riven Rock neighborhood, where Prince Harry and Meghan Markle own a home, is pictured in Montecito, near Santa Barbara, California, on Aug. 24, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)
Schofield noted that Harry was eager for his children to have a closer relationship with their grandfather despite tensions within the royal family.

"I think Harry has reached a point where he recognizes that Britain is a huge part of his children's identity," Schofield said. "Archie and Lili are grandchildren of the king. Their grandfather is on the currency. Their uncle will be king. Their cousins are the future of the monarchy. They would be given privileges and opportunities in the U.K. that they simply wouldn't attract in the States."
Prince Harry told the BBC in 2025 that he's ready for reconciliation. (Samir Hussein/WireImage)

"I think Harry wants to reopen the royal door, but perhaps on his own terms," Schofield continued. "The problem is that the monarchy has never operated that way. Harry may want his children to enjoy the history, relationships and privileges that come with being part of the royal family while maintaining the independence he chose in 2020. That tension has been at the heart of this story from the very beginning."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Prince William and Prince Harry are seen together in 2021. (Getty Images)

"That is the uncomfortable reality: You can bring your children to the U.K. and surround them with British traditions, but their most meaningful connection to Britain is their family. If Harry genuinely wants Archie and Lilibet to understand their royal heritage, eventually he has to confront the fact that his children barely know the relatives who embody it."

Archie was a baby when his parents left the U.K. in 2020. Lilibet was born in California in 2021. Before this year's relocation, their last visit to the U.K. was in July for a private family trip that included a reunion with the king at Highgrove House. Before that, the children had not visited the U.K. since June 2022 for Queen Elizabeth II's Platinum Jubilee.
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle leave a service of thanksgiving for the reign of Queen Elizabeth II at St. Paul's Cathedral in London on June 3, 2022. (Matt Dunham - WPA Pool/Getty Images)

A source told People magazine that Harry and his father spoke by phone during the Duke of Sussex's first week back in the U.K. The two have yet to meet in person again since the Sussexes returned on Aug. 26. Multiple royal experts told Fox News Digital that Harry and his older brother, Prince William, haven't spoken since 2022.
King Charles, Queen Camilla and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex attend The Prince of Wales' 70th Birthday Patronage Celebration at Buckingham Palace in London on May 22, 2018. (Chris Jackson/Getty Images)
"Harry cannot expect the children to repair what the adults have broken," Schofield said. "Any meaningful relationships between the cousins would require trust between their parents first."

"Prince William is going to prioritize his three children, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, and their privacy. If Harry wants those relationships for his children, rebuilding trust with William becomes increasingly important. And I do think that burden is on Harry. Any pressure on Prince William to reconcile is wildly unfair."
Prince Harry celebrated his 42nd birthday on Sept. 15 back in England. (Getty Images)
Still, Chard noted that children could help soften strained relationships between family members and "serve as a bridge."

"So I ran after I tied my shoelace and stood where I possibly could in the front line, and they started counting Malaya, Cyprus and I was the next one. Germany. I went to Germany. I was just I just missed Cyprus by one.
