title: Reporter's Notebook: Congress faces a crisis that the 'AI godfather' warns it may not be ready to address
summary: Geoffrey Hinton warns Congress has a year max to act on artificial intelligence, but political gridlock and midterms could delay legislation.
story: Fox News chief congressional correspondent Chad Pergram reports on House lawmakers leaving Washington for recess before passing artificial intelligence safety legislation. Pergram details briefings from computer scientist Jeffrey Hinton and Senate opposition to proposed kill-switch mandates following a cybersecurity breach involving Google Gemini models.
To hear estimates about the growing power of AI, one might ask AI chatbots how long it will take Congress to regulate the technology.
But you might not need to do that.
You could just inquire with your trusty Capitol Hill correspondent. Let’s call this chatbot "ChadGPT."
REPORTER’S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS MEETS AI AS FEARS OF HUMAN EXTINCTION JOLT CAPITOL HILL
Bipartisan lawmakers, including Senators Josh Hawley and Richard Blumenthal, introduced the GUARD Act to protect minors from unregulated AI chatbots. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
And it truly doesn’t require that much congressional clairvoyance to divine when lawmakers could address AI – despite the forecast of a looming crisis.
You just need a little understanding of the congressional parliamentary posture over the next few months.

It’s doubtful that Congress will do anything about AI until after the midterms. Or, maybe even early next year. Results of the midterms will likely consume the lame duck session – regardless of which party wins or loses. Plus, lawmakers must fund the government by mid-December. If either the House or Senate flips, it might be March or April next year until Congress returns to AI. It simply takes Congress a long time to accomplish anything. Especially when there’s a change in who runs the place.

The Senate is scheduled to meet for the next two weeks. But House Members fled the Capitol last week – a day earlier than planned and two weeks earlier than the original schedule – even as the "godfather of AI" visited Capitol Hill.
Geoffrey Hinton is professor emeritus at the University of Toronto. He’s a 2004 Nobel laureate for his work on "artificial neural networks." He proffered a stark warning for lawmakers.

Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., summoned Hinton to Capitol Hill for a bipartisan, bicameral briefing on AI. Sanders has called for a ban on "superintelligence." Many lawmakers are furious over what’s unfolded with AI over the past few weeks. They want action now.
I had a battery of questions for Hinton when he emerged from the briefing late last week in the Dirksen Senate Office Building. We’ve heard that Congress is lagging when it comes to taking action.
ANTHROPIC CEO CALLS ON AI INDUSTRY TO SLOW DOWN TECH RACE, DRAWING SUPPORT FROM ELON MUSK, SAM ALTMAN
The proposal comes as Republicans seek to convince voters that keeping the GOP in power would translate into more money in Americans' pockets. (Finn Gomez/Getty Images)
"How much time do lawmakers actually have to get ahead of this before this is a big problem," I asked.
"Very little," replied Hinton.
"What is ‘a little,’" I countered. "A few weeks? A month?"
"Maybe a year," opined Hinton. "But not much more than a year."
Sigh.
Hinton characterized the incident where AI agents went rogue and hacked another company as a "little Chernobyl."
For the uninitiated, that was the epic meltdown of the nuclear reactor in the former Soviet Union in 1986. It’s one of the most extraordinary human-made disasters in history.

But some Republican leaders – and House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., in particular – are downplaying potential doom. Especially after President Trump declared on Truth Social that AI concerns were a "HOAX."

"Do you remember when AOC [Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.] said, was it climate change? What was her stupid thing? She said, ‘we're all going to be dead in ten years,’" said Johnson. "This is what the President is saying. You're not all going to be dead in ten years. That's a hoax."

Johnson isn’t opposed to legislative action on AI. But he’s certainly taking his cues from President Trump. And even though many Democrats and some Republicans demanded that the House remain in session to wrestle with AI, Johnson predicted that the exercise would be moot.
REP. TED LIEU: AI IS ALREADY TOO POWERFUL. WE NEED A KILL SWITCH BEFORE DISASTER STRIKES
Speaker of the House Mike Johnson (R-LA) speaks at a press conference with other members of House Republican leadership in Washington, DC on May 6, 2025. (Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images)

"If I called an emergency session today and I brought everybody in the House and said, ‘let's regulate," I tell you, nobody in the room knows yet what that should look like," said Johnson. "We’re going to have steady hands at the wheel on this."
But other Republicans harbor more fear of rapid AI development.
"What would happen if we created an independent species that became superior to a human species?" asked Sen. John Kennedy, R-La.

Shortly after the briefing with Hinton and others, Kennedy went to the Senate floor and implored his colleagues to pass a bill on the spot requiring AI firms to install a kill switch if their agents rebelled again.
However, Senate Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., blocked that on the floor. He feared that such a mandate could stifle innovation.
"We're going to just put this blanket regulation on the whole economy with no discussion in one fell swoop, on one day, by unanimous consent?" questioned Paul.
Paul’s objection stymied the Senate.
The Kentucky Republican is sanguine about what’s ahead for AI. But he worries about congressional intervention.
"People have feared technology since the beginning of time," said Paul. " I wouldn't put Congress in charge of a McDonald's."
Jeffrey Ladish of Palisade Research assesses the risks of new technology. After the briefing, Ladish offered his own foreboding prediction about AI running amok.
"How is this allowed to happen? And how do we ensure this never happens again?" asked Ladish. "Because right now, I guarantee you this will happen again. We are not on track for fixing this."
Ladish argued that even researchers "don't know how to control it."
That’s why some lawmakers insist that Congress must move fast to combat AI – perhaps even treating it as a new threat.
"The people who are the greatest innovators and creators in the world in the AI space are warning us of serious danger. So shame on us if we don't listen to them," said Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va.

Rep. Don Beyer, D-Va., is studying for a master’s degree in AI at George Masson University. He says people are skeptical about AI. But he suggests that the public may grow even more skeptical if one party tries to legislate on AI without bipartisan buy-in.
TRUMP ANNOUNCES NEW 'AI FORCE,' VOWS TO PROTECT INDUSTRY AS AI CZAR ANNOUNCEMENT NEARS
Rep. Donald Beyer Jr., D-Va., attends a protest in Washington. (Tom Williams/Getty Images)
"We need to do it together. Also, if we do it together, Democrats and Republicans are much less likely to try to reverse it when political winds shift," said Beyer.
Some lawmakers are already targeting a scapegoat. Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, chairs the House Progressive Caucus. He pins the issue on big tech.

"This is on a few billionaires who are the Silicon Valley guys who have developed technology they can't even control," said Casar. "What if it's a hospital next? What if it is nuclear facilities next? That should not be allowed."

That introduces a wedge into the debate. Some Republicans are increasingly saying that Congress should lay off the industry and let it innovate. But Casar is producing a foil which has bedeviled both political parties: big tech.
Don’t forget that we are just six weeks before an election. Democrats are already jockeying for political positions on AI.

"The AI safety issue is very real," said House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y. "That's why it's so irresponsible that Mike Johnson and House Republicans have gotten out of town before sundown."

Could another AI catastrophe compel lawmakers to move sooner? Especially since an expert like Ladish suggests it’s just a matter of time? What if the political battle lines are drawn already between Republicans and Democrats? As far as anyone could tell, John Kennedy was the only Republican who attended the briefing last week. And what if there simply isn’t the political will to move during the lame duck? Or, if Democrats flip the House and Senate, do they try to advance something next year – but it’s viewed as partisan and "big government" by Republicans, standing behind President Trump?
You don’t need ChatGPT to grasp how challenging this may be for Congress. You don’t even need "ChadGPT." These are just the legislative realities.
As Mary Shelley wrote in Frankenstein, the acquisition of knowledge can be dangerous. Especially if who acquired that knowledge is suddenly more powerful than those who built it.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Frankenstein is a tale of unhinged hubris, ethics and ambition. Congress has tried to legislate guardrails for those mortal flaws for more than two centuries now. Those laws are for humans. And whatever Congress comes up with might not matter to AI.
Chad Pergram currently serves as Chief Congressional Correspondent for FOX News Channel (FNC). He joined the network in September 2007 and is based out of Washington, D.C.

title: Mamdani in hot seat over post mourning death of inmate charged with callous crime: 'Absolutely shameful'
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani faces fierce backlash after posting condolences for a jail death suspect charged in the murder of Ron Marte.
story: Mayor Zohran Mamdani faces intense backlash after being booed at a Staten Island pro-police celebration. Fox News' Bryan Llenas breaks down the immense financial scrutiny surrounding his proposals, including a free childcare plan amid projected city budget deficits.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is facing strong pushback from critics after posting his condolences for the death of a jail inmate charged in the killing of an autistic man during an ambush.

"A person in City custody died yesterday evening following a court appearance in Queens," Mamdani posted on X on Thursday. "Department of Correction staff performed CPR until emergency medical services arrived to take him to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead. I extend my condolences to his family. In line with standard practice, the DOC and its oversight partners will investigate the circumstances of his death."

The vast majority of social media users who replied to the post took issue with Mamdani not providing more details about the alleged crime. The individual who died was Luis Alberto Lopez Castillo, who faced charges of murder, manslaughter and robbery related to the 2025 murder of 26-year-old Ron Marte, a man with special needs, the New York Post reported.

Prosecutors allege Castillo and his accomplice Axel Martinez ambushed Marte in the Bronx’s Starlight Park as he walked home from work, with Martinez shooting him in the chest while Castillo took his cellphone.
CITY-RUN BOARD CANCELS LEASE OF ISRAEL DRONE SUPPLIER, SPARKING BACKLASH TOWARD MAMDANI: 'LUDICROUS'
Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks with inmates on Rikers Island while they watch a World Cup semifinal soccer match on July 15, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)
Mamdani’s critics highlighted the post as an example of the mayor showing more concern for suspected criminals than victims.

"Again!" FOX Business anchor David Asman posted on X. "I thought somewhere in the beginning of ‘An Idiot’s Guide to Being Mayor’ here’s a suggestion: ‘Display sympathy for the victims; Not the criminals.’"
"Didn’t he murder a 26 year old special needs man?" Jewish advocacy group StopAntisemitism posted on X.
MAMDANI SETS INTERNET ABLAZE WITH VIDEO EXPLAINING CAVE ON PLAN TO ARREST NETANYAHU: 'WHAT A JOKE'

"The guy Mamdani is mourning here was charged with robbing and murdering a 26 year old with special needs," Benny Polatseck, a former digital producer for former NYC Mayor Eric Adams posted on X. "Did you see any tweets from him mourning his helpless victim?"

"Absolutely shameful…," conservative influencer account Proud Elephant posted on X. "Just when you thought Mamdani couldn’t go any lower. Mamdani should do the right thing and resign from office in disgrace."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during a May Day rally at Washington Square Park in New York City on May 1, 2026. (Yuki Iwamura/AP)
Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani’s office for comment.

Mamdani has faced similar criticism before, including in August when he mourned the death of a man with 27 prior arrests who died in Rikers Island jail while facing charges for murdering a man with a meat cleaver in a Brooklyn laundromat.

Mamdani has been outspoken about his efforts to improve safety and living conditions across the jail system and has made several moves he says will accomplish that, including ending 12-hour shifts for correctional staff, addressing the practice of housing people of different ages together, moving to close Rikers Island, and strengthening oversight under the federal Nunez monitoring agreement.

His administration has begun transferring unused Rikers facilities out of the Department of Correction’s control and opened a 104-bed therapeutic housing unit at Bellevue Hospital to provide incarcerated people with specialized medical care.

New York City has been legally committed since 2019 to closing Rikers and replacing it with four smaller borough-based jails, a plan Mamdani has pledged to accelerate. Critics argue the move would leave the city with fewer jail cells and make it more difficult to tackle crime.
Fox News Digital's Robert Schmad contributed to this report
Andrew Mark Miller is a reporter at Fox News. Find him on Twitter @andymarkmiller and email tips to AndrewMark.Miller@Fox.com.

title: White House won't back down as attorney predicts how Trump's latest press tussle will play out in court
summary: A First Amendment attorney predicts Trump's White House ban on CNN, Politico and MS NOW will fail in court, calling the action blatantly unconstitutional.
story: A First Amendment attorney doesn’t think the Trump administration will be successful in defending its decision to ban three news outlets from the White House grounds.
An attorney at a nonprofit that defends the First Amendment doesn't think President Donald Trump will come out on top in a legal battle with three media outlets he banned from the White House.
But after announcing on Friday his ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico — and the resulting lawsuit against him — the White House told Fox News Digital that Trump isn't backing down.

"I think the Trump administration will not fare well in court because its action here is blatantly unconstitutional," predicted Aaron Terr, the director of public advocacy at the Philadelphia-based Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression (FIRE).

Trump took to TRUTH Social on Friday to announce that employees with the three major media outlets will be banned from White House grounds over "reporting FAKE NEWS. He said they "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States."
President Donald Trump was pressed by reporters about his announced ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico. (Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images)
DISNEY SUES FCC OVER ‘RETALIATORY CAMPAIGN AGAINST ABC,’ SEEKS TO BLOCK EARLY RENEWAL PROCEEDINGS
Terr says that what media outlets report is not at issue.

"There's settled precedent that when the White House opens its doors to the press, which it has done, the First Amendment walks in too," Terr said. "So that means the administration can't ban reporters from the White House grounds just because it doesn't like their point of view or thinks their coverage is too negative or critical, and the president in his statements has been crystal clear that this was the exact reason that he banned CNN, MSN, and ... Politico from the entire White House grounds."

Reporters and cameramen with the outlets removed their gear and set up on Pennsylvania Ave. over the weekend and this week continued to film live hits from across the street rather than from their usual spots on White House grounds.
In response to Terr's assessment, the White House remained defiant about the ban.
Former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt addresses members of the media in the press briefing room. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

"The Fake News has no place demanding a spot in the President’s Oval Office," the White House said. "The lies they smear are a disservice to the American public and tear at the very fabric of our Democracy. They’re completely capable of reporting from directly outside."
CNN FIRES BACK AT TRUMP WHITE HOUSE OVER ATTACKS ON REPORTER, CALLS THEM 'BENEATH THE OFFICE'

Monday morning, the three news outlets filed a lawsuit against Trump seeking an injunction that would halt the president's ban temporarily, and asking the court to immediately order the restoration of the media members' White House credentials.

CNN was scheduled for White House television pool coverage on Monday. Fox News Media, ABC News, CBS News and NBC News, the other press pool networks, announced in a joint statement that they would not take CNN's place.

"The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting," the pool members said in a joint statement.
Additionally, White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA) President Jacqui Heinrich of Fox News, released a statement expressing the organization's support of the outlets.

"Today’s action revoking access for journalists from CNN, POLITICO, and MSNOW violates the First Amendment," she wrote. "The implications extend beyond these organizations: a standard used to exclude one news outlet because of its coverage could be applied to any outlet in the future."

"The American people, through a free and independent press, must be able to scrutinize those elected to power, regardless of whether government officials view it favorably," she continued. "The WHCA calls on the administration to immediately restore our colleagues’ access."
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SUBPOENAS NY TIMES JOURNALISTS IN GRAND JURY LEAK PROBE TIED TO AIR FORCE ONE REPORT

Terr said that while nobody has a First Amendment right to report from the White House, he said court precedent established that once a media outlet gains access to the White House, that access cannot be revoked for ideological reasons.

President Donald Trump speaks to reporters in the press cabin of the new, Qatari-gifted Air Force One after changing planes to return to Washington from RAF Mildenhall, Britain, July 8, 2026. (Jonathan Ernst/Reuters)

"The principle here is that once the government provides access, it then can't condition that access on whether you're expressing a viewpoint that the government agrees with," he said. "It's a broader First Amendment principle that the government cannot retaliate against Americans for protected speech, and that includes revoking news outlets' access to a space open to the press just because the president doesn't like the actual or perceived slant of their report."
Terr noted that while there can be bias in media, the alternative of government-controlled media could result in a much worse outcome.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"The First Amendment is designed to prevent exactly that type of government control over the flow of information in a free society," he said. "The First Amendment guarantees that reporters are free to cover the news in a way that they think is best, and it's up to the American public to hear what they have to say and decide whether or not to trust them and their coverage of the government and other issues in our society."
Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: SEE IT: Chinese nationals intercepted in ‘extremely dangerous’ infiltration attempt near Florida coast
summary: Video shows CBP and the Coast Guard intercepting a 27-foot vessel near Key Largo carrying 13 Chinese nationals and other illegal immigrants.
story: U.S. Customs and Border Protection and the U.S. Coast Guard interdicted a smuggling vessel off the coast of Florida carrying Chinese nationals and other illegal immigrants. (Credit: Ozzy Trevino)

A smuggling vessel filled with Chinese nationals and other illegal immigrants was intercepted by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and the Coast Guard in what sources called a rare and "extremely dangerous" attempt to enter the U.S. through Florida.

CBP confirmed the interdiction exclusively with Fox News, sharing video and photos of U.S. authorities intercepting the vessel, which was carrying 22 illegal immigrants, including 13 Chinese nationals. The boat, a 27-foot cuddy cabin vessel, was stopped, and the migrants aboard were arrested without incident Tuesday. The interdiction took place near Angelfish Creek, Florida, near Key Largo.

According to the agency, a CBP Air and Marine Operations multi-role enforcement aircraft first detected the vessel. The interdiction, carried out by CBP alongside Coast Guard personnel, resulted in the apprehension of one suspected smuggler, a Cuban national, 13 Chinese nationals, eight Ecuadorian nationals and one Dominican national.

Sources emphasized to Fox News that it is extremely rare for Chinese nationals to attempt to enter the U.S. through maritime Caribbean routes that are typically used by Haitians, Dominicans and Cubans. During the Biden administration, Chinese nationals typically entered the U.S. through land routes in California and Texas, which are now subject to tighter enforcement under the Trump administration.
CBP, COAST GUARD INTERCEPT MIGRANT VESSEL HEADING FOR PUERTO RICO; 40 APPREHENDED INCLUDING UZBEK NATIONAL

An image of the interdiction shared exclusively with Fox News shows Chinese nationals and others being apprehended by U.S. authorities off the Florida coast. (U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP))

Andres Blanco, executive director of Air and Marine Operations Southeast Region, told Fox News that "attempting to enter the United States illegally by sea is extremely dangerous and will not go undetected."
Blanco said that "this interdiction demonstrates the strength of our maritime partnerships and our commitment to stopping human smuggling organizations before they can put more lives at risk."
He added that "those who attempt these dangerous voyages face arrest, prosecution, removal, and the very real possibility of losing their lives at sea."
The illegal immigrants were transferred to the U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Pablo Valent for processing. Meanwhile, authorities seized the vessel.
ICE-LED FLORIDA OPERATION NETS 500 — INCLUDING ILLEGAL ALIENS ACCUSED OF MURDER, CHILD ABUSE, CARTEL TIES

Coast Guard and U.S. Customs and Border Protection Air and Marine Operations Southeast Region personnel aboard the U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Pablo Valent intercept a human smuggling vessel carrying Chinese nationals and other illegal immigrants near Key Largo, Florida, on Sept. 15, 2026. (U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP))

After the operation, Coast Guard Lt. Corryn Ulrich, the commanding officer of the Pablo Valent, told Fox News that "the U.S. border remains secure due to highly capable teams and coordinated interagency enforcement" and that "we remain ready to save lives and enforce federal law at sea."
The CBP Air and Marine Operations unit is designed to anticipate and confront aviation and maritime threats to America’s national integrity, according to the agency.
President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are set to meet Thursday in Washington, D.C.
Gatestone Institute senior fellow Gordon Chang claimed that, despite the leaders trumpeting a positive relationship, Xi is mulling a war against the United States and organizing troops "for battle."

"Xi Jinping keeps on talking about going to war against us… and also he's preparing China's society, civilian and military, for battle. And we think we're at peace," Chang said Sunday on "Fox News Live." "So, this is a very dangerous period for us."
Chang’s remarks follow reports that China aided Iran in attacks that killed three U.S. troops in Jordan earlier this summer.
ICE SHOOTING ROCKS AUSTIN AS DEMOCRAT DEMANDS BODYCAM VIDEO, INDEPENDENT PROBE
President Donald Trump shakes hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping while leaving after a visit to the Zhongnanhai Garden in Beijing, China, on Friday, May 15, 2026. (Evan Vucci/AP)

The incident comes amid renewed debate over the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement tactics after a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer shot a Venezuelan illegal immigrant in Austin on Sunday. The Department of Homeland Security said the man shot by the officer, Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, "illegally entered the country under the Biden administration and had a final order of removal during a law enforcement operation."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

His lawyer, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, has contested DHS’ statement, saying Perez entered the U.S. lawfully. According to DHS, he survived and is in stable condition and is in federal custody pending removal. The incident has resulted in large protests in Austin and Democratic politicians condemning ICE and the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement.
Fox News Digital's Nora Moriarty and Stepheny Price contributed to this report.

title: Blue state gov ignites online firestorm with plan to send gov't into homes of newborn babies: 'Lunatic libs'
summary: Massachusetts Democratic Gov. Maura Healey's Welcome Family program sparked a firestorm after a viral clip about home visits for new parents.
story: Massachusetts GOP chair Amy Carnevale tells Fox News Digital that Democratic Gov. Healey's new-mom home visit plan is ‘government overreach'

Massachusetts Democratic Gov. Maura Healey set off an online firestorm over the weekend over a plan to expand the commonwealth's Welcome Family program, which she spoke about in a clip that went viral on social media.

Healey made the controversial comments in an appearance last week on Boston Public Radio, where she discussed the state’s taxpayer-funded plan to send nurses into the homes of new parents after childbirth.

"Everybody in the state, when you have a baby, you're going to have a home visit within days, weeks and that will be an opportunity for a healthcare provider to make an assessment to see if you need some additional support and resources," Healey explained.
The clip quickly made waves on social media, with conservatives blasting the governor’s government expansion.
GAVIN NEWSOM ACCUSED OF 'INFANTILIZING' PARENTS WITH DIAPER PROGRAM IN SCATHING WASHINGTON POST EDITORIAL
FILE - Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey discussed the state’s taxpayer-funded plan to send nurses into the homes of new parents after childbirth. (David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)
"Does this sound like a good idea?" conservative radio host Howie Carr wrote on X in a post viewed almost 2 million times.

"I’m sorry what?!" Conservative influencer account Libs of TikTok wrote on X in a post that was viewed over 2 million times. "MA Governor Maura Healey says everyone who has a baby will be visited in their home by a government appointed healthcare provider ‘to make an assessment’. Stay out of our homes you power hungry creep."
"IDK who needs to hear this… but the government DOES NOT OWN your baby," Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C. posted on X. "Everyone needs to re-read 1984. "
‘COVID 2.0’: LAWMAKERS PUSH BACK ON SWEEPING HEALTH 'POLICE POWER' IN KEY BATTLEGROUND STATE
"Lunatic libs," Sen. Tim Sheehy, R-Mont., posted on X.
Fox News Digital reached out to Healey’s office for comment.

Healey announced the expansion last week in a press release that described the program as "voluntary" and meant to "strengthen postpartum care and mental health support for mothers and families across Massachusetts, with a focus on reaching people earlier, making support easier to access and helping providers connect patients to care when they need it."

Postpartum care has been a major topic of conversation in Massachusetts in light of the highly publicized trial of Lindsay Clancy in the commonwealth, where a jury recently deadlocked and could not come to a consensus whether Clancy was guilty of killing her three young children. Clancy's defense team argued that she suffered from severe postpartum mental illness.

"Becoming a mother is a profound life change, and every parent deserves support—not just during pregnancy, but in the months that follow," Healey said in the release. "Postpartum depression, anxiety and other maternal mental health conditions are real medical conditions, and no mother should feel ashamed to ask for help or feel like she has to navigate this journey alone. We’re working to expand postpartum care, identify concerns earlier and connect families to the mental health support they need, because taking care of moms means taking care of the whole family."
Amy Carnevale, chair of the Massachusetts Republican Party, told Fox News Digital in an interview that "this is an example of the government overreaching."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Gov. Maura Healey turns toward supporters after signing legislation strengthening abortion protections and prioritizing access to care at the Massachusetts State House on Aug. 10, 2026, in Boston. (Jessica Rinaldi/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)

"I'm a mom of three," Carnevale said. "I'm blessed to have three wonderful children. And, doctors, today, they ask about postpartum depression. They ask about the need for resources. So, there are plenty of resources available to women after they have children in Massachusetts and nationwide. And this example by Gov. Healey to send people into the homes of new moms is an example of government overreach and the Massachusetts Republican Party has been hearing from moms across the state, moms and dads across the state, really objecting to this new policy."
Fox News Digital’s Amanda Macias contributed to this report

title: The Soros political machine is putting millions to work before Election Day — and zeroing in on key races
summary: Tens of millions from the Soros family flow to Democratic allies as campaign finance records reveal over $40 million in disbursements before Election Day.
story: Senior national correspondent Rich Edson reports from Belleville, Michigan, as progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed wins the Democratic Senate primary, narrowly defeating Haley Stevens. Rep. Jim Banks, R-Ind., discusses El-Sayed's alignment with the Democratic Socialists of America platform, including healthcare and border policies.
Tens of millions of dollars in Soros-linked money are pouring into key Democratic campaigns and political groups as Election Day approaches, campaign finance records show.

As of the end of June, Democracy PAC and Democracy PAC II — a pair of political committees created and funded by the Soros network — have disbursed over $40 million in donations to their Democratic allies, a review of campaign finance records show. Among the largest beneficiaries of the Soros-linked funding have been the Schumer-aligned Senate Majority PAC, House Majority PAC and the J Street Action Fund, the political arm of J Street, a vocal critic of Israeli government policies.

Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, who has made getting money out of politics a pillar of his Senate campaign, is also indirectly benefiting from Soros-linked money flowing into the Michigan Senate race through outside Democratic groups.
MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL CALLS AIPAC DONATIONS 'LEGALIZED BRIBERY,' REMAINS SILENT ON OTHER DONATIONS
George Soros, founder of the Open Society Foundations, arrives for a meeting in Brussels, Belgium, on April 27, 2017. (Olivier Hoslet/AFP via Getty Images)
Senate Majority PAC, which has received $9 million from the Soros-funded Democracy PAC this cycle, has pledged $30 million in spending to help elect El-Sayed in Michigan.

"The fundamental corruption of our politics has been the system that allows corporations and would-be oligarchs and billionaires to buy politicians," El-Sayed said during a 2025 interview with a local news outlet.
"I want to get money out of politics, put money in your pocket, pass Medicare for all," he told a reporter during a follow-up interview.

El-Sayed’s campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Monday. The Senate hopeful is also scheduled to attend a Sept. 28 California fundraiser hosted by Jeffrey Soros – who is the nephew of billionaire George Soros.

"Abdul El-Sayed is only for ‘money out of politics’ when it isn’t being spent on him. He’s wining and dining Soros billionaires and begging Chuck Schumer for money while Mike Rogers is taking on Big Pharma and calling for a suspension of the gas tax to lower costs for working families," Alyssa Brouillet, a spokeswoman for Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers, told Fox News Digital. "Mike Rogers is fighting for Michigan. Abdul El-Sayed is cozying up to billionaires and lying to Michiganders."
The full scale of the Soros family’s 2026 political spending will become clearer as additional campaign-finance reports are filed.
FBI RAIDS SOROS-BACKED VOTER GROUP’S HEADQUARTERS IN REPORTED FRAUD PROBE
Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed leaves the stage after speaking during the Michigan Democratic Party's nominating convention in Lansing on Aug. 29, 2026. (Sarah Rice/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Another major beneficiary of the Soros family’s largesse has been the federal and non-federal arms of its Justice & Public Safety PAC, the primary vehicle behind its efforts to elect progressive prosecutors across the United States. The criminal justice-focused committees have so far pulled in close to $2 million.

The Soros family, chiefly through George Soros’ Open Society Foundations and political committees, has funded efforts to reduce the number of criminals in prison, end cash bail, elect progressive prosecutors, expand rights for illegal immigrants and address alleged racism among law enforcement — efforts that have made Soros a frequent target of criticism from conservative politicians and activists.

Other causes to receive support from the Soros family during the 2026 cycle have included the League of Conservation Voters Action Fund, Fair Fight, which is a voter mobilization organization founded by Stacey Abrams and focused on helping Democrats in Georgia, and the Working Families Party PAC, which works to help elect progressives primarily in New York.
Democratic Govs. Josh Shapiro, of Pennsylvania, and Abigail Spanberger, of Virginia, also received financial support from the Soros family’s political committees during their 2025 campaigns.

Up-and-coming GOP star Rep. title: Trump's Greenland fixation revealed as wars expose why the Arctic island matters now more than ever
summary: President Donald Trump's Greenland interest spotlights critical minerals and oil as Strait of Hormuz disruptions threaten global energy supplies.
story: Robert Price, CEO of Greenland Energy Company and president of USFM Corporation, says the agreement could bolster long-term investment and US security as China, Russia loom over critical mineral supplies.
President Donald Trump's persistent interest in Greenland has put a spotlight on what lies beneath the vast Arctic island, including potentially valuable deposits of critical minerals and oil.

That focus intensified this week after Trump reached a security agreement with Denmark and Greenland that he is signing on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly on Tuesday — a deal the administration says is intended to strengthen U.S. influence in the Arctic and bolster long-term investment in the island.

The focus on obtaining control and influence in Greenland, which also has a highly strategic location in the world, comes as wars in Ukraine and Iran expose vulnerabilities in global energy supplies and the U.S. looks to reduce its dependence on foreign sources of critical minerals.

"One of the reasons that we are exploring for oil in Greenland is because of what's going on in the Strait of Hormuz right now," Robert Price, CEO of Greenland Energy Company and president of USFM Corporation, told Fox News Digital.
Price's two companies are pursuing separate oil and mineral projects in Greenland, including plans to drill an exploratory oil well in 2027 and ongoing mineral exploration in the island's west.
Greenland’s melting ice is opening new Arctic shipping routes and exposing critical mineral resources, adding to the island’s growing strategic importance. (Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Getty Images)
WHY TRUMP ZEROED IN ON GREENLAND, THE WORLD’S LARGEST ISLAND, MOSTLY COVERED IN ICE — IN 3 CHARTS

Those projects are taking on new significance as conflicts abroad strain global energy supplies and highlight vulnerabilities in critical supply chains. The Iran conflict has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical artery for global oil supplies, while the war in Ukraine has put energy infrastructure at the center of the conflict.

Trump announced an agreement with Denmark and Greenland on Friday that would expand the U.S. military presence on the island while keeping Greenland under Danish sovereignty. Full details have not yet been made public, but Fox News Digital obtained exclusive insights into some of the specifics of the agreement.
"We don't want to be dependent on China for our rare earth minerals, and we don't want to be dependent on Russia for them either," Price said.
"Critical minerals, they touch every part of our lives, which includes our cellphones, our computers, batteries, power storage, power generation," he said.
Price's USFM has been drilling around Disko Island in western Greenland for nickel, copper, palladium and cobalt, commodities used in electronics, batteries, energy and manufacturing.
"This mining district could be one of the largest mining districts in the world," he said, comparing its potential with Russia's mineral-rich Norilsk region.
The scale Price described has not been proven, with exploratory drilling still underway.
TRUMP'S AMBITIOUS ENERGY BET COULD BE A WINNING HAND AS THE WORLD BURNS MORE OIL, GAS THAN EVER
Greenland's potential riches aren't limited to minerals.

Price's Greenland Energy Company is pursuing permits for an exploratory oil well planned for 2027. Its licenses are on Greenland's eastern side, where Price said the geology resembles the petroleum-producing North Sea.
"Our licenses are similar to the same petroleum system as the North Sea," Price said, noting that his company has sampled oil on and below the surface.
But Greenland's value extends beyond what may lie beneath the surface.

Sitting between North America and Europe and extending into the Arctic, the island has played a role in U.S. defense for decades. The U.S. maintains Pituffik Space Base there, its northernmost Defense Department installation.

A composite image shows President Donald Trump overlaid on a protest in Greenland. Trump announced an agreement concerning U.S. security interests in Greenland, while Denmark and Greenland have emphasized that the deal preserves their sovereignty and territorial integrity. (Sean Gallup/Getty Images; rtur Widak/Anadolu via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Price said Trump's emerging deal with Denmark and Greenland could provide greater security and give companies more confidence to invest in projects that take years to develop.
"What it does is it shores up long-term investment in Greenland, and that's what our projects are," Price said. "They're long-term investments from oil, gas, and minerals."
"We're really excited about this agreement," he added.

title: AOC joins Macklemore frenzy in bizarre fundraising memo targeting pro-Trump billionaire
summary: Rapper Macklemore gained a new ally in Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who blasted Robert Kraft for allegedly forcing Ed Sheeran to drop him from tour.
story: Fox News contributor Joe Concha analyzes Ed Sheeran addressing concertgoers after multiple opening acts withdrew from his tour over the removal of rapper Macklemore.
Rapper Macklemore is getting a new ally as he continues to face backlash for his pro-Palestinian activism during his opening set for Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour earlier this month.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., invoked the ongoing controversy in a fundraising memo sent to supporters late last week, in which she also criticized billionaire Robert Kraft for reportedly getting Sheeran to drop Macklemore from his concert tour.

"Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez here. Billionaire stadium owner, Robert Kraft, did not like Macklemore, a Grammy-winning rapper, saying 'Free Palestine' on stage — so he made calls and the artist got pulled off of Ed Sheeran’s tour," the fundraising text obtained by Fox News Digital said.

"This is not just about a single musical act. This is about how a small handful of powerful people, like stadium owners, can threaten someone’s livelihood in order to prevent an entire massive issue from being spoken about — in this case, the genocide in Gaza."
COLIN KAEPERNICK ACCUSES NFL OF 'COLLUDING' AGAINST MACKLEMORE AMID 'FREE PALESTINE' CONTROVERSY
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez defended Macklemore in a fundraising text message to supporters. (Graeme Sloan/Getty Images; Kristy Sparow/Getty Images)
She went on to say Macklemore's plight represents a wider battle between social classes.
FORMULA ONE DRIVER LEWIS HAMILTON TELLS MACKLEMORE HE IS ‘STANDING’ IN SOLIDARITY WITH HIM ON PALESTINE

"Oligarchs and billionaires could just as easily prevent people from speaking out about AI, workers’ rights, or any issue they don’t like. That is what makes this a dangerous precedent. This moment is a test of how far the very powerful can go in censoring speech," Ocasio-Cortez said.

"And that’s why it’s important that we speak out about it. That we make clear that this is an abuse of power. And that we keep the focus on Robert Kraft and the way he’s using his influence to try to control what can and cannot be talked about in America."
MACKLEMORE DONATES $1M TO PALESTINIAN AID ORGANIZATIONS AFTER ED SHEERAN TOUR FALLOUT

The memo ended with the progressive congresswoman pledging to protect free speech and fight billionaires "who want to silence any form of dissent or peaceful protest," followed by the call, "Will you chip in $5 or any amount you can afford to power this movement for a better future?"
New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft speaks to the crowd during a Patriots NFL football Send Off rally in Foxborough, Mass., for Super Bowl LX on Feb. 1, 2026. (Steven Senne/AP Photo)

Macklemore, who was made famous for his song "Thrift Shop" in 2012, said "Free Palestine" during a Sept. 4 show in New Jersey while opening for Sheeran's tour. He then performed a song inspired by the Columbia University anti-Israel protests, according to Forbes, then declared, "The people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them. I say: Free Palestine. I say: Free Lebanon. Free Cuba to the Congo to Sudan to Iran."
ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO ‘BUILD A BRIDGE’ OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO

Kraft, who owns the New England Patriots and their home turf Gillette Stadium, then threatened to cancel Sheeran's show there, Macklemore later wrote publicly. Kraft also warned that other stadium owners would follow suit.

And despite being told to stop, Macklemore said "Free Palestine" during the following night's show but clarified to Jews in the audience that his comments were aimed at Israel, not the religion as a whole.
ED SHEERAN FACES GROWING BACKLASH AS RADIO STATION BANS SONGS, PROTEST GROUPS RESPOND TO MACKLEMORE'S REMOVAL
It did not stop the backlash by pro-Israel groups and fellow musical artists, however, culminating in Macklemore being dropped from Sheeran's tour.

Kraft later told NBC News that his boycott was about a broader pattern of public discourse that he saw as harmful to the Jewish people. He told the outlet, "I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same — peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate."
The pro-Israel billionaire also pledged $2 million toward helping Palestinians amid the fallout.
Ed Sheeran and Macklemore attend the 2013 MTV Video Music Awards at Barclays Center in Brooklyn on Aug. 25, 2013. (Kevin Mazur/WireImage)

Kraft also has close ties to Trump, despite a falling out over the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot. He donated money to Trump's first inauguration and was seen next to Trump in the Kennedy Center's presidential box earlier this year for a screening of the first lady's film, "Melania."

Kraft's wife, Dana Blumberg, is also a member of the Kennedy Center Board of Trustees.

title: Spanberger sparks outrage after sneakily ending Youngkin-era women's sports protections
summary: Abigail Spanberger's administration quietly ended Glenn Youngkin's rulemaking process to protect girls sports along sex-based lines in Virginia.
story: The Supreme Court upholds state bans on biological males in girls' sports. FOX Business' Lydia Hu explains Justice Kavanaugh's opinion on biological differences protecting women's sports opportunities like scholarships.

Critics, including parents of athletes, expressed outrage Friday after Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger's administration quietly shut down a rulemaking process that would have required school sports to be divided by sex.
The move to end protections for scholastic sports based on sex is the latest development in the debate over whether biological males who identify as transgender should compete in girls' sports.

"My jaw dropped when I saw the news," former Del. Kim Taylor, R-Petersburg, told Fox News Digital on Friday. "As a mom of a daughter, I’m furious that protecting the privacy, safety, and opportunities of Virginia’s girls has somehow become controversial."

"Governor Spanberger had a chance to stand up for women and girls, and instead she turned her back. Our daughters should never be asked to sacrifice their privacy or a fair playing field for someone else’s political agenda."
VIRGINIA GOVERNOR ABIGAIL SPANBERGER QUIETLY ROLLS BACK YOUNGKIN'S PLANS TO PROTECT GIRLS' SPORTS

Split image shows Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger, left, and former Gov. Glenn Youngkin, right. Youngkin has criticized Spanberger for her decision not to revoke her endorsement of Democratic candidate Jay Jones. (Vitalii Nosach/Getty Images; John Lamparski/Getty Images)
Taylor focused on maternal and children’s issues during her time in Richmond and was the target of an assassination threat during her unsuccessful re-election bid last year.
Del. Wren Williams, R-Stuart, called the move "classic Spanberger."
"Say one thing, do another, don’t tell anyone, and ignore them if they ask about it," he told Fox News Digital.
Former Ball State basketball player and Indiana state Rep. Michelle Davis added that Spanberger appears to be "taking Virginia backwards."
WHAT'S NEXT IN THE BATTLE TO 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' AFTER SCOTUS RULING — AND THE HIDDEN DAMAGE DRIVING IT
Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger speaks with reporters during an April 18, 2026, event. (Graeme Sloan/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
"Women’s sports exist for women, and protecting a fair playing field shouldn’t be controversial," said Davis, R-Whiteland.
"Democrats talk constantly about empowering women, yet we continue to see Democratic leaders roll back protections for female athletes. Virginia’s girls deserve better."
Fox News Digital reached out to Spanberger and a representative for Youngkin for comment.

Former Gov. Glenn Youngkin started the process of barring biological males from girls' scholastic sports, but the process, which was expected to take years, was ended by his successor, according to the Richmond Times-Dispatch.
"[We] did not proceed with the proposed regulation," Virginia Health Commissioner Cameron Webb told the Richmond Times-Dispatch of his agency and the governor’s office.

The rule, supported by the separate Virginia Board of Health during the Youngkin era, would have prevented "biological males from participating in organized female-only athletic teams and competitions in Virginia, and to prevent biological males from using designated female spaces where females are likely to be in any state of undress."
HOUSE DEMS HAND GOP A WIN ON TRANS SPORTS AS PARTY UNITY CRACKS
The decision was made in late July but did not surface until this week. Spanberger did not issue a press release or announcement on it in the interim.
Meanwhile, the Youngkin-appointed chairwoman of the State Board of Health told the Times-Dispatch she had no idea the process was ending.

"Our hearts go out to everybody involved, the athletes on all sides of it," Dr. Melissa Nelson told the paper.

Williams added that the case shows "Democrats continue to fall all over themselves to openly discriminate against our female athletes," as several states continue debating whether to separate transgender students in athletics.

title: 3 VPN settings to check before your next trip
summary: Your VPN may quietly drop protection when switching between airport Wi-Fi and hotel Wi-Fi. Key settings like auto-connect and kill switch help.
story: Travel expert Lee Abbamonte discusses the risks posed by fraudulent wireless connections on commercial flights and what passengers should check before accessing the internet in the air.

Has this happened to you? You're at the airport, connected to the terminal Wi-Fi, VPN running and feeling good about your security. You board, put your phone in airplane mode, land a few hours later and switch airplane mode off. Your phone finds the hotel Wi-Fi. You open your email and start scrolling.

What you probably didn't notice is the moment in between. For a few seconds, your phone may have been reconnecting while your VPN was still catching up. During that brief window, some traffic could have left your device without VPN protection.

Most websites today use HTTPS encryption, so losing your VPN for a few seconds does not mean everything you do suddenly becomes visible. Still, a VPN adds another layer of privacy, particularly when you are connecting to airport, hotel and coffee shop networks you do not control. Here's how you can reduce those connection gaps while traveling.

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

HOW TO STREAM SAFELY WHILE TRAVELING OUTSIDE THE US
Using auto-connect and a kill switch can help keep your VPN protection in place when you move between hotel, airport and other travel networks. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
Why switching networks can interrupt your VPN

A VPN works by building an encrypted tunnel between your device and the internet. While that tunnel is active, your connection to the VPN server is encrypted. However, the VPN relies on an internet connection. When your phone drops one network and connects to another, the VPN may need to re-establish that tunnel.

Usually, this happens so quickly that you barely notice. However, a weak signal, slow hotel login page or network that takes a few extra seconds to connect can create a brief period when your device has internet access before the VPN reconnects.

This can happen during completely ordinary activities. You might switch from cellular data to airport Wi-Fi after landing. Later, your phone may move from the airport network to your hotel's Wi-Fi. The same thing can happen when your phone wakes from sleep in a new location or reconnects after losing cellular service. For travelers who move between networks frequently, those transitions are worth paying attention to.
What happens when your VPN is disconnected

When your VPN is disconnected, websites and online services can generally see the public IP address assigned by your internet provider or Wi-Fi network instead of the VPN server's IP address. That address can reveal information such as your approximate location and internet provider.

A VPN also helps prevent the operator of a Wi-Fi network from easily seeing details about the internet services your device is contacting. Most trusted websites and apps already encrypt sensitive traffic using HTTPS or other encryption. That greatly reduces what someone monitoring a public Wi-Fi connection can see.

However, risks remain if you connect to a fake or compromised Wi-Fi network. Someone controlling the network may try to direct you to a fraudulent login page, interfere with your connection or exploit websites and apps that are not properly encrypted.

A VPN adds another layer of protection by encrypting traffic between your device and the VPN server and masking your normal public IP address. A kill switch can provide an additional safeguard by preventing internet traffic from leaving your device if the VPN unexpectedly disconnects.
1) Turn on VPN auto-connect
The first setting to check is auto-connect. Most VPN apps offer some form of automatic connection. Without it, your VPN may stay disconnected until you remember to open the app and turn it back on.

After a long flight, a trip through baggage claim and the rush to reach your hotel, that can be easy to forget. With auto-connect enabled, your VPN can attempt to restore its connection automatically when your device gets back online or joins a new network. Check your VPN app before traveling and make sure its automatic connection options are configured the way you want them.
THE TRICK TO SMOOTHER STREAMING AT HOME AND ON THE ROAD
Travelers using hotel or public Wi-Fi may benefit from a VPN's added privacy, though it cannot overcome an overloaded network. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images)
2) Enable your VPN kill switch

The second setting to check is the kill switch. A VPN kill switch is designed to block internet traffic if your VPN unexpectedly disconnects. That helps prevent your device from simply falling back to an unprotected connection while the VPN is trying to reconnect.

However, kill switches do not all work exactly the same way. Some protect you only when the VPN connection unexpectedly drops. Others can be configured to block internet access whenever the VPN is not connected.
Android users may also have system-level options such as Always-on VPN and Block connections without VPN, depending on their device and VPN provider.

Some reputable VPN services also offer additional kill switch options on supported platforms. Keep in mind that stronger settings that block all traffic outside the VPN can interfere with local network features or internet access when the VPN is intentionally turned off. The important thing is to understand how your VPN's kill switch works before you depend on it while traveling.

There is one situation that can complicate things: the captive portal. That's the webpage airports, hotels and other public Wi-Fi networks sometimes require you to open before they grant internet access. You may need to accept terms, enter a room number or complete another login step.
Because your device does not yet have normal internet access, the VPN may not be able to connect until you finish that process. Strict kill switch settings can occasionally make this more difficult.

If you encounter a Wi-Fi login page, complete the network's sign-in process and then confirm that your VPN is connected before opening email, financial accounts or other sensitive services. Also make sure you are joining the correct Wi-Fi network. If you are uncertain, ask an airport employee, hotel staff member or business employee for the official network name.
3) Choose a VPN protocol that reconnects quickly

Settings help, but reconnection speed also depends on the underlying technology your VPN uses. This is known as the VPN protocol. Different VPN protocols handle network changes in different ways. Some are particularly well suited to phones and laptops that frequently move between Wi-Fi and cellular connections. For the best VPN software, see my expert review of the best VPNs for browsing the web privately on your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
WHY YOUR VPN KEEPS GETTING BLOCKED AND THE SIMPLE FIX
Using an always-on VPN or your phone’s hotspot can help protect sensitive work accounts while traveling. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
A quick VPN checklist for travelers
Before your next trip, take a minute to check your VPN:

Turn on auto-connect so the VPN can attempt to reconnect when your device joins a new network.Enable the kill switch and understand exactly what it blocks when the VPN disconnects.Choose a VPN protocol designed for fast reconnection, or use your VPN provider's recommended automatic setting.Verify the official Wi-Fi network name before joining public Wi-Fi.Complete any required airport or hotel Wi-Fi login page, then confirm your VPN is connected before accessing sensitive accounts.
Turn on auto-connect so the VPN can attempt to reconnect when your device joins a new network.
Enable the kill switch and understand exactly what it blocks when the VPN disconnects.
Choose a VPN protocol designed for fast reconnection, or use your VPN provider's recommended automatic setting.
Verify the official Wi-Fi network name before joining public Wi-Fi.
Complete any required airport or hotel Wi-Fi login page, then confirm your VPN is connected before accessing sensitive accounts.

You should also test your setup before leaving home. Connect to your VPN, turn Wi-Fi off and switch to cellular data. Then turn Wi-Fi back on and watch what your VPN does. Does it reconnect automatically? Does the kill switch block traffic while the VPN is disconnected? How long does the connection take to return? A quick test can help you catch a setting that needs attention before you are relying on your VPN in an airport or hotel.
Kurt's key takeaways

Most websites already use HTTPS encryption, so a brief VPN interruption does not leave all of your online activity exposed. Still, a VPN provides another valuable layer of privacy when you are using networks you do not control. The biggest issue for travelers is making sure the VPN actually reconnects when a phone or laptop moves between cellular service, airport Wi-Fi, hotel Wi-Fi and other networks. Turn on auto-connect, understand how your kill switch works and use a protocol that handles network changes efficiently. A few minutes spent checking your settings before a trip can help keep your VPN connection more consistent while you are on the move.

title: His home changed hands for $5. Could it happen to your family?
summary: A South Carolina caregiver allegedly gained power of attorney over a 75-year-old with Parkinson's, then transferred his home via quitclaim deed for $5.
story: A woman caught up in a two-year LinkedIn romance scam that used a real man's identity shares the tactics a scammer used to build trust and trick her into sending nearly $1 million.

A deed can change hands without a burglar breaking a window or a scammer hacking a computer. Sometimes the first warning signs are sitting inside county records, bank accounts and email inboxes, waiting for someone to notice.

A disturbing case out of South Carolina shows why families may want to put a few digital safeguards in place now. According to a local report, a daughter says her 75-year-old father, who had Parkinson's disease and a brain injury, became increasingly isolated after a caregiver entered his life.

Within weeks, the caregiver was named as his power of attorney. A quitclaim deed later transferred his Conway home to her for $5. His daughter also says bank statements show money moving from his account to the caregiver, including after his death. Conway police said they were investigating.

The allegations have not been proven in court. Still, the case raises a question every family with an aging or vulnerable loved one should consider: Would you know if someone changed a deed, moved money or took control of an important account? Technology cannot prevent every form of financial exploitation. However, the right alerts can create an early-warning system that makes major changes much harder to hide.

MAN ACCUSED OF STEALING MORE THAN $735K AS POWER OF ATTORNEY TO PURCHASE PROPERTY, ONLYFANS AND LIFE COACHING

Families can use property, bank and account alerts to spot warning signs of possible financial exploitation involving an aging or vulnerable loved one. (Photo by: Andia/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)
Why this case goes beyond home-title theft

Home-title theft usually involves a criminal forging documents, impersonating an owner or recording a fraudulent deed. The allegations in this case raise a different concern. The daughter alleges that her father was vulnerable and may not have understood what he signed after the caregiver obtained power of attorney.

A forged deed can involve identity theft. When someone signs a document after alleged manipulation or coercion or when questions arise about whether that person understood what they were signing, the legal issues can involve undue influence, elder financial exploitation or abuse of legal authority.

Technology cannot determine what happened between two people. What it can do is flag events that deserve a closer look, including a new deed filing, an ownership change, a new lender, an unusual bank transfer or a change to an account's contact information.

The FBI has warned that quitclaim deed fraud can involve forged documents as well as relatives or close associates persuading older adults to transfer property for someone else's financial gain. The agency recommends monitoring property records and enrolling in county title alerts where available.
5 digital safeguards that can help protect your family

You do not need expensive technology to start watching for suspicious changes. Some of the strongest safeguards are free alerts already offered by county governments, banks and financial institutions. The key is setting them up before something happens and making sure the warnings reach someone who can act. Here are five digital safeguards worth putting in place.
DIY IDENTITY PROTECTION VS PAID SERVICES: WHAT WORKS IN 2026
A South Carolina case involving a disputed $5 home transfer highlights how property and financial changes can go unnoticed without alerts. (Photo by: Andia/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Start with the government office that records deeds in the county where the property is located. Depending on the state, it may be called the county recorder, recorder of deeds, register of deeds or clerk's office. Many of these offices offer a free notification service. Look for names such as Property Fraud Alert, Recording Notification Service, Fraud Guard or Land Record Alert. Horry County, where the South Carolina property is located, now offers a free Recording Notification Service. It monitors the county's registry for new filings associated with a registered name and sends an alert when it finds one.
To find a service in your area:

Search for your county's name plus property fraud alert or recording notification service.Open only the official county or local government website. Check the web address carefully before entering personal information.Register the owner's full legal name and any other name used on property records.Add a spouse's name and the name of a trust or business if the county allows it.Confirm the registration through the email the county sends you.
Search for your county's name plus property fraud alert or recording notification service.
Open only the official county or local government website. Check the web address carefully before entering personal information.
Register the owner's full legal name and any other name used on property records.
Add a spouse's name and the name of a trust or business if the county allows it.
Confirm the registration through the email the county sends you.
Keep in mind that an alert does not stop a document from being recorded. Instead, it tells you something was filed so you can investigate quickly.

The reported deed transfer was only one warning sign in this case. The daughter also alleges that money moved from her father's bank account. Most banks and credit card issuers let you create alerts through their apps or websites. You will usually find them under Settings , Security , Alerts or Notifications .

Turn on alerts for withdrawals and outgoing transfers, new external accounts or payees, large purchases, checks clearing, low balances, password resets, new device logins and changes to contact information. Also consider setting transaction alerts at a relatively low dollar amount. Scammers sometimes begin with smaller transactions before trying to move more money.

Whenever possible, use more than one notification method, such as push notifications, text messages and email. Then review those settings every few months. A new phone, changed email address or bank app update can sometimes interrupt notifications.

A trusted contact gives a financial institution another person to reach if it sees signs of exploitation or cannot contact the account holder. That person does not automatically become a joint owner and does not receive power of attorney simply because they were named as a trusted contact.

For brokerage accounts, FINRA rules require firms to make a reasonable effort to obtain a trusted contact. The contact may be asked about the account holder's health, current contact information or possible financial exploitation. Being named a trusted contact does not give someone permission to trade, withdraw money or view account balances.

Some banks and credit unions offer similar protections voluntarily. Ask the fraud department or elder financial exploitation team whether it provides trusted contacts, read-only account access, extra confirmation for large transfers or additional review when money goes to a new recipient. Choose the person carefully.

If a daily caregiver already has access to finances, consider using a different relative, attorney or accountant as the trusted contact. That creates another set of eyes without handing over control of the account. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau says trusted contacts can help financial institutions respond to possible elder financial exploitation while allowing the account holder to retain control.

Alerts only help when they reach the right person. If someone else controls the account holder's phone or email, they may be able to delete warnings, change contact information or reset passwords before a family member notices. Start with the email account connected to banking, investment and property notifications.

Use a password manager to create and store a strong, unique password. Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA). Review recovery phone numbers and email addresses. Check for unfamiliar forwarding rules and signed-in devices. Store backup codes somewhere secure that the person legally authorized to use the account can reach. Then protect the mobile carrier account too.

Add an account PIN and enable any protection the carrier offers against unauthorized number transfers. Someone who takes over a phone number may be able to intercept security codes and account alerts. Also, avoid sharing one online banking password among several relatives or caregivers. Instead, ask the financial institution about separate authorized access, a view-only login or another supported arrangement. Separate logins make it much easier to see who accessed or changed an account.

County and bank alerts provide a strong foundation, but they live in different places. A broader identity theft protection service can bring more warning signs together and provide help if identity theft becomes complicated.

Some services offer home title monitoring that looks for changes involving property ownership, new lenders, financing and notices of default. Depending on the provider and plan, you may also get alerts for suspicious activity involving checking, savings, credit, retirement and investment accounts.

In a situation like the South Carolina case, a recorded ownership change could potentially trigger an alert. Suspicious financial activity may also surface when affected accounts are connected and the activity meets the service's monitoring criteria.

Some identity theft protection plans also provide access to restoration specialists who can help if identity theft or home-title fraud occurs. However, monitoring has limits. Home title monitoring relies on county records, and newly recorded documents can sometimes take time to appear in monitoring systems. These services cannot block a deed, determine whether someone understood a document or prevent someone from misusing power of attorney.

Coverage, reimbursement and insurance benefits vary by provider and plan and may come with terms, conditions and exclusions. A dispute involving alleged coercion or a deed that someone actually signed may also be handled differently from a case involving forged identity theft.
Think of monitoring as an alarm, not a lock. It can warn you that something changed so you can investigate. It cannot make the change impossible.

Why a credit freeze will not stop a deed transfer

A credit freeze remains one of the best tools for making it harder for criminals to open new credit accounts in someone's name. However, freezing your credit does not lock a property title. It also cannot stop activity inside an existing bank account or prevent someone from filing a deed. Use a credit freeze alongside property alerts, financial monitoring and secure account logins.
Warning signs families should watch for

Digital alerts can flag transactions and account changes, but families should also pay attention to changes in behavior and access. Take a closer look if an older or vulnerable person suddenly stops communicating with family, becomes unusually isolated or has a new caregiver or acquaintance speaking for them.

Other warning signs include unexplained financial or legal decisions, missing bank statements or tax bills, unfamiliar people appearing on accounts, sudden password or address changes and property documents signed for little or no apparent value. One change may have a perfectly reasonable explanation. Several changes appearing around the same time deserve attention.
What to do if you suspect exploitation
If something feels wrong, move quickly while preserving records that could help investigators understand what happened.

Call 911 if the person faces immediate danger. Otherwise, contact local police or the sheriff's non-emergency line.Report suspected exploitation to Adult Protective Services. The national Eldercare Locator can connect you with the correct local agency at eldercare.acl.gov or 800-677-1116 .Contact the bank, brokerage and credit card companies. Ask for the fraud department or elder financial exploitation team. Report suspicious transfers and ask the institution to preserve relevant records.Contact the county recorder. Obtain copies of the deed and related filings. Ask about available notification and fraud-response resources.Save documentation. Keep account alerts, bank statements, emails, text messages, voicemails, property filings and a written timeline.Speak with an elder-law or real estate attorney. A lawyer can evaluate power-of-attorney documents, questions about capacity and possible options for challenging a transfer. Laws and deadlines vary by state.

The CFPB says family members do not need every detail before reporting suspected elder financial abuse. Investigators can determine what happened.
THE SCAM TEXT TEST: SPOT DANGER BEFORE YOU TAP
County property notifications, bank alerts and trusted contacts can give families an earlier warning when significant financial changes occur. (Photo by Ute Grabowsky/Photothek via Getty Images)
Kurt's key takeaways

The most unsettling part of this case goes beyond a home allegedly changing hands for $5. It is how many major changes may have happened before the family knew what was going on. No app can tell you whether a vulnerable loved one is being manipulated. A title-monitoring service also cannot replace regular conversations, careful legal planning and people you trust. Technology can still give families an important advantage: an earlier warning. Set up county property alerts. Turn on detailed financial notifications. Add a trusted contact. Secure the phone and email accounts receiving those alerts. Then consider broader monitoring if your family wants another layer of visibility across property, identity and financial accounts. The sooner you know something changed, the sooner you can start asking questions and take action.

title: Flying taxis are taking off in Texas. Is your city next?
summary: Joby Aviation flew its eVTOL air taxi into DFW Airport's busy airspace as Texas launches Project Nexus, a three-year advanced air mobility program.
story: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy addresses rising drone incidents near airports, detailing a recent JetBlue collision and discussing investigations. He unveils new FAA technology for civilian supersonic flights, aiming to reduce travel times. Duffy also highlights innovations in autonomous vehicles and drone deliveries, emphasizing balancing safety with advancing transportation technology across the country.

If you have ever watched your arrival time creep later while sitting in traffic, flying over it sounds pretty appealing. Texas is now testing what that could look like. Earlier this month, the Texas Department of Transportation launched the first phase of Project Nexus, a three-year program focused on preparing next-generation aircraft for use in Texas skies.

The Sept. 10 kickoff at Perot Field Fort Worth Alliance Airport included demonstrations from BETA Technologies and Joby Aviation. Joby brought its electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, better known as an eVTOL. No passengers climbed aboard the initial Project Nexus flights. Instead, Texas is starting to learn how air taxis could eventually fit into the way people get around.

Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.
