title: Woman loses nearly $1M in LinkedIn romance scam
summary: A LinkedIn romance scam cost Gaby close to $1 million after a scammer returned her first payment to build trust, then escalated requests over two years.
story: A woman caught up in a two-year LinkedIn romance scam that used a real man's identity shares the tactics a scammer used to build trust and trick her into sending nearly $1 million.

A message from a stranger on LinkedIn probably would not set off alarms for most of us. Especially when that person appears connected to someone you already know. That is how Gaby's story began. Gaby recently joined me on "The CyberGuy Report Podcast" at cyberguy.com/podcast/ to explain how an online relationship that began in 2019 grew into a devastating romance scam. Over roughly two years, she says she sent close to $1 million to a man she never met. The person Gaby thought she had fallen for was using the photos and likeness of a real man named Brian Haugen, who also joined us to explain what it has been like watching scammers use his photos to target women around the world.

Gaby described how quickly the attention pulled her in. "The words that he spoke, it was like a drug," she told me. The compliments kept coming, the relationship grew more intense and eventually the requests for money began. Her experience is also part of "Hey Beautiful: Anatomy of a Romance Scam," the three-part Hulu docuseries about women who believed they were communicating with the same man.
AI IS CHANGING MODERN DATING, BUT EXPERTS WARN IT'S MAKING PEOPLE 'RELATIONALLY STUPID'
Scammers used photos of Brian Haugen, left, to build trust, fabricate emergencies and convince Gaby, right, to send nearly $1 million. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)

What makes Gaby's story so revealing is how slowly the deception took hold. The scammer built trust over time, returned some of the money she initially sent and always seemed to have another explanation when they could not meet. By the time the biggest requests arrived, the relationship already felt very real.

You’ll learn how to organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare questions for your next doctor’s visit. No technical experience is needed.
Register for free now at CyberGuyLive.com
A LinkedIn message felt safer than a dating app

Gaby says the first contact came through LinkedIn in March 2019. That detail helped lower her guard. She primarily used LinkedIn to connect with business contacts. More importantly, the stranger appeared connected to one of her former colleagues. "So I thought, oh yes, she knows him. Okay. That's fine. So let's contact," Gaby recalled.

That small connection gave the profile credibility it had not actually earned. Scammers can take advantage of exactly that type of information. The FTC says criminals may study what people post on social media and use those details to shape a more convincing approach. The FBI also advises people to be careful about what they make public online because romance scammers can use that information when targeting potential victims. Gaby's experience shows why a mutual connection on a social platform should never replace independent verification.
The money requests started small

The fake Brian did not open the relationship by demanding hundreds of thousands of dollars. Gaby says they spent weeks talking about his supposed business activities. He claimed he worked in the gemstone trade and told her he had traveled to Vietnam. Then came a problem. He said his bank account had been blocked. Gaby remembers sending about $10,000 at first. Then something happened that dramatically changed how she viewed him. He gave the money back. That repayment helped convince Gaby that she was dealing with someone she could trust. As she explained, "I started to trust him because he sent me back money."

That move is especially revealing. If someone takes your first payment and disappears, you know you have a problem. Returning money can create the opposite reaction. It makes the next request feel less risky because you have already seen what appears to be proof that the person keeps a promise. The requests continued. Gaby recalls amounts of $10,000, $20,000 and $40,000 adding up over time. Eventually, she says the man told her he needed about $200,000 to deal with taxes and customs fees. He promised he would repay her once the supposed financial roadblock disappeared.
Scammers are using AI to improve on old tactics, such as romance fraud. (Frank Brennan/iStock/Getty Images)
Every attempt to meet came with an excuse

At some point, an online relationship has to enter the real world. Gaby thought about traveling to Vietnam to see him. The man pushed back. According to Gaby, he said he was under stress and did not want her seeing him when he did not look his best.

They continued talking about meeting. Then the COVID pandemic made international travel far more difficult. I asked Gaby whether the fake Brian always seemed to come up with another reason they could not see each other. She agreed that he did. The FBI identifies that pattern as a major romance scam warning sign. Scammers may promise to meet and then repeatedly cancel because of an emergency or another obstacle. The agency advises people to become suspicious when months pass without an in-person meeting.
Then a medical emergency raised the stakes

Eventually, the story shifted from business trouble to a supposed health crisis. Gaby says the man claimed he needed surgery. She recalled how quickly the request became tied to the relationship itself: "Suddenly he told me he needs surgery to prove my love. I sent 500,000."

That is a staggering amount of money. Yet by this point, Gaby was dealing with someone she had communicated with for a long time. He had become part of her daily life. He had also returned money before. The financial emergency came after the emotional groundwork. Federal authorities repeatedly warn about that progression. Romance scammers can spend weeks or months building trust before introducing an emergency and asking for money. The FBI warns consumers never to send money to someone they have only communicated with online or by phone.
FLORIDA MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY LURED WOMEN WITH DATING APP COULD HAVE MORE VICTIMS: AUTHORITIES
The real Brian had no idea his face was being used

The person in the photographs was real. The identity behind the messages was another story. Brian Haugen joined me in the studio to explain what had happened to his images. "They steal my photo off of a social media account," Brian said. He explained that scammers then used those photos on accounts with different names to approach women and ask for money. That makes Brian another victim of the scheme.

He also described how far the identity abuse had spread. Brian said he had become nervous about traveling because "there's multiple passports that have my photo on it in people's different names." Imagine seeing your face attached to conversations you never had with people you have never met. The FBI says romance scammers frequently use photographs stolen from someone else rather than images of themselves.
Brian Haugen explains how scammers stole his photos and reused them on fake profiles to target women. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)
What Hey Beautiful reveals about romance scams

Brian's experience became part of Hey Beautiful: Anatomy of a Romance Scam. The Hulu docuseries follows women from around the world who fall for an online boyfriend who turns out to be someone else. The series has three episodes and originally debuted in 2025. What makes the story useful for anyone watching is the playbook behind the deception. Romance fraud can rely on stolen identities, information collected online and carefully timed emotional manipulation. Some criminal operations also involve multiple people rather than a single scammer working alone.

Brian described the people who used his identity as "Yahoo boys," a term often associated with certain online fraud groups. That should not be taken to mean that every romance scam comes from one group or one country. Romance fraud can originate in many places and take many forms. The consumer lesson remains the same: do not assume you know who is behind an online profile simply because the pictures look convincing or the person's story feels personal.
Romance scams thrive on social media

Social platforms have become a major starting point for these schemes. According to FTC data released in April 2026, nearly 60% of people who reported losing money to a romance scam in 2025 said it started on social media. Reported losses from romance scams that began on social media reached about $298 million during the year. That makes sense when you consider how much information many of us put online. A scammer may see your photographs or learn about your job. Posts may reveal that you recently traveled, moved or went through a major change in your life.

The FTC says scammers can use information from profiles to tailor their approach before inventing a crisis that requires money. For another example of how personal information can give criminals an opening, see our CyberGuy report on what a scammer can learn by Googling your name.
The email request that finally exposed the lie

Gaby eventually began questioning the person she had been talking to. She had followed the real Brian Haugen and booked an online session connected to him. That gave her a chance to communicate with the actual man whose face appeared in the photos. The fake Brian tried to explain away what she had discovered, but Gaby wanted stronger proof. She asked him to send her a message from the same email account connected with the legitimate Zoom meeting invitation. He stalled.

Gaby says one week passed, then another. She kept pushing for the verification. Finally, she told him, "Otherwise I don't believe you anymore." He never produced the email she requested. For Gaby, that was the moment the deception finally fell apart. Her experience also offers an important lesson. When you have doubts about someone's identity, find an independent way to check their story. Do not let the person you suspect control all the evidence.
Tips to protect yourself from a romance scam
Gaby's story shows how difficult these scams can be to recognize once trust takes hold. These steps can help you spot warning signs earlier and make it harder for a scammer to manipulate you.

Your social media profile can give a stranger plenty of material to work with. Review who can see your posts and photographs. Consider hiding your friends list and avoid publicly sharing details about your routine or upcoming travel.

The FTC recommends limiting who can see your social media posts and contacts so scammers have less information they can use to approach you. People-search websites and data brokers can expose additional information, including old addresses and contact details. You can remove information from many of those sites yourself. If you would rather automate some of that work, a personal data removal service can submit removal requests and continue checking participating sites. Get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web: Cyberguy.com.
SHE DIDN’T EXIST, BUT THE MONEY DID: A REAL INFLUENCER SOUNDS THE ALARM ON AI DECEPTION
A woman says she lost nearly $1 million after a LinkedIn connection turned into a yearslong romance scam using the stolen identity of a real man. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)

A familiar photograph or mutual connection does not prove an account belongs to the person it claims to represent. Look at how long the account has existed and review its activity. Check whether another profile uses the same name or photographs. If the person claims to know one of your friends or colleagues, contact that person separately and ask about the connection. Also run a reverse image search on the profile picture. The FBI recommends this when you suspect romance fraud. If the image appears under another person's name, take that warning seriously. Keep in mind that a clean search does not guarantee the person is legitimate. A scammer may use a newly stolen photograph or an AI-generated image that has never appeared online before.

A video call can still be useful. Someone who repeatedly refuses to appear on camera should raise your suspicions. However, seeing a face on your screen no longer proves who is really behind an account. The FBI warns that scammers can use deepfake technology or involve other people in video conversations. Compare what the person tells you with information you find independently. Look for an online history that makes sense and never send money, because a video call convinced you the person must be real.

Be cautious when someone you recently met online becomes intensely romantic very quickly. The FBI advises people to go slowly and ask plenty of questions. It also helps to tell someone you trust about the relationship, especially before sending money. A friend or family member may notice contradictions that are much harder to see when you are emotionally involved.

A sudden request could involve surgery, a frozen bank account or another supposed emergency. Whatever the story, stop before sending money to someone you have never met. Also refuse any request to receive money in your account and forward it somewhere else. The FBI warns that romance scam victims can become unwitting money mules when scammers convince them to move stolen funds.

Money may not be the only thing a romance scammer wants. They may also ask for account credentials, copies of identification or other sensitive information that can lead to identity theft. Even with good security habits, your Social Security number, financial information or other personal data may already be exposed without you knowing it. Consider using an identity theft protection service that monitors for suspicious activity tied to your personal information and alerts you when something needs your attention. Depending on the service and plan, protection may also include credit monitoring, financial account alerts and help recovering from identity theft. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com.
You should also review your credit reports regularly, watch your bank and credit card accounts for unfamiliar activity and change passwords immediately if you believe an account has been compromised.
Gaby recounts how an online relationship that began on LinkedIn eventually cost her close to $1 million. (Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson)

If you discover a scam, do not immediately delete the conversation. Save messages, emails, screenshots and payment records. Keep links to the scammer's profiles as well. If you already sent money, contact your bank or payment provider immediately and report the fraud. The FTC says acting quickly may improve your chances of stopping or reversing certain transactions. You should also report the scam to the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center and the FTC.

A previous scam victim can become a target all over again. The FTC warned in August 2026 that recovery scammers may contact people who have already lost money and promise to get it back. They may claim to represent a government agency, law firm or recovery service. Then they demand an upfront fee or ask for financial information. Do not pay someone who unexpectedly contacts you and promises to recover money you lost to a scam.
Kurt's key takeaways

What stays with me about Gaby's story is how normal the beginning sounded. She was on LinkedIn. The profile seemed to share a professional connection with her. He talked about business. Later, he borrowed money and actually returned it. Each interaction gave the next one more credibility. As I said during our conversation, "Here's what I know about romance scams. They are highly involved. They take weeks if not months of time to evolve." That time gives scammers a chance to become part of someone's routine before the biggest financial request ever arrives. It is also why we need to watch out for people we care about. During the podcast, I pointed to another warning sign: "If any of the people that you love and your family or really good friends suddenly go quiet and claim that they're in love with someone from far away, or that they're dating a celebrity, it happens. Really. It's time for a reality check." That reality check does not have to start with an accusation. Ask questions. Listen to the story. Find out whether the person has actually met their new partner and whether money has entered the relationship. Sometimes an outside voice can spot the pattern before another transfer goes through. Hear Gaby's full story and my conversation with the real Brian Haugen on "The CyberGuy Report Podcast" at cyberguy.com/podcast/.

title: iOS 27 is here: 10 iPhone features you’ll want to try now
summary: Safari's Notify Me can monitor websites for price changes and restocks, while new AI photo tools let you reframe and extend shots in iOS 27.
story: Apple's newly unveiled foldable iPhone Duo sparks significant consumer interest despite a hefty $1,999 starting price tag. On 'Varney & Co.', Taylor Riggs explains the premium device's unique dual-screen capability and ultra-thin design. Host Stuart Varney admits he plans to purchase the high-end smartphone, which can cost up to $3,000 for the two-terabyte storage model.
Your iPhone is getting a major update. Apple released iOS 27 to the public on Monday, Sept. 14, bringing a wave of new features along with the long-awaited Siri AI beta.

However, there is much more happening under the hood. Safari can now watch websites for changes. The Photos app gets powerful new editing tools. Apple also says it has made iOS faster across compatible iPhones.

Some of these changes could save you from digging through apps or hunting for information yourself. Others give you more control over how your iPhone looks and works. Here are the iOS 27 features I think are worth trying first, along with how to find them.
NEW! Join our upcoming CyberGuy LIVE class: Get Better healthcare With AI

In this free live online class, Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will show you five practical ways AI can help you take a more active role in your healthcare. You’ll learn how to organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare questions for your next doctor’s visit. No technical experience is needed.
Register for free now at CyberGuyLive.com.
8 BIGGEST THINGS WE LEARNED FROM APPLE'S 2026 EVENT
Apple’s iOS 27 adds smarter Photos tools, Safari upgrades, stronger privacy controls and the long-awaited Siri AI beta for supported iPhones. (Anna Barclay/Getty Images)
Will your iPhone get iOS 27?

The good news is that Apple kept support fairly broad. iOS 27 works with the iPhone 11 family and newer models. It also supports the second-generation iPhone SE and later. That means plenty of people can upgrade without buying a new phone. However, the biggest AI features have tougher hardware requirements. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI require an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 15 Pro Max, or an iPhone 16 model or later. So, an iPhone 11 can run iOS 27, but it will miss Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features.

Keep in mind that many of the features below, including the new AI photo tools, Safari Notify Me and Call Context, also require an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone. Siri AI is rolling out in beta in English on supported devices. Apple says support for additional languages will follow later. Availability can also vary by region.
iOS 27 should also feel faster

Apple says iOS 27 brings performance improvements across the system. In Apple's testing, apps can launch up to 30% faster, new photos can load in the Photos app up to 70% faster and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% faster. Apple also says iOS 27 improves transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular connections and makes Mail search more relevant. Those are Apple's own figures, so your results will vary depending on your iPhone and how you use it.
How to install iOS 27 on your iPhone
Before installing a major update, I recommend backing up your iPhone. Also, connect to Wi-Fi and make sure you have enough battery life or plug your phone into power.
Then follow these steps:

Open Settings.Tap General.Tap Software Update.When iOS 27 appears, tap Update Now or Update Tonight.Enter your passcode if prompted.Agree to Apple’s terms.Let the update download and install.Your iPhone will restart when the installation finishes.
Open Settings.
Tap General.
Tap Software Update.
When iOS 27 appears, tap Update Now or Update Tonight.
Enter your passcode if prompted.
Agree to Apple’s terms.
Let the update download and install.
Your iPhone will restart when the installation finishes.
If iOS 27 does not appear immediately, check again later. Apple software releases can take some time to appear on every compatible iPhone.
1) Reframe a photo after you take it

Apple Intelligence moves deeper into the Photos app with Spatial Reframing. It lets you change the composition and perspective of a photo after you took it. Apple Intelligence can generate additional parts of the scene when your new framing exposes areas that were outside the original shot.

Open the Photos app.Choose a photo.Tap the three-slider Edit icon at the bottom of the screen.Tap Tools in the bottom-right corner.Tap Reframe.Drag the photo to change the perspective or framing.Zoom as needed.Review the AI-generated result.Tap Done when you like it.
Open the Photos app.
Choose a photo.
Tap the three-slider Edit icon at the bottom of the screen.
Tap Tools in the bottom-right corner.
Tap Reframe.
Drag the photo to change the perspective or framing.
Zoom as needed.
Review the AI-generated result.
Tap Done when you like it.
Because AI may create new portions of the scene, I would zoom in and inspect the result before sharing an edited photo. Generative tools can still produce odd details.
Spatial Reframing in iOS 27 lets you adjust a photo’s composition and perspective after you take it. (Apple)
2) Extend a photo beyond its original edges
Maybe you took a photo too close to your subject. The new Extend tool lets you expand beyond the original edges while Apple Intelligence generates the missing surroundings.

Open Photos and select your photo.Tap the three-slider Edit icon.Tap Tools in the bottom-right corner.Tap Extend.Pinch inward with two fingers or drag the edges of the frame.Tap Extend again.Review the generated result before saving it.
Open Photos and select your photo.
Tap the three-slider Edit icon.
Tap Tools in the bottom-right corner.
Tap Extend.
Pinch inward with two fingers or drag the edges of the frame.
Tap Extend again.
Review the generated result before saving it.
The feature will not work with every photo. Apple also says its intelligent photo-editing tools can be subject to daily usage limits.
3) Clean Up can remove bigger distractions
Apple has also upgraded Clean Up in Photos. The tool can now tackle larger unwanted objects and distractions while using AI to fill in the space left behind.

Open the Photos app.Select the photo you want to edit.Tap the three-slider Edit icon.Tap Tools in the bottom-right corner.Select Clean Up.Tap, brush or circle the object you want to remove.Tap Clean UpReview the result and tap Done when you are satisfied.
Open the Photos app.
Select the photo you want to edit.
Tap the three-slider Edit icon.
Tap Tools in the bottom-right corner.
Select Clean Up.
Tap, brush or circle the object you want to remove.
Tap Clean Up
Review the result and tap Done when you are satisfied.
This could be especially handy for removing a person in the background or another distraction that pulls attention away from the subject.

Apple is also giving Image Playground a major upgrade in iOS 27. You can now generate images in many more styles, including photorealistic ones. You can also start with an existing image and describe how you want Apple Intelligence to change it.

For example, you could ask it to change the setting or adjust the overall look without starting from scratch. As with Apple’s other generative image tools, usage limits may apply. I would also look closely at the results before sharing them, especially when people or detailed objects appear in the scene.
4) Safari can watch a website for you

This may end up being one of my favorite iOS 27 features because it solves a very common frustration. Safari’s new Notify Me feature can monitor a webpage for a change you care about. For example, you could ask Safari to watch for a product coming back in stock. It can also monitor a page for a price change. Instead of reopening the same page over and over, Safari can alert you when something changes.

Open Safari.Visit the webpage you want to monitor.Tap the puzzle piece icon in the search bar.Tap Notify Me.Choose a suggested request or type what you want Safari to watch.Adjust how often Safari should check the page if you want.Tap the blue check mark.Tap Allow to receive notifications.
Open Safari.
Visit the webpage you want to monitor.
Tap the puzzle piece icon in the search bar.
Tap Notify Me.
Choose a suggested request or type what you want Safari to watch.
Adjust how often Safari should check the page if you want.
Tap the blue check mark.
Tap Allow to receive notifications.

You can choose hourly, daily, weekly or monthly checks. However, Notify Me does not yet work on every website. Safari can also automatically organize open tabs by topic, which could help anyone whose browser looks like a digital junk drawer by the end of the week.
APPLE AI SECURITY UPDATE PROVES HACKERS MOVE FAST
5) Your iPhone can surface information while you are on a call
Apple Intelligence is also getting involved when you call businesses. A new feature called Call Context can surface useful information from other apps while you are on a call.

Say you call an airline about a reservation. Call Context can pull up a confirmation code from Mail rather than forcing you to leave the Phone app and search for it while someone waits on the other end.
There is no complicated workflow to learn. When you place a supported business call and Apple Intelligence identifies relevant information, it can surface that information during the call.

Apple says its system determines what could be useful based on who you are calling. It can do that without analyzing the audio from your call. That is the kind of AI feature I want to see more of, because you do not have to change your behavior to benefit from it.
6) Liquid Glass gets a much-needed adjustment

Last year, Apple introduced the transparent Liquid Glass design across iOS. Some people liked the new look. Others found certain screens harder to read. With iOS 27, Apple says it has improved contrast and readability. More importantly, you now have greater control over how transparent the interface appears. Apple added a slider that lets you move the look from ultraclear toward fully tinted.
Open Settings.Tap Appearance.Tap Liquid Glass.Drag the slider left for a clearer, more transparent look or right for a more tinted, opaque look.Stop when the interface looks easiest for you to read.
Open Settings.
Tap Appearance.
Tap Liquid Glass.
Drag the slider left for a clearer, more transparent look or right for a more tinted, opaque look.
Stop when the interface looks easiest for you to read.

The changes appear in real time as you move the slider. The setting applies across iOS, including places such as Control Center, notifications and app overlays. This is a small change, but I like that Apple is giving people a choice rather than assuming one visual treatment works for everyone.
Apple’s newest iPhone software brings meaningful upgrades beyond Siri, with faster performance, smarter apps and practical everyday tools. (Kena Betancur/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
7) Put your favorite Camera controls within easy reach

If you are always digging around for the timer, exposure or another Camera setting, iOS 27 lets you keep the controls you use most right above the camera frame. Apple starts you with Flash and Live Photo there, but you can customize the row with other tools you use regularly.

Open the Camera app.Tap the Camera Controls button. It looks like six small dots inside a circle near the camera controls area.Tap Edit.Tap a tool you want to keep above the camera frame.Tap the minus button next to a tool if you want to remove it.Tap Done when you are finished.Swipe down on the tools menu to return to the Camera.
Open the Camera app.
Tap the Camera Controls button. It looks like six small dots inside a circle near the camera controls area.
Tap Edit.
Tap a tool you want to keep above the camera frame.
Tap the minus button next to a tool if you want to remove it.
Tap Done when you are finished.
Swipe down on the tools menu to return to the Camera.

Depending on your iPhone and camera mode, available controls can include Flash, Live Photo, Timer, Exposure, Styles and Aspect. Apple also gives you a Reset to Essentials option if you want to return to the default setup.
8) Parents get more control over what kids can open

Apple has put a lot of work into parental controls in iOS 27. The new Ask to Browse feature lets a child request access to a website that has been restricted. The parent receives that request through Messages and can approve or decline it.
You first need Family Sharing set up with your child in the family group.
Open Settings.Tap Family.Select your child.Tap Screen Time.Tap Content & Privacy Restrictions.Tap App Store, Media, Web & Games.Configure the web restrictions you want for your child.
Open Settings.
Tap Family.
Select your child.
Tap Screen Time.
Tap Content & Privacy Restrictions.
Tap App Store, Media, Web & Games.
Configure the web restrictions you want for your child.

When your child tries to visit restricted web content, they can send an Ask to Browse request for your approval. Apple has also expanded Communication Safety. It already helps protect children from nudity in supported Apple services. With iOS 27, Apple says the system can intervene when it detects gore or violent content in shared photos and videos.
9) Find My gives you more control over location sharing

Find My gets a useful privacy upgrade in iOS 27, especially if you only want someone to see your location for a limited amount of time. You can now choose a custom duration for location sharing or set an exact date and time for it to stop. That could come in handy on a trip, during an event or anytime you want temporary location sharing without having to remember to turn it off later. You can also pause location sharing until the end of the day for specific people. Apple says this can be useful when you want to keep something like a surprise party or gift-shopping trip private.

Open the Find My app.Tap People.Tap the contact you want to share your location with.Scroll down and tap Share My Location.Choose Indefinitely, Until End of Day, For One Hour or Custom.If you choose Custom, set the duration or exact date and time when you want sharing to end.
Open the Find My app.
Tap People.
Tap the contact you want to share your location with.
Scroll down and tap Share My Location.
Choose Indefinitely, Until End of Day, For One Hour or Custom.
If you choose Custom, set the duration or exact date and time when you want sharing to end.

If you already share your location with someone, you can also pause sharing with that person until the end of the day from their location-sharing options. I like having more control here because location sharing often makes sense for a specific situation. You may want someone to know where you are during a weekend trip without giving them indefinite access afterward.
Apple’s latest iPhone update introduces 10 standout features, including website monitoring in Safari and customizable Camera controls. (Nikolas Kokovlis/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
10) You can describe a Shortcut and let AI build it

Shortcuts can be incredibly powerful, but building one manually can get complicated fast. iOS 27 makes the process much easier with Describe a Shortcut. You can tell Apple Intelligence what you want your iPhone to automate in plain English. Shortcuts then connects the actions needed to build it. For example, Apple says you could ask your iPhone to message someone with your ETA when you leave work. You could also build automations that work across supported apps.

Open the Shortcuts app.Tap the + icon.Tap Describe a Shortcut.Type what you want the Shortcut to do.Tap the send arrow.Answer any follow-up questions if prompted.Review the Shortcut Apple Intelligence creates.Describe any changes you want if you need to refine it.
Open the Shortcuts app.
Tap the + icon.
Tap Describe a Shortcut.
Type what you want the Shortcut to do.
Tap the send arrow.
Answer any follow-up questions if prompted.
Review the Shortcut Apple Intelligence creates.
Describe any changes you want if you need to refine it.

This could make Shortcuts much more approachable for people who have always liked the idea of automating their iPhone but never wanted to figure out how all the individual actions fit together. Some Shortcuts that rely on Apple’s cloud-based AI models may be subject to daily usage limits.
ASKED SIRI TO CALL YOUR BANK? A SCAM COULD COST THOUSANDS
Bonus: Siri AI is here, but it is still in beta

This is the feature many iPhone owners have been waiting for, but I would treat it differently from the 10 features above. Siri AI is rolling out as a beta in English on supported devices, so expect some rough edges while Apple continues to improve it.
Siri AI can hold more natural conversations and handle follow-up questions. It can also use personal context from information on your device.

For example, you could ask Siri to find an old photo without remembering when you took it. You can also ask it to locate something buried in an email or note. Siri can take more actions inside apps, too. Apple says it can work across messages, emails, photos and other supported apps. Siri can also pull information from the web when you ask broader questions.

The real test will be whether Siri can save you from bouncing between apps. I have always found voice assistants most useful when they remove a few steps from something I already wanted to do. If Siri AI can reliably find a buried email or pull up a photo from years ago based on a vague description, that could change how often people use it. Because this is still a beta, I would double-check important answers or actions before relying on them.
Apple has also given Siri its own app, which makes it feel more like the AI assistants people have grown used to using.
Open the new Siri app.Tap the new conversation icon.Type or speak what you want to ask.Continue with follow-up questions.Return to previous conversations from the main Siri screen.
Open the new Siri app.
Tap the new conversation icon.
Type or speak what you want to ask.
Continue with follow-up questions.
Return to previous conversations from the main Siri screen.
You can also pin conversations you want to keep handy. Apple says you can invoke Siri AI by saying "Hey Siri," pressing the side button or swiping down from the Dynamic Island on supported iPhones.
Kurt’s key takeaways

What I like most about iOS 27 is that some of its best features solve problems you actually run into. Safari can keep an eye on a webpage so you do not have to. The new photo tools could rescue a shot you thought was unusable. Find My also gives you better control over how long someone can see your location. I am especially interested in what Apple Intelligence can do with Shortcuts. Describing an automation instead of building it action by action could finally make Shortcuts approachable for people who have always found it too complicated. Siri AI is still the feature I will be watching most closely. Apple is asking us to trust Siri with more personal context and more complicated requests, so getting the answers right will be critical. The fact that Siri AI launches as a beta tells me we should expect some bumps along the way. What I want from AI on my iPhone is pretty simple. Save me time without making me think about the technology doing the work. If iOS 27 can consistently do that, these features could become the ones you use every day without even thinking about them.
What would Siri AI have to prove before you let it handle more of your day? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.

title: Texas prosecutors take death penalty off the table for man accused of murdering wife and fleeing to Italy
summary: Lee Gilley fled the United States to Italy using forged documents and a fake name after allegedly killing his pregnant wife in Harris County, Texas.
story: Anne Bremner, a Seattle trial lawyer was an advocate for Amanda Knox, explains why Lee Gilley's flight to Italy shielded him from the death penalty he faced in Texas.

Texas prosecutors announced they won't seek the death penalty against a man accused of killing his wife and fleeing the country as his trial was set to begin, they told an Italian court, clearing a path for his extradition to the United States.

Lee Gilley, 39, faces a capital murder charge in connection with the October 2024 death of his wife, Christa, who was nine weeks pregnant when she died. The Harris County Medical Examiner's office determined her death was a homicide resulting from neck compression. He pleaded not guilty.

Authorities allege Gilley removed his ankle monitor on May 1 and left Texas before his scheduled trial was to begin. He got to the Milan Malpensa Airport in Italy by using a fake name and forged travel documents, according to court records. He was taken into custody by Italian authorities.
EXCLUSIVE: FBI EXTRADITIONS SOAR AS PATEL RAMPS UP FOREIGN OUTREACH, VOWS 'NO SANCTUARY'

Lee Mongerson Gilley and his defense attorney, Ed McClees, right, are shown in the 497th District Court at the Harris County Justice Center, 1201 Franklin, Thursday, Oct. 17, 2024, in Houston. He is charged with capital murder in the death of his wife, Christa Gilley. (Melissa Phillip/Houston Chronicle via Getty Images)

Gilley's American attorney, Dick DeGuerin, previously told Fox News Digital that Italy wanted a written guarantee prosecutors wouldn't seek the death penalty before considering his return. Italian authorities may also demand assurances against a sentence of life without parole, he said.

The Harris County District Attorney said in a Friday court filing obtained by Fox News Digital that it won't be pursuing the death penalty against Gilley, but stopped short of taking life without parole off the table as a possible sentence.
MULTIPLE DEATH SENTENCES IN DIFFERENT STATES ARE SET TO BE CARRIED OUT WITHIN 24 HOURS: 'NOT VERY COMMON'

title: Mississippi grand jury declines to indict anyone in death of 18-year-old who vanished in coastal waters
summary: A 23-member Jackson County grand jury heard from 43 witnesses and found Nolan Wells' death on Horn Island was consistent with drowning, not foul play.
story: A caller aboard the boat that brought Nolan Wells to Horn Island tells a Sea Tow dispatcher the vessel is sinking with seven people onboard on July 4. (Credit: MDMR)

A Mississippi grand jury found no evidence of criminal conduct in the death of 18-year-old Nolan Wells, concluding that the college football player’s body was found under circumstances "consistent with drowning" after his disappearance during a Fourth of July boating trip.

The 23-member Jackson County grand jury found no criminal charges were warranted after hearing from 43 witnesses and reviewing physical and digital evidence, police reports, interviews, videos, images and maps, according to the grand jury report released by District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath on Monday.

Wells disappeared July 4 after traveling with friends to Horn Island, a barrier island off Mississippi’s Gulf Coast. His body was recovered in the waters off the island two days later after a multi-agency search.
NEW AUDIO RELEASED FOLLOWING NOLAN WELLS DISAPPEARANCE DOESN'T SHOW 'ANYTHING NEFARIOUS': RETIRED FBI AGENT
Nolan Wells smiles on the field while playing wide receiver for Southwest Mississippi Community College. (Christine Wonsley/Facebook)

The report said the "position of, condition of, time of discovery, and location" of Wells’ body were consistent with drowning and that there was "no credible evidence" anyone traveling to or from the island committed a crime related to his death.

The grand jury also found that bruising on the back of Wells’ head was "not a fatal injury." The report said there was no evidence of a fatal injury or organic disease, though investigators could not determine how Wells suffered the bruise.

One witness testified that Wells was seen slipping "awkwardly off the side of a boat" around the time he was last seen. The witness could not say whether Wells struck his head during the fall and said Wells continued socializing afterward and did not appear injured.
The report also said Wells was not involved in a physical altercation or argument that day.
SHARPTON OFFERS $50K FOR NOLAN WELLS CASE ARREST WITH LAWYER TO RELEASE AUTOPSY AT NAACP
A private autopsy commissioned by Wells’ family had previously listed his cause and manner of death as "undetermined pending investigation."
Nolan Wells wears blue swim trunks and sunglasses on a boat off Horn Island, Mississippi, on July 4, 2026. (Jackson County Sheriff’s Office)

During a July 22 news conference, civil rights attorney Ben Crump said the examination found an area of "red discoloration" on the back of Wells’ head, but pathologist Dr. Roger Mitchell could not determine a cause or manner of death.
Questions had also been raised about Wells’ alcohol consumption.

A July 5 Mississippi Department of Marine Resources Marine Patrol email previously obtained by Fox News Digital listed Wells’ alcohol intake as "heavy" while authorities searched for him. The email did not identify the source of that information.
The grand jury found that Wells bought alcohol using a fake ID and that no adults of legal drinking age provided him with alcohol on the island.

The report said toxicology testing was "not particularly informative" because decomposition fluid is an unreliable source for determining substance levels in a body. It also said there was no cocaine in Wells’ system and no evidence he had ever used the drug.
The report also shed light on Wells’ cellphone, which was taken back to the mainland without him.
CAJUN NAVY LEADER WARNS NOLAN WELLS' SEARCH AREA HAS DEADLY 'WASHING MACHINE' CURRENTS: 'LOTS OF DROWNINGS'

The grand jury said it was not unusual for people visiting the island to return on different boats or leave phones and other belongings aboard boats while socializing. Wells’ phone was not the only one that returned to the mainland without its owner, according to the report.
White sand beaches are seen at Horn Island in the Gulf of Mexico, Mississippi, on June 26, 2010. (James Edward Bates/Biloxi Sun Herald/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)
Wells’ death attracted national attention and widespread speculation online.

The grand jury said allegations targeting the occupants of the three boats involved in the trip had spread to their relatives and friends, calling the "public attacks" "malicious, false," and having "no truth in fact or evidence."

Wells’ family was given an opportunity to provide evidence from its private investigation. According to the report, the family’s attorneys said their investigation had found no witnesses or evidence they reasonably believed pointed to potential criminal activity that warranted referral.
The case could still return to a grand jury if new evidence emerges. Mississippi has no statute of limitations on homicide cases.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"If credible evidence comes to light in the future that suggests Mr. Wells’ death was non-accidental, this matter should be represented to the Jackson County Grand Jury for further consideration," the report said.
Fox News Digital's Stepheny Price contributed to this report.

title: Kirk family may have path around archaic law shielding gov't in police chief’s alleged ‘got you covered’ text
summary: A key text message from UVU's police chief could help Charlie Kirk's family pierce Utah's governmental immunity shield in their wrongful death claim.
story: While Utah state law gives broad immunity to governmental entities from civil damages claims related to assault and battery, attorney Randolph Rice says Turning Point USA "detrimentally relied" on an alleged statement from UVU's chief of police.

Utah law granting broad immunity to government entities and their employees could make it difficult for Charlie Kirk’s family to pursue a wrongful death claim against the state and Utah Valley University — but there's a key piece of evidence they've raised in legal filings that could clear the hurdle, according to a trial attorney and legal analyst.

"Utah law makes it very difficult for the Charlie Kirk family to proceed with a civil claim against the state and the university," said Randolph Rice, a Maryland-based attorney and former prosecutor who is following the case.
The Utah Governmental Immunity Act shields government entities and employees from many civil damages claims, he said.
CHARLIE KIRK'S FAMILY ALLEGES UVU KNEW OF ROOFTOP SECURITY RISK BEFORE HIS ASSASSINATION: LEGAL FILING

Law enforcement officers work at Utah Valley University, where U.S. conservative commentator Charlie Kirk was shot and killed during an event, in Orem, Utah, U.S. on September 10, 2025. (REUTERS/Jim Urquhart)

A lawsuit from the family of Gabby Petito against the Moab Police Department alleged that officers were negligent in their response to a traffic stop involving Brian Laundrie two weeks before he killed her. A judge dismissed the case on governmental immunity grounds. The Petito family is appealing.
GABBY PETITO'S MOTHER URGES PUBLIC 'RIPPLE EFFECT' TO HELP FIND THE MISSING 5 YEARS AFTER DAUGHTER'S MURDER

Charlie Kirk throws hats to the crowd after arriving at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025, in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)
"Generally speaking, they are immune from any type of civil suit, meaning money damages," Rice said — but there is a potential exception.

Kirk's family filed a notice of claim, which is a precursor to a lawsuit, last week — alleging that Utah Valley University, the state of Utah and key officials failed to properly secure the event even after acknowledging responsibility for rooftop security, leading to his wrongful death.
CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION: NEW UVU PRESIDENT SAYS IT WILL CONTINUE TO 'HOST THE FRAYS,' EMBRACE FREE SPEECH

Among the claims in the filing, UVU Police Chief Jeffrey Long allegedly told Turning Point USA organizers "I got you covered" when they raised concerns about rooftop access around the campus courtyard.
Area near the roof of the Loose Center on the campus of Utah Valley University. (Stepheny Price/Fox News Digital)
That text message could be key to overcoming Utah's immunity law, he said, because Kirk was shot and killed by a sniper on a rooftop.
SURVEILLANCE VIDEO TIMELINE TRACKS ACCUSED CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSIN ACROSS UVU CAMPUS BEFORE FATAL ROOFTOP SHOT

title: Maryland hunter's alleged mistake leaves Delaware mother dead
summary: A hunter faces manslaughter charges after allegedly mistaking a woman who was walking through a field for a deer while he was hunting in Delaware.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
A Maryland hunter is accused of fatally shooting a woman after mistaking her for a deer while she walked through a Delaware field with her children, according to state police.
Walter Moorhead, 74, was arrested for manslaughter and other charges after he shot Santos Maria Chilel Soto, 39, on Friday evening in Ellendale, Delaware, State Police said in a press release.

Soto was walking through an open field with a man and two children at around 7:40 p.m. as Moorhead was hunting deer from a ground blind, which is a camouflaged structure used by hunters to hide from the sight of game animals.
MANHUNT UNDERWAY IN CALIFORNIA AFTER ARMED SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY POINTS GUN AT PEOPLE, SHOOTS AT OFFICERS
Walter Moorhead, 74, was arrested for manslaughter and other charges. (Delaware State Police)
According to police, Moorhead believed he saw a deer and fired his rifle, striking Soto.
State troopers responded to the scene and provided life-saving medical care before Soto was rushed to a local hospital, where she was later pronounced dead.

Moorhead was was slapped with multiple felony charges — manslaughter recklessly causing the death of another person, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony and three counts of first-degree reckless endangerment.
SUSPECT IN DEATHS OF 5 FOUND DEAD AFTER COPS UNCOVER GRIM SCENE AT RURAL PROPERTY OUTSIDE PORTLAND
Santos Maria Chilel Soto was described as a mother of five children and a "beloved" aunt. (Iglesia De Dios Fuente De Verdad Delaware)
He was released from custody after posting a $43,000 cash bond.
The incident remains under investigation.
Soto was described as a mother of five children and a "beloved" aunt, according to a GoFundMe page.

"Maria’s family is now facing the overwhelming pain of this sudden loss while also trying to make sure she is laid to rest with dignity," the fundraiser reads. "This heartbreaking situation has placed a heavy financial burden on the family at a time when they are grieving deeply."
Police said Walter Moorhead mistakenly believed he saw a deer and fired his rifle. (Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

The fundraiser was launched to help the family cover funeral services and the cost of sending her body to Guatemala. Roughly $12,000 has been raised as of Monday evening.

title: Austin ICE shooting sparks fight over Venezuelan illegal immigrant's deportation
summary: LULAC and Rep. Lloyd Doggett are demanding an independent investigation into the shooting and questioning federal officials’ account of the involved shooting in Austin.
story: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez was shot during an ICE pursuit in Austin on Sept. 20, 2026, and taken to a local trauma center in serious but stable condition (Credit: Heidi Ann Clark via Storyful).

One of the nation's largest Hispanic civil rights groups called Monday for the Venezuelan illegal immigrant who was shot during an ICE pursuit in Austin to not be deported, arguing he is a key witness in the investigation into officers' use of force.

The League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC) made the statements Monday afternoon after an agent shot and wounded Wilber Rafael Garces Perez during a traffic stop. Garces Perez was hospitalized in serious but stable condition. The shooting sparked protests in Austin and calls from local officials for an independent investigation.
"Wilber is a victim of the shooting and the most important witness to it. You do not deport the key witness to your own officers' use of force," LULAC CEO Juan Peruano said.
According to Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, the attorney for Garces Perez and his wife, Garces Perez was delivering DoorDash when an "unmarked black truck sideswiped him."
ICE SHOOTING ROCKS AUSTIN AS DEMOCRAT DEMANDS BODYCAM VIDEO, INDEPENDENT PROBE
She said he did not know the vehicle was operated by ICE and subsequently made a U-turn under the highway before the agents continued to pursue him.
"The truck chased him and sideswiped him again. And the agents came out and shot him in the back of the neck and pulled him out of the car," Lincoln-Goldfinch said.
Lincoln-Goldfinch also claimed Garces Perez did not receive sufficient medical care, and the bullet remained lodged hours after the shooting.
ICE OFFICER PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO LYING ABOUT MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING INVOLVING VENEZUELAN MAN
Wilber Rafael Garces Perez was shot following an ICE traffic stop in Austin, Texas, on Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026. (Wilber Garces / Facebook)

"We learned that at 4:00 he still had a bullet lodged in his back. He was shot here in his back, and they didn't take the bullet out, and they didn't give him pain medication. And they transferred him to ICE, to a processing center, where he spent the night without a bed," Lincoln-Goldfinch said. "There is absolutely zero justification for having shot him in the back of the neck. And this is why we're calling for a stop to ICE traffic stops. ICE officers are over armed, overpaid, under trained and violent. They don't know how to safely conduct traffic stops."

According to his attorney, Garces Perez had a work permit and was seeking asylum after entering the U.S. in 2024 through the CBP One app, which the Biden administration expanded to allow migrants to request asylum at ports of entry.
His attorney claimed he received a removal order after a notice for his immigration hearing was sent to his old address, despite him having updated his address with the court.

"He changed his address with the immigration court, and a notice of hearing was sent to his old address. He didn't know he had a hearing. He didn't go. And so he got a deportation order in absentia, which is a very common thing," she said. "The court is notorious for sending notices of hearings to the wrong address. So it appears that that is what happened with him. That's why he has a removal order. We are working on that."

According to the Austin Police Department, hundreds of protesters gathered Sunday evening following the ICE operation, throwing rocks, bottles and pieces of concrete. Three police vehicles were damaged, and multiple officers sustained minor injuries, officials said.

At least three people were arrested for rioting, resisting arrest, assaulting a peace officer, or a combination of the charges. The individuals were identified as Robert Padgett, 48; Armando Menagarcia, 29; and Matthew Hemby, 44.
Lincoln-Goldfinch further to condemned the accounts provided by federal agents, claiming ICE officials do not tell the truth.
"We are fed up with ICE and DHS telling us lies about what has happened in these incidents where people are being murdered and shot," she said.
Rep. Lloyd Doggett echoed Lincoln-Goldfinch's assertions, claiming that federal immigration officials often lie.
"ICE has no credibility anymore. It lies. We know it lies. We've seen it demonstrated again and again, and we need the kind of independent structure to demand some accountability," he said.

DHS sources confirmed to Fox News on Sunday that Garces Perez is an illegal immigrant from Venezuela with a final order of removal.
DHS said Garces Perez illegally entered the United States under the Biden administration. The agency said he was shot during a law enforcement operation.
"The illegal alien's condition is stable, and he is in federal custody pending removal," DHS added on X.

title: Murdaugh defense says detectives found male DNA under victim's nails but skipped key testing
summary: Alex Murdaugh's defense accuses prosecutors of stalling on unidentified male DNA found under Maggie Murdaugh's fingernails before his retrial.
story: Former prosecutor Joshua Ritter breaks down the risk in Alex Murdaugh's push to test the unknown male DNA under Maggie Murdaugh's fingernails, a move he says could backfire if it comes back to a man with an alibi.

Attorneys for Alex Murdaugh have filed a motion asking a judge to force South Carolina prosecutors to hand over pieces of key forensic evidence, like the unidentified male DNA found under Maggie Murdaugh's fingernails that they say the state crime lab never fully tested.

The 93-page filing by Alex Murdaugh's attorneys on Friday seeks the additional DNA and ballistics evidence, along with raw data from a laser scan of the crime scene in Colleton County, South Carolina.
Attorneys for Alex Murdaugh accused the state of stalling in a way that could jeopardize the defense's trial preparation.
MURDAUGH WANTS IDAHO MURDERS DNA DREAM TEAM BEHIND KOHBERGER CASE TO HELP REWRITE SECOND MURDER TRIAL

Alex Murdaugh enters the courtroom for a pretrial hearing ahead of his murder retrial at the Lexington County Courthouse in Lexington, S.C., Aug. 14, 2026. (Tracy Glantz of The Columbia, South Carolina, State/Pool)

"Every week the State withholds this material is a week taken from the preparation of the defense, and if the delay continues the defense may be forced to seek a continuance that Mr. Murdaugh does not want and that the Court has said it will not grant. The State should not be permitted to create, through inaction, the very delay it would then oppose," the motion states.

Alex Murdaugh's defense team previously requested that DNA evidence from underneath Maggie Murdaugh's fingernails be released to Othram, Inc. After Othram tested the DNA, the defense argued that additional testing is needed to recover a male DNA profile that the defense says the state crime lab found but never fully pursued.
SEND US A TIP
READ IT: Alex Murdaugh defense team's motion to compel evidence
His defense argued that the partial DNA profile from swabs on Maggie Murdaugh's phone should be further tested as well.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Alex Murdaugh appears in court during a pretrial hearing ahead of his murder retrial at the Lexington County Courthouse in Lexington, S.C., Aug. 14, 2026. (Tracy Glantz of The Columbia, South Carolina State/Pool)

Defense attorneys are also asking for a list of every shooting in the counties surrounding the crime scene where .300 Blackout cases or projectiles were recovered, along with details about each crime. They also asked for raw data from a 3D laser scan SLED took of the crime scene. Prosecutors handed over a read-only viewer file in 2022, but the defense says it needs the raw data to reconstruct the scene.

Alex Murdaugh's defense also accused prosecutors of flip-flopping on the murder weapon. The state argued at his 2023 trial that the .300 Blackout rifle was uncommon, pointing toward the family's guns, but now calls it one of the most popular AR cartridges in the country, according to the motion.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

"The State has had continuous and exclusive custody of every item of physical evidence in this case, including the biological material that is the subject of Part III of this motion, for more than five years. It has tested what it wished to test, in the sequence it wished to test it, without notice to the defense and without the defense's consent. It now proposes that the defense may not do the same," defense attorneys argued.
Joshua Ritter, a former prosecutor and Fox News contributor, said Murdaugh's request for additional DNA may backfire, calling it a "big gamble."

"I think it's probably better left alone by the defense so that they can make that argument about this unknown male. 'Who is that? Why didn't the prosecution test it? Why didn't they do anything about it?' Maybe they're concerned that the prosecution could point the finger right back at them and say, well, you guys didn't test it either, you had it for as much time as we did," he said.

Defense attorney Dick Harpootlian represented his client, Alex Murdaugh, on June 29, 2026, at a status hearing at the Marc H. Westbrook Judicial Center in Lexington, South Carolina. (Tracy Glantz/The State via Pool)

Alex Murdaugh was convicted in 2023 of murdering his wife, Maggie, and son, Paul, at the family's Moselle property in Colleton County. The South Carolina Supreme Court later overturned the convictions after finding that former Colleton County Clerk of Court Becky Hill improperly influenced the jury. His retrial is scheduled to begin April 5, 2027.

title: Lindsay Clancy defense files motion to dismiss under double jeopardy grounds, with focus on holdout juror
summary: Lindsay Clancy's defense team is raising a double jeopardy claim, seeking to avoid a second trial after jurors deadlocked when deliberating the charges against her.
story: A mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case prompts holdout juror Michael P. Desronvil to defend his position through a statement. Criminal defense attorney Mercedes Colwin breaks down the juror's reasoning and outlines potential next steps for prosecutors in Massachusetts, including a possible retrial or negotiated plea deal as the high-profile legal battle continues.
Lindsay Clancy's defense has filed a double jeopardy motion seeking to have the three first-degree murder charges she faces for the strangling deaths of her young children dismissed.

Attorney Martin Weinberg, who also represented Karen Read in her double jeopardy claim, filed a motion for Clancy Monday raising claims under the Fifth, Sixth and Fourteenth Amendments.  Read's claim failed, but she was later acquitted of all homicide-related charges in her second trial.

Weinberg argued that there was no "manifest necessity" to declare a mistrial on Sept. 4 "given the absence of judicial inquiry regarding repeated reports that one juror was refusing to apply the Court's instructions regarding reasonable doubt."

The jury split 11-1, with only the holdout wanting to find her guilty. The others were in favor of finding her not criminally responsible for the children's deaths after Clancy's defense claimed she suffered from postpartum psychosis.
LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR MAKES NEW PROMISE AS LAWYER WARNS OF PUBLIC ATTACKS

Michael P. Desronvil, left, the lone holdout juror who forced a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case, has retained an attorney who once represented President Donald Trump. Clancy, right, faced three counts of first-degree murder in the strangling deaths of her three children. (Facebook/Brittany K and Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via AP, Pool)

Judge William Sullivan previously overruled a defense motion to have the holdout juror dismissed and replaced with an alternate, saying he felt it was not appropriate for him to get involved in the deliberations.

"The jury twice informed the Court that one of its members was refusing to apply the Court's instructions regarding the fundamental concept of reasonable doubt," Weinberg wrote. "After the first such report, the Court asked each juror individually whether he or she was able to apply the law. Upon receiving the second report, the Court tempered its response even further, simply reminding all jurors as a group of their obligation to follow its instructions generally. The Court denied Ms. Clancy's explicit requests to go further."

Weinberg's motion argued that Sullivan's decision to declare a mistrial before investigating the holdout is improper, alleging that the jury foreperson accused the holdout of making "statements acknowledging doubt but refus[ing] to apply it to the verdict as the law states."

"Ms. Clancy, like all criminal defendants, had a Constitutional right to have her fate decided by an impartial jury of her peers, faithfully applying the law as instructed rather than superimposing the juror's own view of legal right and wrong, including the foundational principle that, absent proof beyond a reasonable doubt of her guilt, she must be acquitted," he wrote. "The multiple reports of a juror violating this bedrock principle, therefore, required a judicial inquiry sufficient to ascertain whether her right to an impartial jury was being violated."

Weinberg also argued that there was a legal basis for conducting a probe into the holdout before the mistrial was declared. However, Sullivan did not hold one.
LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN

On Friday, Clancy's trial attorney Kevin Reddington called for an investigation into the holdout juror who wanted to find her guilty of murder charges in connection with the strangling deaths of her three young children.

"[The other jurors] know that they were robbed — by one man — for whatever his agenda was, who stole seven weeks of the life of these other jurors that were so attentive, so beautiful, so wonderful and listened to this evidence," he told reporters after leaving the courthouse following her mistrial.

Reddington is asking a Massachusetts judge to preserve juror records from all 12 panelists and six alternates, including their questionnaires, courthouse hallway surveillance video taken outside the deliberation room and sign-in sheets for the jurors' cellphones.

Reddington is asking the court to conduct a "limited inquiry" into the holdout and for information on any potential background checks stemming from a February motion for access to prospective juror information filed by Plymouth County prosecutors.

He's also seeking the holdout's juror questionnaire and any supplemental filings, probation records and "Juror Doe's record from the statewide domestic violence registry." He is asking the judge to require prosecutors to divulge whether it has had any contact with the holdout as a defendant, complainant or subject going back to January 2021.

Additionally, Reddington is looking for the holdout's phone records between the hours of 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. on each deliberation day and asking for the court to order an independent examination into his phone use during the deliberation period.

Lastly, he wants the holdout to be grilled regarding the truthfulness of his juror questionnaire and voir dire answers, his statements to the court on Sept. 3, and the use of a phone or outside information during deliberations.

title: Suspects in Haitian president's assassination transferred to Miami, accused of funding plot with COVID fraud
summary: Exclusive video shows 18 shackled suspects arriving in Miami after transfer in the assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse case.
story: Fox News reporter Danamarie McNicholl reports as the suspects in the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse arrive in Miami to face federal charges on 'Special Report.'

Eighteen allegedly involved in the brazen 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse have touched down on U.S. soil to face federal charges, with Fox News cameras on the tarmac for their arrival Sunday.

In exclusive footage, the defendants can be seen stepping off a U.S. military aircraft in Miami, shackled and tightly guarded by FBI and Department of Homeland Security agents in military-like fatigues. The dramatic transfer marks a major turning point in the international investigation into the plot that left the Haitian leader dead in his bedroom.

"Today, the FBI and our interagency partners executed the largest foreign transfer of custody in FBI history," FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital in a statement. "It is the latest in an all-out 18-month blitz by this FBI man-hunting high-value targets across the world and bringing them back to the United States to face justice."

The ​53-year-old president was shot dead in July 2021 at his private residence in ​the hills above Port-au-Prince, a killing that left a gaping political vacuum ⁠in the Caribbean nation and emboldened powerful armed groups in the country.
FBI EXTRADITES FORMER TEN MOST WANTED FUGITIVE ARRESTED FOR 2000 MURDER OF 5-YEAR-OLD GIRL IN PHILADELPHIA
Fox News cameras captured the arrival of 18 suspects in the 2021 killing of Haitian President Jovenel Moise out of Haiti on Sunday. (Fox News Channel)

According to FBI Miami, the accused — comprising operatives from Haiti and Colombia — were transferred from Haitian custody to face the U.S. justice system. Federal prosecutors established jurisdiction because the conspiracy was largely organized and financed in South Florida.

Prosecutors allege the defendants utilized fraudulent COVID-19 Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans to bankroll the deadly mission. A complex five-year federal investigation into 30 suspects charged with crimes revealed the assassination was financed by American taxpayer dollars to businesses based in Florida to gather the weapons, tactical gear, and Colombian mercenaries that killed Moise inside his own home.

The charges include conspiracy to kill or kidnap a person abroad, as well as wire fraud. Some of the assassins even allegedly posed as federal agents with the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) in order to get inside the presidential residence in Haiti.
MAN PLEADS GUILTY TO STEALING OVER $1M IN PPP LOANS FOR SUPPOSED AMATEUR BASKETBALL LEAGUE

As the 18 suspects arrived in Miami, Department of Justice prosecutors unsealed an indictment detailing the sprawling conspiracy. Court documents outline a plot initially aimed at violently overthrowing the Haitian President, which ultimately escalated into an assassination.

The defendants were brought to the U.S. to make their first appearance in federal court in Miami on Monday at 10 a.m. ET. Because cameras are strictly prohibited inside federal courtrooms, the exclusive tarmac video serves as the only visual of the suspects entering U.S. custody. (Fox News Channel)

This was "really about greed," Miami Special Agent in Charge Brett Skiles told Fox News. "These were people that owned business interests in the United States that were looking to get lucrative contracts from the government of Haiti and believed that if they could initiate a regime change to the assassination, that those contracts could then come their way, and they would profit off of it."

The defendants were making their first appearance in federal court in Miami Monday morning. Because cameras are strictly prohibited inside federal courtrooms, the exclusive tarmac video serves as the only visual of the suspects entering U.S. custody.

"This assassination plot was planned, financed, conspired, here in Miami," U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Florida Jason Reding Quiñones told Fox News. "It's not only just holding people accountable for committing murder, but it's holding people accountable if they use government funds in a fraud to facilitate that murder."
KASH PATEL REVEALS FBI'S CAPTURE OF ALL 10 MEMBERS OF MOST WANTED FUGITIVE'S LIST DURING HEARING
The four ringleaders of this 2021 assassination plot were convicted in Miami in May and they face life in prison.
Prosecutors ⁠argued during the nine-week trial in a Miami federal court that the men assembled two dozen former Colombian soldiers and supplied them ​with money, guns, ammunition and tactical vests.
"When you pick up the phone and engage with foreign partners at a historic level, as we’ve done – a 400% increase these last 18 months – this is what happens," Patel's statement concluded.
"Thank you to FBI Miami for their leadership in this investigation as well as our law enforcement partners who executed."
Haitian Justice Minister Patrick ​Pelissier confirmed in a statement that suspects had been transferred from Haiti to the US, adding that Haitian judicial proceedings had been delayed.

"While the American procedure has recorded significant progress, notably arrests, prosecutions, and ​convictions, the Haitian procedure remains confronted with major difficulties and has not, to date, resulted ​in a trial being held, after five years of proceedings," Pelissier said.

title: ‘American Idol’ contestant’s 100K texts with mistress show motive in wife’s murder, prosecutors say
summary: Caleb Flynn allegedly texted his mistress about ways to kill his wife months before prosecutors say he staged Ashley Flynn's death as a break-in.
story: Former 'American Idol' contestant Caleb Flynn faces trial for his wife's murder. Fox News contributor Josh Ritter weighs in on the incriminating text messages Flynn sent his mistress before he allegedly murdered his wife. Ritter also discusses the Missouri woman who allegedly threatened to kill Austin Metcalf's family.

Former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn allegedly told his mistress he was "literally trying to think of ways to kill" his wife without going to jail before prosecutors say he shot her and staged the scene to look like a break-in.
The chilling message was among more than 100,000 texts prosecutors say Flynn exchanged with his mistress in the year before his wife, Ashley Flynn, was killed Feb. 16, WHIO in Dayton reported.
"I was up until 4 a.m. last night crying, literally trying to think of ways to kill her and not go to jail," Flynn allegedly wrote in one of the messages.
NEW JERSEY MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING WIFE WITH BARBELL ALLEGEDLY CONFESSED IN MESSAGES TO RELATIVES: REPORT
Prosecutors revealed during opening statements Friday that Flynn had been carrying on a year-long affair and argued the messages showed his motive and intent, WHIO reported.

Caleb Flynn appears in Miami County Common Pleas Court, Troy, Ohio, March 30, 2026. Flynn is charged with the murder of his wife, 37-year-old Ashley Flynn, who was shot to death in their Tipp City home in February. (Matthew Symons for Fox News Digital)

Miami County Prosecutor Paul Watkins told jurors the messages, some sent months apart and others just hours before Ashley was killed, showed Flynn repeatedly expressing hatred toward his wife and a desire to be free of her so he could pursue a future with his mistress.
MICROSOFT EXEC'S GRIEVING WIDOW FACES MAN ACCUSED OF PLOTTING HIS MURDER AS SHE REVEALS EERIE FINAL CALL
Flynn has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and other charges in his wife's death.
Fox News legal analyst Josh Ritter said Sunday that one message sent the day before Ashley's killing could be particularly damaging.
LUIGI MANGIONE'S LIVESTREAM STUNT AIMS TO GET INFLUENCERS TO 'PRESSURE' JURORS: FORMER PROSECUTOR
Body camera footage shows Caleb Flynn bending down to vomit after his wife’s murder inside their home in Tipp City, Ohio on Feb. 16, 2026. (Tipp City Police Department)

CHARLIE KIRK MURDER CASE AS 'STRAIGHT-FORWARD' AS IT GETS, PROSECUTORS ARGUE AS CASE NEARS TRIAL DECISION

Defense attorney Emily Smith told jurors prosecutors were offering a theory built around circumstantial evidence rather than proof that Flynn killed his wife, arguing Ashley deserved justice based on more than speculation.
Testimony Monday shifted to the physical evidence inside the Flynn home, where a veteran crime scene investigator challenged Flynn's claim that an intruder broke in and killed his wife.

Caleb Flynn becomes emotional in court during his murder trial in Ohio. Flynn is accused of killing his wife, Ashley Flynn, in February 2026 and staging the scene to look like a break-in. (COURTESY: WKEF)

Flynn became emotional as jurors were walked through evidence collected from the home, at one point sitting with tears streaming down his face as the investigator testified.

The investigator also testified that authorities were told Flynn kept a loaded handgun in the center console of his Ford F-150. The console was found open, but investigators did not find the gun or ammunition inside.

title: Tourists seeking 'dramatic' photo on isolated beach trapped by incoming tide
summary: Drone footage captures three tourists spelling out "SOS" on Oregon's Lost Boy Beach after a rising tide trapped them in the Tillamook County cove.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Tourists went to snap an iconic photo on Oregon's Lost Boy Beach and wound up getting one taken of themselves in a storybook SOS rescue by the local fire department last week.

Three unnamed sea gawkers were stranded for five hours Wednesday, Sept. 16, after a rising tide cut them off from the mainland at the secluded Tillamook County cove. Having reportedly lost cell phone service at the bottom of the steep cliff, the group managed to contact 911 using an emergence satellite feature, The Oregonian reported.

Netarts-Oceanside Fire District received the call and found them stranded on the shrinking patch of beach with the tide rolling in on them, using a drone to capture footage of them spelling out a large "SOS" with sticks.
11 VISITORS TRAPPED AS DANGEROUS FLASH FLOODING TEARS THROUGH ICONIC NATIONAL PARK

Stranded thrill-seekers were discovered by local rescue workers on Lost Boy Beach in Oregon, spelling out SOS with dead sticks in footage captured by an emergency drone. (Netarts-Oceanside Fire District)

Lost Boy Beach is accessible only by scrambling over rocky terrain and passing through a sea cave that is open at both ends. While the small beach is inviting during low tide, the rising water blocks the only exit.
"When people are stranded there, we may not be able to get to them," NOFD Chief Jeff McBrayer told the paper.
HELICOPTER RESCUE CREW CAUGHT ON CAMERA SAVING 2 CLIMBERS TRAPPED ALONG POPULAR CALIFORNIA BEACH CLIFF

Three unnamed tourists were stranded on Lost Boy Beach in Oregon after trekking down a cliff to get what they called a 'dramatic' photo of an icon seascape. They wound up getting drone photos taken of their own rescue. (Netarts-Oceanside Fire District)

Crews initially considered waiting for the tide to recede, but opted for an active rescue due to rough surf, the presence of sneaker waves, and the fact that the tourists were already wet and cold, he added.

Navigating the dangerous conditions, rescuers hugged the remaining shoreline while secured to ropes instead of wading directly through the unpredictable water. Once they reached the tourists, responders provided life vests, clipped the group to the safety ropes, and guided them through the surf to a secure area where they could walk out on their own.
CALIFORNIA DAD PARALYZED FROM NECK DOWN AFTER DIVING INTO OCEAN TO RESCUE CHILD

The Netarts-Oceanside Fire District was able to rescue three thrill-seeking tourists who were stranded and wrote SOS with nearby sticks and issued a future warning about repeating their mistake. (Netarts-Oceanside Fire District)
The visitors emerged from the ordeal with only minor bumps and bruises.
Following the rescue, Chief McBrayer used the incident to remind coastal visitors of the area's deceptive dangers of exploring isolated coves.
"You have to ask a local or check a tide app on a phone for tide information," he said.
HIKERS STRANDED ON MOUNT SHASTA AFTER RELYING ON AI TO PLAN TRIP, SHERIFF SAYS

Drone footage captured the stranded sea gawkers after an emergency 911 signal sent from the location that was cut off from regular cell phone service, according to the report. (Netarts-Oceanside Fire District)

Lost Boy Beach, situated on the northern Oregon coast just south of a towering basalt cliff, derives its ominous name from a century-old local legend. According to regional lore, the highly secluded spot was named after a young boy who was believed to have drowned after being trapped by the incoming tide. While it remains unverified if the tragic tale is historically accurate, the name has persisted for roughly 100 years, functioning as a built-in, enduring warning to visitors about the cove's unpredictable and deadly conditions.

Historically, reaching this hidden stretch of sand has remained notoriously treacherous, wedged between Short Beach to the north and Tunnel Beach — sometimes known as Star Trek Beach — to the south. Unlike its neighboring Short Beach, which finally received a community-built "stairway of 100 steps" around 2000 to stop visitors from cracking their heads on a slippery cliff face, Lost Boy Beach has never featured safe overland access.
