title: ‘DWTS’ Pro Witney Carson’s Sons Help Her With Adorable Gender Reveal
summary: Witney Carson and husband Carson McAllister had their two sons help them with their gender reveal. Find out if she’s having a boy or girl.
story: Witney Carson and husband Carson McAllister just found out the gender of baby No. 3.
In a Sept. 21 Instagram video, the “Dancing With the Stars” pro shared how she found out if her family was adding a little boy or a little girl to their crew.
The video shows the couple on a dock with their backs turned while their two sons — Kevin, 5, and Jet, 3 — picked a pink or blue bouquet of flowers, announcing the baby’s gender.
After reading the card that tells them which bouquet to grab, Kevin grabs the blue one, but Jet then picks up the pink one, confusing his parents for a second.
“It’s a boy,” Carson says, as McAllister adds, “Are we just a house full of brothers?”

“Baby McAllister number 3 is a,” the caption reads, which also includes blue hearts and teary-eyed emoji. “We couldn’t be happier or feel more blessed with all these boys. I love being a boy mom. My greatest honor in life is to raise them.”
The couple were congratulated in the comments section by friends, including Robert Irwin, who was Carson’s “DWTS” Season 34 winning partner.
“SO EXCITED,” Irwin wrote, along with a number of blue heart emoji.

“As a mom of three boys, you’ll always have a full dance card for life. It is the best,” one fan wrote, while another added, “This gets me so teary eye because raising boys to be men is such a privilege and the excitement he had when he saw it was a brother is just unbeatable.”
Carson announced that she was pregnant on Aug. 17, weeks before she was confirmed to be returning for Season 35 of “DWTS.”
In an interview with TODAY.com, the dancer shared that she and her husband knew it was time to expand their family.

“We know that we want a lot of kids and we thought it was a perfect year to start doing that,” she said. “Then this opportunity came up again to do the show, and it just felt like, ‘You know what? I kind of want to prove to myself that I can do both!’ And I love both.”
She was determined to continue working, saying she didn’t feel like she had to put work on hold.

“I don’t feel like people necessarily have to lose parts of themselves to keep growing their family. That’s kind of my mantra. I’m gonna stay true to what I love and continue on my career and continue to grow my family,” she said.” It’s a big blessing to be able to do both.”

Carson competed with partner Guillermo Rodriguez on the first night of the two-night “DWTS” Season 35 premiere. During the Sept. 15 episode, they danced a cha cha to “Mr. Big Stuff” by Jean Knight, scoring a 10 out of 30.
Though they had the lowest scores of the night, the pair escaped an elimination and are gearing up for their second dance on the Sept. 22 episode.
Carson told TODAY.com that she was “feeling good” and during rehearsals was listening to her body, making sure her baby’s healthy.

“As much as I want to dance and want to do all of it, I really have to be careful to make sure that I don’t overdo it,” she said. “It’s perfectly safe to do all the things and I’m really not taking this any differently than I would any other season as far as mentally and physically.”

title: When Is ‘The Voice’ On? How to Watch the Season 30 Premiere
summary: “The Voice” is back for another season filled with inspiring singers, along with new and returning faces taking a seat on the famous red chairs.
story: “The Voice” is back for another season filled with inspiring singers, along with new and returning faces taking a seat on the famous red chairs.
Celebrating its milestone 30th season, the NBC singing competition show kicks off with a three-night premiere that starts on Monday, Sept. 21.
During her appearance on TODAY ahead of the premiere, Kelly Clarkson called this season “fun” and exciting, especially with the addition of two new coaches.
Carson Daly returns as host, along with coach Adam Levine who won Season 29. Clarkson is back for her 11th season, while the newcomers are Queen Latifah and Riley Green.

Clarkson told TODAY that Green and Queen Latifah’s addition was “seamless.” She then jokingly added it was “annoying” because she does have to “fight really hard” to get country artists on her team now.

During the premiere episode, viewers will see the Blind Auditions, the first round of the show, where singers will showcase their impressive vocals in hopes of getting the coaches to turn their chairs. Once a coach hits their button and shows interest in a contestant, they try to persuade the artist to be on their team.
Find out the date, time and how to watch Season 30 of “The Voice” below.
What Day Does ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere?
The new season of “The Voice” premieres on Monday, Sept. 21 on NBC.
The Blind Auditions will continue on Tuesday, Sept. 22 and Wednesday, Sept 23.
What Time Does ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Air?
The first episode of “The Voice” Season 30 will air at 8 p.m. and end at 10 p.m.
The Sept. 22 and Sept. 23 episode will air from 8 p.m. to 9 p.m.
All episodes will be available to stream the next day on Peacock.
What to Know About ‘The Voice’ Season 30

“The Voice” is returning to its live shows format following the Blind Auditions and Cut Week, an elimination round. The six weeks of live shows will include special guest appearances and themed weeks. These episodes will be simulcast on Peacock.

During this season’s Blind Auditions, the show is introducing the all-new “First  In  Button.”  The button, which can only be used once, “gives the coach who turns first on a multi-chair turn the opportunity to claim an artist before the artist’s final decision,” the show’s press release said.

title: Who Was Lizzie Borden’s Sister, Emma?
summary: Who was Lizzie Borden’s sister Emma and what happened to her after the trial? Find out the true story of Emma Borden.
story: Lizzie Borden’s sister Emma Borden doesn’t appear all that much in Netflix’s newly released show “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.” However, when she does, she leaves quite an impression as the more accomplished sibling of the household whose inner turmoil plays out during the infamous trial for the gruesome Aug. 1982 murders of the pair’s father and stepmother.
But what was she really like?

The true story of Emma Borden doesn’t quite match that of the “It Girl” character in the series, which was released Sept. 17. While Emma, played by actor Billie Lourd, is portrayed as a foil to her awkward, spinster sister Lizzie, the real-life eldest daughter wasn’t a popular gal, swimming in suitors and often away from home. Rather, experts and historical accounts show that Emma Borden was attached to her younger sister and lived for years, upholding a promise she once made to look after Lizzie Borden.

“More than a passive bystander, she was the emotional rock, the financial guardian, and ultimately, the keeper of secrets that would remain buried forever,” the Lizzie Borden House wrote of Emma Borden on its website.
What Is Emma Borden Like on ‘Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story?’
In the Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan series, Emma is considered the superior child by her stepmother and father. Most of the time, she’s not home, instead spending her days with suitors.

In one scene during the second episode, Emma reveals that high society man Bard Wainwright is courting her. And in that same episode, he asks for her hand in marriage. Emma responds by collapsing elegantly on the fainting couch before enthusiastically agreeing to tie the knot.

“Emma comes and goes with the wind,” Lizzie, played by Ella Beatty, tells maid Bridget as she watches the private engagement through a crack in the door. “Everything a girl could want just falls into her lap.”

In a private conversation with Lizzie, Emma reveals that she has no such intentions of marrying Bard, but plans to string him along “just like the last two.” The eldest daughter explains to Lizzie that she isn’t interested in being “hog-tied to one man for the rest of your life.”

In another standout moment in the conversation, Emma reveals that she will be inheriting the bulk of their father Andrew Borden’s fortune due to her strong will. Lizzie, on the other hand, will be relegated to just 5% of the wealth because she, instead, is “feebleminded.”

Viewers don’t see much of Emma until much further in the series, when she walks into the crime scene and discovers her father’s gory cadaver on the couch. Emma jumps to conclusions and upon seeing her sister, immediately accuses Lizzie of being behind the murders.

While Lizzie is being detained as a suspect, Emma visits the younger sister and expresses doubt around her innocence. She reveals that on their late mother’s deathbed she had promised to always protect Lizzie, but that the shifting narratives and unusual sequence of events make it all difficult.
But when it comes to her actual testimony, Emma makes a resounding defense of Lizzie and is among the key figures who contribute to the younger Borden’s exoneration.

After the trial, Emma turns to laudanum and alcohol to cope with her depression. Gone are the days that men are interested in marrying her, as the Borden name has turned into “a bit of an albatross,” she says. And near the end of the show, she decides she can no longer tolerate the idea of being under her sister’s roof, leaving Lizzie for good.
“I hope that on your deathbed, you admit what you did,” Emma says in her last words to Lizzie.
What Was The Real-Life Emma Borden Like and Where Was She During The Murders?

The “Monster” version of Emma Borden is a sharp departure from the real-life woman. Emma, it turns out, was a quiet, highly conservative person, according to the Lizzie Borden House. And there were simply no records of her ever having a suitor.

As for her relationship to her stepmother, Emma Borden was said to be more resentful of Abby Borden than Lizzie Borden was. Emma, who was 14 when her father remarried, always called Abby by her first name.
“Perhaps her grief foreclosed a warmer relationship with the woman she viewed as her mother’s replacement,” author Cara Robertson wrote in her book “The Trial of Lizzie Borden.”
Robertson also suggests that Emma may have “felt she served as mother to Lizzie and resented Abby’s intrusion.”

And unlike what the show depicted, Emma was not the main beneficiary of the Andrew Borden fortune. In fact, Andrew had used his resources to buy Abby’s family a home — something that did not sit well with the Borden sisters.

“We know that from that point, both Lizzie and Emma blamed their stepmother for their father’s actions,” Robertson previously told TODAY.com “Even though he tried to equalize matters by deeding over some property to them, they viewed their stepmother as having played this negative role in siphoning away Borden money to (Abby’s) family.”
One aspect of the Netflix series’ portrayal of Emma does ring true, however. Robertson’s book points out that Emma once spoke of the promise she made to her mother.
“When my darling mother was on her deathbed she summoned me, and exacted a promise that I would always watch over ‘Baby Lizzie,’” Emma said, according to Robertson’s book.
On the day of the murders, Emma was visiting friends in another town, Fairhaven, Massachusetts, some miles away from the family’s home in Fall River, the book mentions.
It wasn’t until Emma received a telegram that afternoon that she learned about the double homicide, according to the Lizzie Borden House website.
What Was Emma Borden’s Role in The Murder Trial?

During the famous trial that shocked the nation, Emma Borden stepped up, using her inheritance to retain former Massachusetts Governor George D. Robinson along with other heavy-hitting attorneys to defend her sister.
What’s more, Emma put on an invaluable performance during her testimony. As Robertson writes, Emma was the key defense witness who provided the “most potent character support for her accused sister.”
“Fortunately, Emma was up to the difficult task: ‘There was no swaying of her slender form, no dropping of her straight-cut eye, no quivering of her tight-shut mouth,’” Robertson wrote in her book.
What Happened to Emma Borden After Lizzie Borden Was Acquitted?

Though Emma and Lizzie lived in peace for a stretch of time after the murders, moving into an estate they called “Maplecroft” in Fall River’s affluent neighborhood of the Hill, the calm didn’t last forever, according to Robertson’s book.

Following the trial, Lizzie attempted to start a new life, rebranding herself as “Lizbeth” and ingratiating herself with the theater crowd. Emma, Robertson wrote, strongly disapproved. The much more conservative, elder sister sought the advice of her pastor, who encouraged her to move on.
In 1905, more than a decade after the murders, Emma left and never spoke to Lizzie again, according to Robertson’s account.
Emma died just nine days after Lizzie. According to the Lizzie Borden House, Emma was unaware her sister ever died.

title: Cindy Crawford and Son Presley Gave a Rare Interview on TODAY a Year Before His Death
summary: Cindy Crawford and her children, Presley and Kaia Gerber, sat down on TODAY in 2025 for an interview. Here’s what they said.
story: Cindy Crawford and her family are mourning the loss of her son, model Presley Gerber, who has died at 27 years old.
His death comes a year after the supermodel shared a heartwarming discussion about family on TODAY with her son and daughter, actor and model Kaia Gerber.

A family representative confirmed Presley Gerber’s death to NBC News on Sept. 21. He died at a “rehab facility,” according to online records of the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. No cause of death or further detail was given.
He was Crawford’s oldest child with husband Rande Gerber, whom Crawford married in 1998.
The supermodel and her two children appeared together on TODAY in May 2025, where Presley and Kai Gerber spoke about growing up with Crawford as their mother.
“It was definitely the attention, like when people would walk by and you’re like, ‘Oh my God, that’s Cindy Crawford.’ I was like, ‘Yeah, yeah. I think. I’m pretty sure it is,’” Presley Gerber said.
Presley Gerber worked as a model himself, which included starring in an updated version of his mother’s famous Pepsi Super Bowl commercial.
While both children got into modeling as a career, they said Crawford never micromanaged them.
“You are so not a stage mom,” Kaia Gerber said to Crawford.
“Not at all,” Presley added.

In 2025, Crawford and her two children partnered as the face of Vuori Clothing, a clothing brand Rande Gerber found at a popup store in Malibu, California. Presley celebrated it as a chance for the whole family to work together.

“I think it’s given my dad and I, and the rest of the family, as well, an opportunity to be creative in a way where we typically don’t all have an interest in one thing,” he said. “I think that kind of opened up a new a new door.”
In the years before his death, Presley Gerber posted online about his struggles with depression and addiction in a program he called “Mental Health Mondays” on his Instagram account.
Kaia Gerber also referenced her brother’s struggles in an interview with Vogue in August.

“My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn’t share anything — and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, ‘I’m gonna be very human for everyone,’” she said. “There’s only so much you can hide from the world. And trying to put a lid on something just makes the person feel like you’re ashamed of them.”
Gerber had just turned 27 in July, which his mother celebrated on Instagram.
Happy birthday @presleygerber 🎂 I’m so proud of the man you’ve become, but I’ll always see you as my little boy!” she wrote. “Love you ❤️”

title: What Dolly Parton Was Like ‘On a Personal Note,’  According to Kelly Clarkson
summary: Kelly Clarkson will always have a special place in her heart for Dolly Parton.
story: Kelly Clarkson will always have a special place in her heart for Dolly Parton.
Following the country legend’s death on Aug. 25, Clarkson opened up about her relationship with Parton while stopping by Studio 1A Sept. 21.
“She was just very cool as a human, not only as a musician,” she said.
Clarkson called Parton “such a lovely woman” and said she was “very sweet” and “very cool.”
“Even the first time I met her, (it) was like we’ve known each other for years,” she said.
Clarkson, who recently wrapped up her final season of “The Kelly Clarkson Show,” selected one of Parton’s most famous songs, “9 to 5,” to open the first episode of her talk show in 2019.
“That was our first cover. That was the first Kellyoke,” she recalled.
Clarkson described Parton as a “beautiful soul” and said she was a “pioneer for a lot of women.”
“She just paved the way for so many,” she said. “But on a personal note, she was so nice every time we ran into each other, like she was just so cool.”
In 2022, Clarkson had the opportunity to honor Parton during the ACM Awards and perform a rendition of the country crooner’s hit song, “I Will Always Love You.
While appearing on TODAY, Clarkson recalled how she felt when she was asked to pay tribute to Parton.

“I was like, ‘Of course! I’ll show up. Where do you want me?’ And then they were like, ‘Oh, she picked this song.’ And I was like, ‘What?’ I was like, ‘You want me to sing which one?’ And I was very nervous because that’s not a song anyone wants to touch. But yeah, but I would for her,” she said.
The same year, Parton and Clarkson teamed up for a duet of “9 to 5” for the documentary “Still Working 9 to 5.” At the time, Parton applauded Clarkson for her fresh take on the famous song.
“Nobody sings like Kelly Clarkson. She makes any song come alive,” Parton said in a press release, per People. “I love her voice on ‘9 to 5,’ and I am so proud I got to sing with her on it.”

title: ‘The Voice’ Welcomes 2 New Coaches for Milestone Season 30
summary: “The Voice” Season 30 has two new coaches sitting in the famous red chairs. Find out who is joining reigning champ Adam Levine and Kelly Clarkson.
story: “The Voice” will soon usher in the reign of a new queen for its milestone Season 30, and possibly an artist who is looking to take Blake Shelton’s king of country crown.

As the new season of “The Voice” kicks off, here are the official four coaches who are seated in the spinning red chairs when the singing competition series premieres. Joining returning coaches Adam Levine and Kelly Clarkson are two newcomers: country music singer Riley Green and icon Queen Latifah.
Levine was the first coach to be announced for Season 30 as “The Voice” officially announced “the champion” would be back in April. Then, Clarkson was confirmed on May 7.
“The Voice” waited a few days before surprising fans with the special announcement that two new faces were joining the NBC family.
Riley Green Takes a Seat in the Red Chair
On May 10, the show posted an Instagram video of Green, a four-time CMA and four-time ACM winner, listening to a voice message from Clarkson in which she welcomed him to the crew.

In the clip, she greeted him and said, “I’m super stoked to work alongside you. Welcome to ‘The Voice.’ I was stoked when I heard you were going to be a coach because I’m actually a super-fan of your music, man. You’re so good.”

She then added, “Needless to say, it is a competition so I, as a future friend, sent you something.” Clarkson explained that the gift was meant to help him prepare for his time as a coach before she “whooped that a--.”
“The Voice” later uploaded a video of Green sitting in his chair and practicing pressing his red button.
Queen Latifah Is Ready to Reign
The show saved Queen Latifah’s grand reveal for last, confirming her debut in a press release May 12.
Queen Latifah, already a Grammy, Emmy and Golden Globe winner with an Academy Award nomination, will soon try to add a “Voice” championship to her long list of accolades.

The multi-hyphenate and Green will look to dethrone Team Adam, who secured a victory in the Season 29 “Battle of Champions” finale in April with Alexia Jayy taking home the trophy. Levine and Clarkson are now tied with four wins each behind original coach Shelton, who won nine times.
Season 30 of “The Voice” premieres with a three-night premiere event starting Monday, Sept. 21 at 8 p.m.

title: Taylor Swift’s 3-Word Reaction to Travis Kelce’s 1st Touchdown of the Football Season
summary: Taylor Swift had an adorable show of support for her husband Travis Kelce after his first touchdown of the Chiefs 2026 season.
story: Taylor Swift’s show of support for Travis Kelce at the latest Kansas City Chiefs game left onlookers swooning.
The “Opalite” singer was spotted cheering on her husband at Arrowhead Stadium Sept. 20 during their game against the Indianapolis Colts.
Sporting a Chiefs tank top and jeans, the newlywed couldn’t contain her excitement as Kelce scored his first touchdown of the 2026 season.
As other fans in the stands began to cheer, Swift proudly pointed at her engagement ring and wedding band and said, “That’s my husband!” Then she proceeded to clap for the Chiefs tight end.
The NFL and Chiefs Instagram pages captured the moment and shared it, captioning the post, “@taylorswift is a proud wife after @killatrav’s TD ❤️.”
Fans of the couple, who tied the knot at Madison Square Garden in July, took to the comments section to share their love for Swift’s show of affection for her husband.
“Good job Travis, love how proud she is😍😍😍,” one commented.
“Love this couple! Pure joy,” another wrote.
One fan weighed in, writing, “I love this ❤️🙌🔥👏 Taylor is so excited for her husband and his team. I absolutely adore her. Never stop being you, Taylor. Your laughter and joy are infectious.”
Swift is jubilant in the stands, but has received criticism for the attention she’s given at games. The NFL regularly pans the camera to the singer during games.

In a 2023 interview with Time, Swift addressed the topic, saying, “I’m just there to support Travis,” she said. “I have no awareness of if I’m being shown too much and p------ off a few dads, Brads, and Chads.”
Referencing the quote, one Swiftie shared the following reaction to the latest video of the singer supporting Kelce: “It’s going to be a long football season for the ‘Dads, Brad’s and Chad’s hahaha.”
The 2026 football season only recently kicked off. On Sept. 14, Swift attended the Chiefs season opener and sat next to Tom Cruise.
While appearing on “The Tonight Show,” the actor later told Jimmy Fallon about the conversation he had with the singer.
“She was schooling me on football,” he said.
Cruise called the singer “a genius” and said he’s been “following her since she was a kid.”
“She’s funny. She’s got such a great sense of humor,” he said.

title: Gwyneth Paltrow Reveals Story Behind Her ‘Conscious Uncoupling’ With Chris Martin
summary: When Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin used the term “conscious uncoupling” to describe their separation in 2014, the phrase ended up going viral at the time, taking the internet by storm.
story: When Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin used the term “conscious uncoupling” to describe their separation in 2014, the phrase ended up going viral at the time, taking the internet by storm.
And now, we finally have its backstory.

Paltrow, 53, opened up about the term during a recent episode of podcast “Friends Keep Secrets.” It turns out, her introduction to the phrase came from a therapist that she and Martin had at the time.

“Chris and I had this therapist that was really brilliant, and he sort of introduced us to the concept,” Paltrow told hosts Benny Blanco, Lil Dicky and his wife Kristin Batalucco during the Sept. 8 episode. “We just made a commitment to really put the kids first, and so what that meant was to stay a family, even though we weren’t a couple.”
Paltrow — who is currently married to writer and director Brad Falchuk, 55 — shares two children with Martin, 49. The two announced the news of the divorce through a statement on her Goop website.

“We are parents first and foremost, to two incredibly wonderful children and we ask for their and our space and privacy to be respected at this difficult time,” Paltrow and Martin wrote in the statement. “We have always conducted our relationship privately, and we hope that as we consciously uncouple and coparent, we will be able to continue in the same manner.”
Paltrow told the podcast that when she and Martin decided to get divorced, she turned to friends who came from divorced households for guidance.

“I said, ‘Tell me, what was the worst thing? What do you feel you have scars from to this day?’” Paltrow recounted. “They said the worst part was ... ‘My dad used to drop me off at the end of the driveway.’ ‘It was so tense at my birthday parties.’ ‘They never ate dinner in the same room until my college graduation, and it caused me so much pain.’”

She added that she and Martin sought to “circumvent all of that awful stuff.” Paltrow also shared one particular trying moment during the divorce in which she had to put the conscious uncoupling philosophy to work. She explained that when the family moved to Los Angeles early on in the separation, they continued to have brunch together every Sunday. One particular brunch date proved difficult.

“Chris and I were upset with each other about something – I can’t even remember what it is — and I was like, ‘This might go really off the rails,’” she recalled. “It was getting tense, and we looked at each other. We went outside on the front porch, and we’re like, ‘Let’s just not.’”
She said that the two ended up embracing.
“We just hugged,” she said. “We like fist-bumped and then we went to brunch.”

Paltrow, to be clear, did not invent the term “conscious uncoupling.” The tactic, believed to be coined by late marriage and family therapist Katherine Woodward Thomas, has long existed with therapists and counselors encouraging the mindset as part of the final stage of marriage counseling after a decision to divorce is made.
Life coach Jeanne Byrd Romero previously told TODAY.com that conscious uncoupling is a method that can help the parties heal.
“It’s really a way of moving out of blame and shame so people can transform the experience into healing and peace,” Romero said. “It can be done with just one of the partners are the couple.”

title: Miley Cyrus Shares Her One Hilarious, Relatable Fear About Getting Married To Maxx Morando
summary: Singer Miley Cyrus recently shared the one reservation she has about getting married to fiancé Maxx Morando — and it is oh, so relatable.
story: Singer Miley Cyrus recently shared the one reservation she has about getting married to fiancé Maxx Morando — and it is oh, so relatable.
Cyrus, 33, spoke about the relationship in a Sept. 17 interview with Apple Music’s Zane Lowe. The singer, who got engaged to Morando last year, was brutally honest about her fears.

“We’ve been together six years, and I’ve never gotten the ick. But I was like, all of a sudden, got in my head,” Cyrus told Lowe. “I was like, ‘Oh my god, I’m about to get married. What if I get the ick?’”
The ick, of course, refers to that sudden onset of feeling of disgust when a love interest does something one finds awkward, embarrassing or gross.
Morando pretty successfully squashed the fear, Cyrus said.

“I asked him, ‘What happens if you get the ick once you’re married?’ He’s like, ‘You deal with it, and like you move on, and you don’t be a baby. The ick is for when you’re in fifth grade,’” she said.

Cyrus, who got engaged to Morando in Kyoto, Japan, has previously been married once to actor Liam Hemsworth. The pair separated in 2019 after eight months of marriage. The “Flowers” singer then met Morando on a blind date years later in 2021.
In the interview with Lowe, Cyrus said that her experience with the ick was put to the test shortly after she talked the subject with Morando.
“Then suddenly I got the ick,” Cyrus shared. “He did something that icked me for a minute, and I was like, ‘Don’t ever do that again. It gave me the ick.’”
It led her to wonder if she’s ever given her partner the ick as well, Cyrus told Lowe.
“He said, ‘When you’re a brat,’” Cyrus said of Morando’s ick. “Which is so true. Dude, I’m so icky when I’m a brat.”

Cyrus and Morando have been rather private about their relationship, sparingly attending events together. However both have spoken highly of one another. In a July interview with Wonderland Magazine, Morando said that he loves “going with her to certain things to support whatever she’s doing.”
Cyrus told Lowe in their chat that Morando has allowed her to “soften.”
“I realized so much of my life was performative that I didn’t even realize that he’s given me the permission to really like soften into the reality,” she said.

The pair have also collaborated professionally, with Morando co-writing multiple songs with Cyrus. Recently, the couple appeared together in the steamy music video for her aptly-titled song “Let’s Get Married,” shot at the Chateau Marmont in Los Angeles. The song is part of her new album “Bass Persuades,” which debuted on Sept. 18.

title: Alexis Ohanian Shares 1 Sweet Rule He And Serena Williams Have For Their Daughters
summary: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian shared how he and his wife, tennis icon Serena Williams approach their kids’ aspirations in life.
story: Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian shared how he and his wife, tennis icon Serena Williams approach their kids’ aspirations in life.

Ohanian — who spoke to reporters Sept. 18 at the international debut of his all-women track and field league, Athlos, in London — told USA Sports that the couple just has one rule when it comes to the future careers of young daughters Olympia, 9, and Adira, 3.
“The one rule in the house is we don’t care what you want to do when you grow up, as long as you do your best at it and you’re doing something useful,” Ohanian, 43, told the outlet.

Ohanian attended the event with Williams, 44, along with their two children in a rare family appearance all together. The meet also included Olympic gold medalist sprinters Sha’Carri Richardson and Gabby Thomas, who are also two of the league’s athlete-owner advisors.
Ohanian explained to USA Sports that that day, Williams was tasked with monitoring their youngest, Adira. Meanwhile, Olympia was out, interviewing the star athletes.
Ohanian explained to the outlet that while Olympia was comfortable chatting it up with the athletes, she’s not firm on becoming a journalist.
“She hasn’t mentioned journalist yet,” Ohanian told the outlet. Right now, fashion designer is the number one career path that she’s circling around.”
He joked to the outlet’s journalist that their job is “safe for now, but watch out.”
“She’s coming for journalism,” he said. “She’s gonna go be great.”
Ohanian and Williams welcomed Olympia in September 2017 while Adira was born in August 2023. They’ve previously spoken about honoring their kids’ own passions.

In a January interview with TODAY hosts Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones, Williams shared that her children are in different sports that align with their personalities. Olympia, for example, is more interested in golf because she doesn’t like to run, Williams said, laughing. Adira may end up being the tennis player in the family, she added.

title: Celine Dion Dances Barefoot Atop Car After Paris Show In Ultimate Display Of Queen Behavior
summary: After a Sept. 18 show at the Plenitude Arena just outside Paris, France, power ballad icon Celine Dion surprised fans outside of her hotel with an impromptu performance in which she climbed up on the roof of a car barefoot and sang along with the giant crowd.
story: The queen is in her element.

After a Sept. 18 show at the Plenitude Arena just outside Paris, France, power ballad icon Celine Dion surprised fans outside of her hotel with an impromptu performance in which she climbed up on the roof of a car barefoot and sang along with the giant crowd.

Her iconic fan interaction comes amid her ongoing Paris residency that marks her first concerts in six years. Dion previously took a break from the stage after publicly revealing her stiff person syndrome diagnosis.
Multiple fan videos captured the magical moment. And it’s clear that the “My Heart Will Go On” singer is soaking it all up.

In the videos, Dion is seen climbing on top of the car and clapping along to her song “Pour que tu m’aimes encore.” Dressed in a more casual jacket and baggy pants, Dion engages with the enthusiastic crowd, dancing, playing air guitar and more.   She’s loving every second.

The past few weeks have been particularly significant for the artist, who has been performing in the City of Love amid a 26-date residency. During her first show back on Sept. 12, Dion made an emotional speech, reflecting on her return.
“I had promised myself not to cry,” said Dion, breaking down in tears. “But I’m so happy to see you all. I missed you.”
She added that she had always promised to come back to the stage — a commitment she kept.

“So here I am, singing for you,” Dion said during that first show at Plenitude Arena. “Thank you so very much for your support, your patience and if I may say so, I am everything I am because you loved me.”
Dion told the world about her diagnosis in 2022, canceling a string of performances at the time to navigate the condition.

Stiff person syndrome, a progressive, neurological disorder, causes stiff muscles in the torso, arms and legs, according to the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke. People with the syndrome can also experience greater sensitivity to noise, touch and emotional distress which can set off muscle spasms.
In the September cover story of Harper’s Bazaar, Dion revealed that she had experienced symptoms of the condition for 17 years prior to her diagnosis.

title: Ruby Rose Tears Up, Remembering Friend Hayden Panettiere: ‘We Spoke Every Day For 5 Years’
summary: Actor Ruby Rose recently got emotional while reflecting on the bond she shared with her good friend and confidante Hayden Panettiere, who died in August.
story: Actor Ruby Rose recently got emotional while reflecting on the bond she shared with her good friend and confidante Hayden Panettiere, who died in August.

Rose spoke about Panettiere’s passing during a Sept. 18 interview with Entertainment Tonight, sharing details about the friendship that the two shared over the years. The comments come weeks after Panettiere was found unresponsive at an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina. She was 36.

Rose — who was promoting the upcoming season of reality show “Special Forces: World’s Toughest Test,” on which she is a cast member — began to tear up while speaking about her connection with the late actor.
“That was my best friend,” Rose told the outlet. “We spoke every day for five years.”
Speaking to the outlet ahead of the show’s premiere on Sept. 24, Rose, 40, also revealed the way in which she met Panettiere.
“I didn’t even think we were going to be friends,” Rose said. “I didn’t know if I wanted to have any celebrity friends because I ... don’t have a great experience with the industry.”
Rose explained that while she was initially hesitant to befriend Panettiere, her reservations quickly dissolved.

“She saw me, and I just remember thinking, ‘Oh no!’ And then she ran up anyway and was like, ‘Hey, I’m Hayden. Can we go talk somewhere? We’ve got a lot in common,’” Rose said. “And then we went and talked, and we had everything in common.”
Rose told Entertainment Tonight that she and Panettiere would chat daily, texting and “checking in on each another.”
“It’s a bigger group now. There’s 14 of us that we’ve collected over the years,” Rose said. “That’s really — that’s my family.”
Rose added that all Panettiere “really ever wanted was to have her story told — her way on her terms.”
Panettiere was in cardiac arrest, meaning her heart had stopped beating, when emergency personnel arrived to the apartment on Aug. 16. Her cause of death has not yet been released.

Chief Deputy Coroner Shelton England of the Greenville County, South Carolina Coroner’s Office told NBC News Sept. 16 that the final toxicology results — that will determine Panettiere’s official cause and manner of death — are expected to be released within the next two weeks, he estimated, or possibly sooner.

Both Panettiere and Rose have been vocal about their negative experiences in the entertainment industry. Panettiere reflected on the trauma she endured first as a child actor and later on as an adult in Hollywood in her memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” published in May 2026.
“Reality merged with my imagination and burrowed into my core memories, where all my shame and trauma lived. Is it any wonder why I’ve faced so many real struggles in my life?” she wrote.

Rose has also voiced many of her difficult experiences. In 2021, she alleged that she was fired from the CW’s “Batwoman” after she was seriously injured on set. Warner Bros. Television Group denied the allegations, saying in a statement Rose was fired over multiple complaints about her behavior.
Since Panettiere’s death, Rose has posted on social media about the painful loss.
“Missing Hayden more than life today,” Rose wrote in a Sept. 14 Threads post.

title: Rescue Cat Named ChipPurr Jones ‘Throws’ 1st Pitch, Unites Baseball Fans Everywhere With His Cuteness
summary: What do Greg Maddux, John Smoltz and a teeny tiny orange rescue kitten have in common?
story: What do Greg Maddux, John Smoltz and a teeny tiny orange rescue kitten have in common?
Well they’re all iconic pitchers who’ve made their mark in the Atlanta Braves organization, of course.

The weeks-old kitten — appropriately named ChipPurr Jones after another Braves Hall-of-Famer — “threw out” the ceremonial first pitch Sept. 15 for the club’s Triple-A affiliate, the Gwinnett Stripers.
And the little guy delivered some heat ...by trotting alongside the ball to home plate.
To no one’s surprise, ChipPurr has since gone viral, with one post about the incredible outing amassing more than 109,000 likes as of the afternoon of Sept. 19.
ChipPurr’s handler Tricia Wurmstein, who’s also the Stripers’ manager of marketing tells TODAY.com that she’s proud of his performance on the mound.
“Honestly, it went so much better than I anticipated,” Wurmstein says, laughing. “He was ready for the moment.”
Videos of the miraculous moment show the kitten following a treat from the mound all the way to home plate as Ozzy Osbourne’s “Crazy Train” blares on the speakers.
Though there’s a ball in his periphery, he doesn’t interact with it at all. It’s really there for vibes.

ChipPurr’s pitching appearance was part of the team’s “Purr in the Park” night, which also included a pet supply donation drive, benefitting area rescue shelters. Fans were permitted to bring their beloved cats to the stadium for the occasion as well.
Like all pitchers, ChipPurr put in the work to make sure he delivered. Wurmstein helped him out with practice by incorporating treats into his “bullpen sessions.”

At first, she says, she positioned herself at home plate while he was on the mound in an attempt to see if he would run to her. But when she called out to ChipPurr, his trot was interrupted by the changing texture beneath him, she says. He wasn’t really feeling the pivot from dirt to grass.
“So I was like, ‘Maybe I can try and lead him with the treat, so he can directly see it and smell it right in front of him.’” Wurmstein recalls.
The rest is history.
Wurmstein says that ChipPurr came into the team’s orbit when he was spotted on a busy street a few weeks ago near the team’s home field in Lawrenceville, Georgia.

“One of our staff members happened to just be driving to work and saw him literally in the middle of the road in traffic,” Wurmstein explains. “So he got out of his car, scooped him up, and then brought him.”

ChipPurr was brought to a suite at the facility for safe keeping, Wurmstein says. And when word got around to her that there was a rescued kitten at work, the cat lover says she was swiftly on her way to meet him.
“I was like, ‘Yep, we will be keeping this cat,’” says Wurmstein, who’s been a longtime cat owner herself. “By ‘we,’ I mean me.”

As the person in charge of the team’s social media, Wurmstein says she not only began caring for the little guy, but she also introduced him to the team’s fans online. At one point, the team had an online naming poll for him, which ultimately led to his all-star moniker.
These days, ChipPurr, who’s estimated to be around six weeks old, lives at the stadium and has a whole apartment there with a ton of toys, including foam baseballs, Wurmstein says.
The proud cat mom adds that she’s got an eye on him at all hours of the day, even when she’s not physically at the field. She’s installed a camera to capture his movements, she says.
“I live literally three minutes from the stadium, so if anything were to happen, I’d be right here,” she says.
After ChipPurr starts his first round of vaccinations in a few days, he’ll join Wurmstein’s other cat for a cozy life at her home, she explains.

“I’ll start the integration process with them,” Wurmstein says of the cats. “And now that the season’s over on Sunday, it’ll be a lot easier for me to ... actually watch over them as they interact for the first time in the next couple of weeks.”
With all the attention from fans across baseball, Wurmstein hopes that his presence can help spread a simple message.

“Be kind to humans and animals alike. It’s great that we have Chipper now, but it was a really unfortunate circumstance in which we he came into our care,” Wurmstein says. “I just want to make sure that people are being kind to each other and being kind to animals.”
Now as for eight-time All-Star, two-time Silver Slugger and 1995 World Series champ Chipper Jones? He seems pretty impressed with his young protégé.

title: Watch How Amy Poehler Gets Famously Reserved Robert De Niro To Chit Chat More
summary: Leave it up to Amy Poehler to get a couple laughs out of one of the most iconically stoic actors of our day.
story: Leave it up to Amy Poehler to get a couple laughs out of one of the most iconically stoic actors of our day.

The “SNL” alum sat down with legendary actor Robert De Niro on the latest episode of her podcast “Good Hang,” released Sept. 15. While De Niro is famously known to be, well, not the chatterbox type, Poehler appears to get him to crack through a pretty nontraditional interview tactic.
“I’m gonna ask you a favor,” Poehler says, pleading with the actor. “If I don’t meet my word count by the end of this interview, I’m screwed.”
While De Niro seems to understand the assignment, he comes up a tad short when answering Poehler’s first question, “Would you consider yourself an introverted person?”
“In some ways I am,” he says. “Depending on the situation.”
And the comedian does not let him off the hook.
“We need at least 10,” Poehler replies, as the two dissolve into giggles. “We need at least 10 more words every sentence.”

During the podcast episode, Poehler and De Niro touch on a wide range of subjects from thirst traps to his new documentary “Tribeca 25,” which explores the beginnings of the famous film fest that he started with producer Jane Rosenthal after the 9/11 attacks.
The comedian truly hits it off with De Niro. At one point, she even moves him to tears when she praises his activism.
“It makes everybody feel very safe,” Poehler says of De Niro’s advocacy. “I’ve seen you do it over and over again, and I really appreciate it.”
Moments later, Poehler realizes that the comments have made De Niro emotional.
“This is going to be a real switcheroo,” Poehler says. “I can’t believe I just made you cry.”

title: Snooki Announces ‘Mawma Is Cancer Free’ After Diagnosis, Hysterectomy
summary: Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi announced in a Sept. 19 Instagram video that she is officially cancer-free.
story: Congratulations are in order!

Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi announced in a Sept. 19 Instagram video that she is officially cancer-free. The good news comes after the “Jersey Shore” star told fans in February that she was diagnosed with Stage 1 cervical cancer, undergoing a hysterectomy months later to treat the disease.
“After a colposcopy, conization & hysterectomy, mawma is cancer free,” Polizzi, 38, wrote in some text that accompanied a video of the reality star, enjoying a celebratory drink.
A colposcopy is a procedure that checks the cervix, vagina and vulva for signs of disease while conization refers to a different procedure in which abnormal tissue is removed from the cervix.
The announcement received an outpouring of support, including positive messages from fellow “Jersey Shore” cast mates Mike “The Situation” Sorrentino and Sammi “Sweetheart” Giancola.
Other social media users, who have also gone through cervical cancer, shared their excitement for Polizzi.

“I’m so happy for you and your family 🥹♥️ I know the struggle you have been through 🥹♥️I got diagnosed with cervix cancer in 2022 and went through chemo and radiation therapy, I’m cancer free now ♥️LOVE from Denmark ♥️” one user wrote.
In her post, Polizzi showed her appreciation for her medical team.
“Thanks to all the doctors who helped me on this journey!” Polizzi wrote in the caption. “It wouldn’t be possible without you!”
The reality star — who shared that she will be getting pap smears every three months to ensure that the disease doesn’t reappear — also encouraged women to be vigilant about their health.
“GET UR PAP SMEARS LADIES! & stay on top of those appointments!💗” Polizzi wrote.
Back in July, the mother of three shared a video on social media that gave fans a glimpse of her experience with hysterectomy surgery, documenting the entire day of the procedure.
“It’s a scary thing, and a lot of us women deal with it, and no one really talks about it,” Polizzi said in the video. “So I’m here to give that platform for all of us ladies.”

Polizzi also shared her honest emotions around the surgery. She said in the video that she was “terrified” while going into the procedure. The doctors ended up removing her uterus, cervix along with “some parts” of the vagina “just to make sure we get everything,” she said.
“Just dealing with all that pain — it’s not great,” a tearful Polizzi said.
